Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 1:

The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The interpreters differed regarding this.

Some of them said its interpretation is: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing."

Mention of those who said this:

17518. Yahya ibn Dawud ibn Maymun al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing." [[The report: 17518 – "Yahya ibn Dawud ibn Maymun al-Wasiti," a teacher of al-Tabari, has passed under numbers 4451 and 11545.]]

17519. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his words ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, he said: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing."

* *

Others said: They are letters from the name of Allah which is "al-Rahman."

Mention of those who said this:

17520. Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabwayh narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ and ﴿Nun﴾ are the letters of "al-Rahman," separated.

17521. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, who said: Salim ibn Abdullah was mentioned: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ and ﴿Nun﴾, and he said: the name "al-Rahman" is separated; then he said: "al-Rahman."

17522. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: Mandal narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ and ﴿Nun﴾ are the name "al-Rahman."

17523. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Amr al-Kalbi narrated to us, from Abu Awanah, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from Amir: that he was asked about ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ and ﴿Sad﴾, and he said: They are names from the names of Allah, separated by spelling; when you join them, they are a name of Allah, exalted is He.

* *

Others said: They are a name of the names of the Qur'an.

Mention of those who said this:

17524. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ is a name of the names of the Qur'an.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already mentioned the differences of people, what each speaker went to in what he said, and the correct view among us on this matter, in its counterpart, which is at the beginning of "Surat al-Baqarah"; that suffices and makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [[See what has passed, 1: 205–224.]]

We have mentioned in this place only the portion we mentioned, because of the disagreement of those we mentioned here with their saying regarding ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾. As for those who reconciled the meanings of all of that, we have mentioned their view there, being content with not repeating it here. [[In the printed edition: "wa-muktafiyan," and I have restored what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words ﴿Tilka ayatu l-kitabi l-hakim﴾ (1)

Abu Ja'far said: There has been difference regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: "Those are the verses of the Torah."

Mention of those who said this:

17525. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Tilka ayatu l-kitabi l-hakim﴾: "The Torah and the Gospel."

17526. ... narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Amr, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Tilka ayatu l-kitab﴾: "The scriptures that were before the Qur'an."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "These are the verses of the Qur'an."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations, as regards the truth, is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it as: "These are the verses of the Qur'an," and directed the meaning of ﴿tilka﴾ to the meaning of "hadhihi" (these). We have already explained the direction of ﴿tilka﴾ to this meaning in "Surat al-Baqarah," in a manner that suffices and makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See what has passed, 1: 225–228.]]

* *

And ﴿al-ayat﴾ means the signs; and ﴿al-kitab﴾ is one of the names of the Qur'an. We have explained all of that earlier. [[See the explanation of "ayah" in the language indexes earlier under (a-y-y), and the explanation of "kitab" in the language indexes earlier under (h-k-m).]]

* *

We only said that this interpretation is more correct because no prior mention of the Torah and the Gospel has come, nor any subsequent recitation, so that the report would be directed toward them.

Since that is so, the sense of the speech is: "And the Compeller (al-Rahman)? These are the verses of the wise Qur'an."

* *

The meaning of ﴿al-hakim﴾ in this place is "al-muhkam" (the perfected/fixed), the form "mufʻal" being turned to "faʻil," just as it is said: ﴿'adhabun alim﴾ meaning "painful" (mu'lim). [[See the explanation of "hakim" in the language indexes earlier under (h-k-m).]] And as the poet said: [[He is Amr ibn Ma'dikarib al-Zubaydi.]]

"Is it from Rayhanah, the one who calls, the one who hears?"* [[The verse has passed, with its takhrij and explanation, in 1: 283.]]

We have explained that in more than one place in the book. [[See what has passed, 1: 283, 284, and other places in the indexes of Arabic and grammatical topics and others.]]

Its meaning, then, is: "Those are the verses of the Book which is perfected, which Allah perfected and made clear to His servants, as His majestic praise says: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra. A Book whose verses have been perfected, then detailed, from One who is Wise and Aware﴾ [Surah Hud: 1]."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 2:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He says: Was it a wonder for the people that We sent the Qur'an down to a man from among them, to warn them of God's punishment for their disobedience, as though they did not know that God had revealed to men like him before him, so that they marvelled at Our revelation to him? [[See the explanation of "wahy" (revelation) and "indhar" (warning) in the earlier linguistic indices, under (w-h-y) and (n-dh-r).]]

* *

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said this:

17527- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Imarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When God sent Muhammad as a messenger, the Arabs denied it, or those of them who denied it said: "God is greater than to have as His messenger a human being like Muhammad!" So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed to a man from among them﴾, and He said: ﴿We did not send before you except men﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 109].

17528- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Quraysh wondered that a man from among them was sent. He said: And similar to this is: ﴿And to 'Ad their brother Hud﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 65], ﴿And to Thamud their brother Salih﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 73], and God said: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 69].

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that for them is a firm standing (qadam sidq) with their Lord﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His praise, He says: Was it not a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: that he should warn the people, and give good tidings to those who believe in God and His messenger: ﴿that for them is a qadam sidq﴾, which is coordinated with ﴿warn﴾.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿qadam sidq﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is that for them is a good reward for the righteous deeds they sent forward.

Those who said this:

17529- Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord﴾, he said: a reward of truth.

17530-. . . . related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid: ﴿that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord﴾, he said: the righteous deeds.

17531- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord﴾, he said: a good reward for what they sent forward of their deeds.

17532- Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Hayyan related to us, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from al-Walid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mughith, from Mujahid: ﴿that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord﴾, he said: their prayer, their fasting, their charity, and their glorification of God.

[[The report 17532: "Zayd ibn Habbab al-Tamimi", who has passed several times, the last being no. 11490. In the printed edition it was "Yazid ibn Hayyan", the editor having misread the manuscript and dealt with it very poorly.

"Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khuzi" is weak; he has passed several times, the last being no. 17313.

"al-Walid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mughith" is trustworthy; he has passed at no. 16259 and 17313.

In the printed edition and the manuscript it was "al-Walid ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abi Mughith", which is a plain error.]]

17533- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿qadam sidq﴾, he said: good.

17534- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿qadam sidq﴾, the same.

17535- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

17536-. . . . Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: ﴿qadam sidq﴾, a reward of truth = ﴿with their Lord﴾.

17537- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the same.

17538- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that for them is a qadam sidq﴾: "The qadam sidq" is the reward of truth for what they sent forward of deeds.

* *

Others said: its meaning is that for them is a precedence of truth (sabiq sidq) in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz) of happiness.

Those who said this:

17539- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord﴾, he says: happiness has preceded for them in the First Remembrance.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is that Muhammad, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, is an intercessor for them, the qadam sidq.

Those who said this:

17540- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Fudayl ibn 'Amr ibn al-Jawn, from Qatadah, or al-Hasan: ﴿that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord﴾, he said: Muhammad is an intercessor for them. [[The report 17540: I have found no biography of "Fudayl ibn 'Amr ibn al-Jawn". I do not know whether he is "Fudayl ibn 'Amr al-Fuqaymi" or someone else.]]

17541- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord﴾: that is, a past truth (salaf sidq) with their Lord.

17542- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning His saying: ﴿that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord﴾, he said: Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is that for them are righteous deeds with God, by which they deserve His reward.

* *

This is because it is related from the Arabs: "These are the people of precedence (ahl al-qadam) in Islam", meaning those who sent forward good in it, so that they had precedence in it. And it is said: "He has with me a qadam sidq and a qadam su'" (a precedence of truth and a precedence of evil), meaning what was sent forward to him of good or evil. From this is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit:

For us is the highest precedence towards You, and our allegiance
to our first (ancestors) in obedience to God follows.
[[The verse has passed with its sourcing earlier, 13:209, where its version is: "For us is the first precedence".]]

And the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

For you is a precedence which people do not deny,
along with inherited nobility that rose over the sea.
[[From his poem in praise of Bilal ibn Abi Burdah ibn Abi Musa al-Ash'ari, after which he says: "Among the qualities of the Prophet, the chosen one, with his Lord, and 'Uthman and al-Faruq after Abu Bakr."

The version in his Diwan is: "rose over the boast".]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: "And give good tidings to those who believe that for them is a precedence of good from righteous deeds with their Lord."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The disbelievers said: "Indeed, this is clearly a sorcerer" (2)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited: ﴿Indeed, this is clearly sorcery (la-sihrun mubin)﴾, meaning: indeed, this which you have brought to us, they mean the Qur'an, is clear sorcery.

* *

Masruq, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and a group of the Kufan readers recited: ﴿Indeed, this is clearly a sorcerer (la-sahirun mubin)﴾.

* *

I have already explained in similar cases that every described thing is indicated by its description, and its description by it.

The reciter has a choice in this recitation, as with this letter: ﴿The disbelievers said: "Indeed, this is sorcery, clear"﴾ and "sahir mubin" (a clear sorcerer). [[See what has passed at 11:216, 217.]]

This is because they only described him as "a sorcerer", and their description of what came to them as "sorcery" indicates that they had described him with sorcery. Since that is so, whichever of the two the reciter reads is equivalent, as the meanings of the two readings agree.

* *

In the speech there is an omission, which is indicated by what has been mentioned, and so its mention is dropped, and it is: "So when he gave them good tidings and warned them, and recited the revelation to them", the disbelievers said: "Indeed, this which has come to us with is clear sorcery."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: "Was it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: that he should warn the people, and give good tidings to those who believe that for them is a qadam sidq with their Lord?" So when he came to them with the revelation of God and recited it to them, those who denied the Oneness of God and the messengership of His messenger said: "Indeed, this which Muhammad has brought us is clear sorcery", meaning: it makes clear to you that he is a liar in what he claims. [[See the explanation of "sihr" (sorcery) and "mubin" (clear) in the earlier linguistic indices, under (s-h-r) and (b-y-n).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 3:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne, arranging the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not be reminded?﴾ (10:3)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed your Lord, to whom all worship belongs, and to whom alone worship is fitting, is the One who created the seven heavens and the seven earths in six days, and He alone created them, without partner or helper. Then He established Himself upon His Throne, arranging the affairs and decreeing in His creation what He wills, none opposing His decree, none challenging His arrangement, and no disorder entering His affairs. [[See the explanation of "istiwa'" (establishment/settling) above, 1: 428-431 / 12: 483 = and the explanation of "al-'Arsh" (the Throne) above, 12: 482 / 14: 587.]] = ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾: meaning, on the Day of Resurrection no intercessor will intercede with Him for anyone except after He has given permission for the intercession. [[See the explanation of "al-shafa'ah" (intercession) above, 12: 481, footnote 1, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-idhn" (permission) above, 14: 112, footnote 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾: He, may His majesty be exalted, says: This One who has these attributes is your Master and your Lord, not those who do not hear, do not see, do not arrange, and do not decree, from among the gods and idols. = ﴿So worship Him﴾: meaning, worship your Lord who has these attributes, devote worship sincerely to Him, and single Him out for divinity and lordship, submitting to Him in humility, rather than to your idols and all that you associate with Him in worship. = ﴿Will you not be reminded?﴾: meaning, will you not take heed and learn from these signs and proofs, [[See the explanation of "al-tadhakkur" (remembrance/reminding oneself) above, 12: 493, footnote 1, and the references there.]] so that you turn back in submission to the Oneness of your Lord and His singling out for worship, and renounce the rivals and disown them?

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said this:

17543 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿arranging the affair﴾, he said: He decrees it alone.

17544 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid: ﴿arranging the affair, there is no intercessor except after His permission﴾, he said: He decrees it alone.

17545 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿arranging the affair﴾, he said: He decrees it alone.

17546 - ... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

17547 - al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you, as a promise of Allah, true. Indeed, He originates creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾ (4)

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted remembrance says: To your Lord, whose attributes are what His praise described in the verse before this one, is your return, O people, all of you, on the Day of Resurrection. [See the explanation of "al-marji'" (the return) above, 12:287, note 1, and the references there.] ﴿As a promise of Allah, true﴾: ﴿Promise of Allah﴾ is put in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar) from His saying ﴿To Him is your return﴾, because it carries the meaning of "promise." Its meaning: Allah promises you that He will bring you back to life after your death, a promise that is true. Therefore ﴿a promise of Allah, true﴾ is in the accusative. ﴿Indeed, He originates creation and then repeats it﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed your Lord initiates the creation, its production and its bringing into existence. ﴿Then repeats it﴾: He says, then He repeats it, bringing it into existence living as it was on the day He originated it, after its annihilation and decay. [See the explanation of "al-bad'" (origination) and "al-'awd" (repetition) above, 12:382-388.] As related:

17548. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿He originates creation then repeats it﴾, he said: He gives it life, then makes it die. Abu Ja'far said: I think he also said, "then gives it life."

17549. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid: ﴿He originates creation then repeats it﴾, he said: He gives it life, then makes it die, then gives it life.

17550. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed He originates creation then repeats it﴾, he said: He gives it life, then makes it die, then originates it, then gives it life.

17551. ... narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

The readers of the cities recited it: ﴿Innahu yabda'u al-khalq﴾ with a kasra on the alif of ﴿innahu﴾, as a resumption (isti'naf).

* *

It is related from Abu Ja'far al-Razi that he read it ﴿annahu﴾ with a fatha on the alif of ﴿annahu﴾.

* *

It is as if he intended: "Truly, that He originates creation and then repeats it," so "anna" in that case is in the nominative, as the poet said: [I do not know who said it.]

Ahaqqan 'ibad Allah anna lastu za'iran ... rubá jannatin illa 'alayya raqib
[In the printed edition: "Aba hubba illa 'ala raqib", which is a distortion of what is in the manuscript, where it is written without dots: "rubahu". The correct reading is what has been given.]

* *

His saying: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾: He says, then He repeats it after its death as it was before its death, when He resurrects it from its grave. ﴿That He may reward those who believed﴾ means to reward those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger and did the deeds Allah commanded them, and avoided what He forbade them, for their good deeds. [See the explanation of "al-jaza'" (recompense) in the lexical indices above, under (j-z-y).] ﴿With justice﴾: He says, that He may reward them for the good of the deeds they did in the world with the good reward and the righteous recompense in the Hereafter. That is "al-qist," and "al-qist" is justice and equity. [See the explanation of "al-qist" above, 12:379, note 2, and the references there.] As related:

17552. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿With justice﴾, with equity.

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water﴾: He, exalted is His praise, began the report about what Allah has prepared for those who disbelieved of punishment, and it carries the sense of conjunction with the first. For He, exalted is His remembrance, generalized the report about the return of all of them, their disbelievers and their believers, to Him. Then He informed that their repetition is so that each group may be recompensed according to what it did: the good-doer with goodness, and the wrongdoer with wrongdoing. But since the resumed report about what has been prepared for those who disbelieved of punishment had already preceded, which indicates to the listener of that the intended meaning, the report was begun, and the meaning is conjunctive, so He said: And those who denied Allah and His Messenger and called His signs lies — ﴿for them is a drink﴾ in Hell ﴿of scalding water﴾, and that is a drink that has been boiled and whose heat has intensified, to the extent that it is related from the Prophet ﷺ that it strips the scalp from one of them when it is brought close to him. And as His exalted praise described it: ﴿Like molten brass, it scorches the faces﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29].

* *

Its origin is "maf'ul" changed to "fa'il," and it is really "mahmum," meaning heated; and everything heated among the Arabs is "hamim." [See the explanation of "hamim" above, 11:448, 449.]

From it is the saying of al-Murraqish:

And every day for her is a cauldron (miqtarah), in which is burning wood (kiba') prepared and scalding water (hamim).

[The verse and its takhrij and explanation were given above, 11:448, and its narration there is: "in every evening."]

He means by "al-hamim," heated water.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a painful punishment﴾: He says, and for them besides that is a painful torment, [See the explanation of "alim" above in the lexical indices, under (a-l-m)], in addition to the drink of scalding water, because they used to disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 5:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a light, and determined for it stations, that you might know the number of years and the reckoning. Allah did not create that except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth. ﴿He it is who made the sun a shining light﴾ by day, ﴿and the moon a light﴾ by night. The meaning of that is: He it is who gave light to the sun and illuminated the moon. ﴿And determined for it stations﴾, meaning: He decreed it and arranged it in stations, neither exceeding them nor falling short of them, in one state forever. [See the explanation of "taqdir" (determination) above, 11:560.]

* *

He said: ﴿and determined for it stations﴾, using the singular pronoun, although "the sun" and "the moon" have been mentioned. There are two possible explanations for this:

The first: the pronoun "hu" in His words ﴿determined for it﴾ refers to the moon specifically, because the ending of months and years is known by the crescents, not by the sun.

The second: that one of the two is mentioned and the other is dispensed with, as He said in another place: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 62], and as the poet said: [This is Ibn Ahmar, or al-Azraq ibn Tarafa ibn al-Amrad al-Firasi.]

*"He threw at me a matter from which I and my father were innocent, and from the depths of the well he threw me..."*

[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:458; Lisan (j-w-l), and others. There was a dispute between him and a man over a well; his opponent said, "He is the son of a thief," so he recited this poem, and after it: "He called me a thief among thieves, and my father had not been called by two men..." The correct wording of the verse is "and from ajl al-tawi," where "al-tawi" is the well, and "al-jul" and "al-jal" are the side of the well, from its bottom up to its top.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿that you might know the number of years and the reckoning﴾, meaning: He determined that in stations ﴿that you might know﴾, O people, ﴿the number of years﴾, the entry of what enters of them, or the ending of what lies ahead of them, and their reckoning. That is, the reckoning of the times of the years, the number of their days, and the reckoning of the hours of their days. ﴿Allah did not create that except in truth﴾: He, exalted is His praise, says that Allah did not create the sun, the moon and their stations except in truth. He, exalted is His mention, says: I created all of that in truth by Myself alone, without help or partner. ﴿He details the signs﴾: He makes clear the proofs and evidences. [See the explanation of "tafsil" (detailing) above, 14:152, note 2, and its references; and the explanation of "ayah" (sign) above in the language indexes (a-y-y).] ﴿for a people who know﴾, when they reflect upon them, the reality of Allah's oneness and the truth of what Muhammad ﷺ calls them to, namely the renunciation of rivals and the disavowal of idols.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 6:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, are signs for a people who fear Allah.ﴩ

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, whose remembrance is great, says, alerting His servants to the place of evidence for His lordship and that He is the Creator of everything other than Him: Indeed, in the night succeeding the day and the day succeeding the night, when this goes, that comes, and when that comes, this goes, [[For the interpretation of "the alternation of the night and the day," see what has preceded, 3:272, 273.]] and in what Allah has created in the heavens, of the sun, the moon and the stars, and in the earth, of the wondrous creations that indicate that it has a Maker, none like unto Him, there is nothing [such as] ... ﴿signs﴾, meaning: proofs, arguments and clear indicators; ﴿for a people who fear Allah﴾, meaning: who fear His threat and dread His punishment by sincerely devoting worship to their Lord.

If someone says: Is there not evidence in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth of its Creator, except for those who fear Allah?

It is said: In that there is clear evidence of its Creator for everyone whose natural disposition is sound and whose heart is free of defects. He did not intend by this a report that there is evidence in it only for one who has already made himself conscious of the fear of Allah; rather its meaning is: indeed, in that there are signs for one who guards against the punishment of Allah, so that his desire does not drive him to oppose the truth that has become clear to him, because that indicates to every person of sound disposition that there is a Director who deserves to be submitted to in worship, to the exclusion of whatever other gods and rivals there are.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 7–8:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us and are satisfied with the worldly life and at rest therein, and those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ (7) ﴿Their refuge is the Fire because of what they used to earn﴾ (8).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, those who do not fear meeting Us on the Day of Resurrection, and so they deny reward and punishment, competing for the adornments of the world and its embellishments, content with it as a substitute for the Hereafter, at rest in it and dwelling in it [[See the explanation of "al-ittmi'nan" (being at rest) above, 13:418, note 2, and the references there.]] = and those who are heedless of the signs of God = meaning His proofs of His oneness and His arguments against His servants regarding sincere worship of Him = ﴿heedless﴾, turning away from them and being unconcerned, [[See the explanation of "al-ghaflah" (heedlessness) above, 13:281, note 2, and the references there.]] not contemplating them as one who counsels his own soul, so that they might know by them the truth of what they indicate and recognize by them the length of what they remain upon = ﴿Their refuge is the Fire﴾, He, exalted is His praise, says: these people who have these characteristics = ﴿their refuge﴾, their destination is the Fire, the Fire of Hell, in the Hereafter [[See the explanation of "al-ma'wa" (refuge) above, 14:425, note 6, and the references there.]] = ﴿because of what they used to earn﴾, in the world, of sins and crimes, and what they committed of evil deeds. [[See the explanation of "al-kasb" (earning) above in the language indexes (k-s-b).]]

* *

The Arabs say: "So-and-so does not expect (yarju) so-and-so" when he does not fear him.

From this is the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect dignity from God?﴾ [Surah Nuh: 13]. [[See the explanation of "al-raja'" (expectation) above in the language indexes (k-s-b).]] From this is the verse of Abu Dhu'ayb:

When the bees sting him, he does not expect their sting, and he opposes them in a house of honeycomb, bees... [[The verse has passed with its takhrij and explanation above, 9:174.]]

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them﴾: it means rivers of Paradise will flow beneath these believers whose qualities He, may His praise be exalted, has described. ﴿In Gardens of Bliss﴾: that is, in gardens of bliss, which Allah has granted to the people of His obedience and of faith in Him. [[See the explanation of "Gardens of Bliss" in the earlier passages, vol. 10, pp. 461–462.]]

* * *

If someone asks: How can it be said, ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them﴾, when He, may His praise be exalted, describes the rivers of Paradise throughout the Qur'an as flowing beneath the gardens? How is it possible for rivers to flow beneath them, unless they were above the ground while the rivers flowed beneath its surface? That is not a characteristic of the rivers of Paradise, for their characteristic is that they flow over the surface of the earth without trenches?

It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have supposed. Rather, the meaning is: rivers will flow before them, in front of them, to what lies ahead of them in the gardens of bliss. This is like the saying of Allah: ﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾ [Surah Maryam: 24]. It is known that He did not place the "sari" (stream) beneath her while she sat upon it, since the "sari" is the watercourse; rather, it means: He placed it in front of her, before her. Likewise, He, may His praise be exalted, related the words of Pharaoh: ﴿Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 51], meaning: "in front of me, before me."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Their call therein: "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾, its meaning is: their supplication therein is "Glory be to You, O Allah." [[See the explanation of "al-da'wa" in the earlier passages, vol. 12, pp. 303–304.]] As follows:

17563. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I was told that His saying: ﴿Their call therein: "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾: when a bird passes by them and they desire it, they say, "Glory be to You, O Allah!" That is their call. Then the angel comes to them with what they desired, greets them, and they return the greeting to him. That is His saying: ﴿And their greeting therein is "Peace."﴾ He said: When they have eaten, they praise Allah their Lord. That is His saying: ﴿And the last of their call is: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

17564. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Their call therein: "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾, he said: That is their saying therein. ﴿And their greeting therein is "Peace."﴾

17565. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ubayd Allah al-Ash'ari related to us, saying: I heard Sufyan say: ﴿Their call therein: "Glory be to You, O Allah. And their greeting therein is peace"﴾. He said: When they desire a thing, they say, "O Allah," and what they called for comes to them.
