As for the disbeliever, when he comes out of his grave, his deed takes the form of an evil image and an evil appearance [[In the printed edition: "wabashara" (and good tidings); the correct reading, as I have established it, is from the manuscript.]]. It says to him, 'What are you?' By Allah, I see you as an evil man! He says, 'I am your deed!' And it drives him until it brings him into the Fire."

17559. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿Their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾, he said: It will become a light for them by which they walk.

17560. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

17561. ... [chain omitted] ... Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from Waraqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

17562. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it. And Ibn Juraij said: ﴿Their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾, he said: His deed will appear to him in the form of a good image and a pleasant wind; it will confront its companion and give him good tidings of every good. It says to him, "Who are you?" He says, "I am your deed!" So He makes for him a light before him until He brings him into Paradise. That is His saying: ﴿Their Lord will guide them by their faith.﴾ As for the disbeliever, his deed appears to him in the form of an evil image and a foul wind; it clings to its companion and presses upon him until it hurls him into the Fire. [[In the printed edition: "wayuladduhu" (with a dal); the manuscript has the reading I have adopted. "Lazzahu yalazzuhu mula zatan wa lizazan": to adhere to him and cling to him.]]

* * *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "by their faith," their Lord guides them to His religion. That is, by their affirmation He guided them.

Those who said this:

[The chain is missing here. After the words "Those who said this," nothing follows in the text. The margin of the manuscript reads "thus," which is evidence of an early omission.]

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them﴾: it means rivers of Paradise will flow beneath these believers whose qualities He, may His praise be exalted, has described. ﴿In Gardens of Bliss﴾: that is, in gardens of bliss, which Allah has granted to the people of His obedience and of faith in Him. [[See the explanation of "Gardens of Bliss" in the earlier passages, vol. 10, pp. 461–462.]]

* * *

If someone asks: How can it be said, ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them﴾, when He, may His praise be exalted, describes the rivers of Paradise throughout the Qur'an as flowing beneath the gardens? How is it possible for rivers to flow beneath them, unless they were above the ground while the rivers flowed beneath its surface? That is not a characteristic of the rivers of Paradise, for their characteristic is that they flow over the surface of the earth without trenches?

It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have supposed. Rather, the meaning is: rivers will flow before them, in front of them, to what lies ahead of them in the gardens of bliss. This is like the saying of Allah: ﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾ [Surah Maryam: 24]. It is known that He did not place the "sari" (stream) beneath her while she sat upon it, since the "sari" is the watercourse; rather, it means: He placed it in front of her, before her. Likewise, He, may His praise be exalted, related the words of Pharaoh: ﴿Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me?﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 51], meaning: "in front of me, before me."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Their call therein: "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾, its meaning is: their supplication therein is "Glory be to You, O Allah." [[See the explanation of "al-da'wa" in the earlier passages, vol. 12, pp. 303–304.]] As follows:

17563. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I was told that His saying: ﴿Their call therein: "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾: when a bird passes by them and they desire it, they say, "Glory be to You, O Allah!" That is their call. Then the angel comes to them with what they desired, greets them, and they return the greeting to him. That is His saying: ﴿And their greeting therein is "Peace."﴾ He said: When they have eaten, they praise Allah their Lord. That is His saying: ﴿And the last of their call is: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

17564. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Their call therein: "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾, he said: That is their saying therein. ﴿And their greeting therein is "Peace."﴾

17565. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ubayd Allah al-Ash'ari related to us, saying: I heard Sufyan say: ﴿Their call therein: "Glory be to You, O Allah. And their greeting therein is peace"﴾. He said: When they desire a thing, they say, "O Allah," and what they called for comes to them.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Glory be to You, O Allah﴾, its meaning is: "I declare You free of" (tanzih), O Lord, from what the people of polytheism attribute to You of lies and slander against You. [[See the explanation of "subhan" in the earlier passages, vol. 1, pp. 4, 213, note 2, and the references there.]]

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

17566. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: I heard my father, from more than one person, [saying that] 'Atiyyah said concerning them: "Subhan Allah" is a declaration of God's freedom from imperfection (tanzih li-Allah).

17567. Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn Mawhab, who said: I heard Musa ibn Talhah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about "Subhan Allah," and he said: It is the clearing of Allah from evil.

17568. Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa'ib, and Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Qabus related to us, from his father, that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, about "Subhan Allah." He said: It is a word which Allah has approved for Himself.

17569. Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi related to me, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, from Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn Mawhab al-Talhi, from Musa ibn Talhah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about "Subhan Allah," and he said: "A declaration of Allah's freedom from evil."

[[Report 17567 and 17569: "Sufyan" is Sufyan ibn Sa'id, the famous imam al-Thawri. "Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn Mawhab al-Taymi," client of the family of Talhah, who is ascribed to his grandfather and is called "Uthman ibn Wahb," is a reliable Successor (tabi'i) who related from Ibn Umar, Abu Hurayrah, and Umm Salamah. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/155.

"Musa ibn Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah al-Taymi" is a reliable Successor who related from his father and other Companions. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/286, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/147.

This is a report that is mursal (its chain omits the Companion), and it will come connected in the one that follows. But these reports do not have a sound chain.]]

17570. Ali ibn Isa al-Bazzar related to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Hafs ibn Sulayman related to me, saying: Talhah ibn Yahya ibn Talhah related to us, from his father, from Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the explanation of "Subhan Allah," and he said: It is the declaration of Allah's freedom from every evil. [[Report 17570: "Ali ibn Isa al-Bazzar," the teacher of al-Tabari, is "Ali ibn Isa ibn Yazid al-Baghdadi al-Karajiki," reliable, mentioned at No. 2168.

"Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Hafs al-Taymi al-Aishi" is of the descendants of Aishah bint Talhah, reliable, upright in hadith. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/335.

"Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad ibn Imran ibn Musa ibn Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah" is weak in hadith (munkar al-hadith), not to be used as proof. He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan 3:412, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/226, and Mizan al-I'tidal 2:102.

"Hafs ibn Sulayman al-Asadi al-Bazzar" is weak in hadith, mentioned at Nos. 5753 and 11458.

"Talhah ibn Yahya ibn Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah al-Taymi": Ibn Ma'in and others declared him reliable, but al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith," and in his Kitab al-Du'afa al-Saghir (p. 46) he said: "not strong." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/477.

His father, "Yahya ibn Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah al-Taymi," is a reliable Successor. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/283, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/160.

This is a report with a ruined chain (halik al-isnad), as you have seen.]]

17571. Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Tammam al-Kalbi related to me, saying: Sulayman ibn Ayyub related to us, saying: My father related to me, from my grandfather, from Musa ibn Talhah, from his father, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the saying 'Subhan Allah'?" He said: "The declaration of Allah's freedom from evil." [[Report 17571: "Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Tammam al-Kalbi al-Misri," Abu al-Kurus, the teacher of al-Tabari, is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/34.

"Sulayman ibn Ayyub ibn Sulayman ibn Isa ibn Musa ibn Talhah" transmitted a copy from his father, from his forefathers in general. His reports are not followed by others, and he related munkar reports. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the reliable narrators. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/101.

This report is also weak in its chain.]]

* * *

[Tabari continues:] ﴿And their greeting﴾: that is, the greeting of some of them to others. ﴿Therein is peace﴾: that is, you are safe and secure from what the people of the Fire are afflicted with. [[See the explanation of "al-tahiyya" in the earlier passages, vol. 8, pp. 586–590.]]

* * *

The Arabs call a king "al-tahiyya" (the greeting/sovereignty), and from this is the saying of Amr ibn Ma'di Karib:

"I visit with it Abu Qabus, until I make my camel kneel at his tahiyya with my army."

[From a long qasida of his, related by Abu Ali al-Qali in his Amali 3:147–150, and in Lisan al-Arab (h-y-y), with variations in the transmission.]

And from it is the saying of Zuhayr ibn Junab al-Kalbi:

"Of all that a young man attains, I have attained it, except the tahiyya."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And the last of their call﴾: that is, the last of their supplication [[See the explanation of "al-da'wa" in the earlier passages, p. 30, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿is: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾: that is, the last of their supplication is that they say, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds." That is why "an" (that) is made light (the particle أن is lightened) and not doubled, because it is intended as a quotation (hikaya).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 11:

The explanation of His saying, ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them﴾ [and] ﴿So We leave those who do not expect a meeting with Us in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾:

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And if God were to hasten for people the response to their supplications concerning evil, which is that which harms them in self or property, ﴿as He hastens for them the good by responding when they call upon Him for it﴾, meaning: as He hastens for them in good by responding when they call upon Him with it. ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾, meaning: they would have been destroyed, and death, which is their term, would have been hastened for them. [See the explanation of "al-ajal" (term) above, 13:290, footnote 6, and the references there.]

* *

By His saying, ﴿would have been decreed﴾, it is meant: would have been brought to completion for them from their term, [see the explanation of "qada" (decree) above, 13:290, footnote 6, and the references there], and would have been announced to them, as Abu Dhu'ayb said:

"And upon them two coats of mail that Dawud (David) finished, or that the craftsmen of the flowing coats, Tubba', made."

[The verse, its sourcing and its explanation appear above, 2:542.]

* *

= ﴿So We leave those who do not expect a meeting with Us﴾, meaning: We leave those who do not fear Our punishment, and do not believe with certainty in the Resurrection or the Raising [see the explanation of "yadhar" (leave) in the linguistic indices above, root (w-dh-r), and the explanation of "al-raja'" (hope/expectation) above, p. 26, footnote 3, and the references there]. ﴿In their transgression﴾, meaning: in their rebellion and insolence, [see the explanation of "al-tughyan" (transgression) above, 13:291, footnote 2, and the references there], ﴿wandering blindly﴾, meaning: vacillating. [See the explanation of "al-'amah" (blind wandering) above, 13:291, footnote 2, and the references there.]

God, may His praise be exalted, only informed about these disbelievers in the Resurrection of what He informed about them: their transgression and their vacillation concerning it, when He hastens the answer to their supplications concerning evil, if He were to respond to them, that this would lead them to draw near to the idol that one of them associates with God, or attributes that [answer] to its action.

* *

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

17572- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good﴾, he said: It is the saying of a person when angry over his child and his property: "May God not bless it and curse it!"

17573- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good﴾, he said: The saying of a person to his child and property when angry at it: "O God, do not bless it and curse it!" If God were to hasten the answer to them in that, as He answers in good, He would destroy them.

17574- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good﴾, he said: The saying of a person to his child and property when angry at it: "O God, do not bless it and curse it!" ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾, he said: He would have destroyed whoever he prayed against and caused him to die.

17575- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good﴾, he said: The saying of a man to his child when angry at him, or to his property: "O God, do not bless it and curse it!" God said: ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾, he said: He would have destroyed whoever he prayed against and caused him to die. He said: ﴿So We leave those who do not expect a meeting with Us﴾, he said: He says: We do not destroy the people of polytheism, but We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.

17576- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good﴾, he said: It is a man's supplication against himself and his property with what he dislikes, that it be answered for him.

17577- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾, he said: We would have destroyed them. And he recited: ﴿He leaves not upon its back any creature﴾ [Fatir: 45], and said: He would destroy them all.

* *

The phrase ﴿as they seek to hasten﴾ is in the accusative, governed by the verb ﴿hasten﴾ (yu'ajjilu) placed upon it, like the speaker's saying, "I stood today your standing," meaning: I stood as your standing. It is not a verbal noun from ﴿yu'ajjilu﴾, because if it were a verbal noun, the prefixed "ka" (like) of comparison would not properly be introduced before it.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾.

The majority of the readers of Hijaz and Iraq recited it: ﴿Luqdiya ilayhim ajaluhum﴾, in the passive form (what has not been named as agent), with a damma on the qaf of "qudiya" and a raised "ajal" (term).

* *

The majority of the people of Syria recited: ﴿Laqada ilayhim ajalahum﴾, meaning: God decreed for them their term.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: These are two recitations agreeing in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. However, I recite it in the passive form, because most readers hold to it.

**The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿And when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing. But when We remove his adversity from him, he continues on as if he had never called upon Us for adversity that touched him. Thus has it been made attractive to the wasteful what they were doing.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His mention, the Exalted, says: When hardship and distress befall man, ﴿he calls upon Us﴾, meaning he seeks Our help to remove it from him [[See the explanation of "al-mass" (touch) above, 14:64, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "al-dhurr" (adversity) in the lexical indices above, under (d-r-r).]] ﴿lying on his side﴾, meaning lying down on his side. ﴿Or sitting or standing﴾, in the condition he is in when that harm descends upon him. ﴿But when We remove his adversity from him﴾, meaning: when We relieve him of the distress that befell him [[See the explanation of "al-kashf" (removal) above, 11:354 and 13:73.]] ﴿he continues on as if he had never called upon Us for adversity that touched him﴾, meaning: he persists in his former way before the harm reached him, and forgets or ignores the hardship and trial he was in, and abandons thanks to his Lord who relieved him of the affliction that had descended upon him when he sought refuge in Him, and returns to polytheism and to claiming gods and idols as lords alongside Him. His mention, the Exalted, says: ﴿Thus has it been made attractive to the wasteful what they were doing.﴾ Meaning: just as this man we have described had his persistence in disbelief after God removed the harm he was in made attractive to him, so likewise it has been made attractive to those who were wasteful in lying against God and against His prophets, and who exceeded in what they said about them beyond what God had permitted them, [[See the explanation of "al-israf" (wastefulness) above, 12:458, note 1, and the references there.]] what they were doing of the disobedience toward God and of associating partners with Him.

* *

And those who interpret (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

17578 – Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words ﴿calls upon Us lying on his side﴾, he said: "Lying down."

The Interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they did wrong, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, yet they would not believe. Thus do We recompense the guilty people﴾ [10:13]

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We certainly destroyed the nations that denied the messengers of God before you, O polytheists, who associate others with their Lord [[See the explanation of "generations" (al-qurun) above, 11:263.]] = ﴿when they did wrong﴾, meaning: when they associated partners with God and disobeyed His command and prohibition [[See the explanation of "wrong" (al-zulm) above in the lexical indexes (z-l-m).]] = ﴿and their messengers came to them﴾ from God, ﴿with clear proofs﴾, namely the signs and arguments that make manifest the truthfulness of the one who brought them [[See the explanation of "clear proofs" (al-bayyinat) above in the lexical indexes (b-y-n).]].

The meaning of the statement: their messengers came to them with clear signs, [showing] that they were true = ﴿yet they would not believe﴾, meaning: these nations which We destroyed were not going to believe in their messengers and confirm them in what they called them to, namely the affirmation of God's oneness and sincere worship of Him = ﴿Thus do We recompense the guilty people﴾. He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Just as We destroyed these generations before you, O polytheists, for their wronging of themselves, their denial of their messengers, and their rejection of their counsel, so will I deal with you: I will destroy you as I destroyed them, for your denial of your Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and your wronging of yourselves by associating others with your Lord, if you do not turn back and repent to God from your polytheism. For the reward of the one who disbelieves in Me for his disbelief, with Me, is that I destroy him by My wrath in this world and lead him to the Fire in the Hereafter.

**The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth after them, that We might see how you would act﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then We made you, O people, successors (khala'if) after those generations whom We destroyed when they did wrong, succeeding them in the earth and dwelling in it after them.[[See the explanation of "khala'if" above, 13:122, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿That We might see how you act﴾ means: Your Lord looks to see how your deeds compare with the deeds of those nations who perished before you because of their sins and their disbelief in their Lord. Will you follow their example and thereby deserve the punishment they deserved? Or will you oppose their way, believe in God and His Messenger, and affirm resurrection after death, and thereby deserve from your Lord a great reward? As [it is reported]:

17579. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth after them, that We might see how you would act﴾: It was mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Our Lord has spoken truly. We were only made successors so that He may see how our deeds are. So show Allah good deeds from yourselves, by night and by day, in secret and in public."

17580. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Zayd ibn Awf Abu Rabi'ah Fahd narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla: that Awf ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): "I saw in a dream, as one sees in sleep, that a rope was lowered from the sky, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was pulled up by it,[["Intashata" (in the passive form) means: was pulled out, drawn up to the sky and raised to it, from the saying "nashaṭa al-dalw min al-bi'r" when one draws the bucket out of the well, pulling it up without a pulley.]]

then it was lowered again and Abu Bakr was pulled up, then the people were measured around the pulpit,[["Dhara'a al-nas" means: the distance between them and the pulpit was measured by the cubit. One says "dhara'a al-thawb" when one measures it by the cubit.]]

and Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) exceeded [the others] by three cubits to the pulpit." Umar said: "Leave us from your dream; we have no need of it!" When Umar became caliph, [Awf] said: "O Awf, [remember] your dream!" He said: "Do you have any need of my dream? Did you not rebuke me?" He said: "Woe to you! I disliked that you should announce to the successor of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself!" So he related the dream to him, until he reached: "The people were measured to the pulpit by these three cubits." He said: "As for one of them, he will indeed be a caliph. As for the second, he will not fear the blame of any blamer in God's cause. As for the third, he will be a martyr." He said: Then he said: God says: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth after them, that We might see how you would act﴾ – "So you have been made a successor, O son of Umm Umar. Look how you act."

As for his words, "I will not fear the blame of any blamer in God's cause," so be it, if God wills.

As for his words, "He will be a martyr," how can Umar attain martyrdom while the Muslims surround him? Then he said: "Indeed, God does what He wills, and He is All-Powerful."[[The report 17580: "Zayd ibn Awf al-Qati'i," "Abu Rabi'ah," "Fahd," is abandoned (matruk) [in hadith], and it has passed as numbers 5623, 14215, 14218, 14221. In the printed edition here it read: "Yazid ibn Awf, Abu Rabi'ah, the same," and similarly in Ibn Kathir's tafsir 4:287, and this is a strange, shared error! This report was also transmitted by Ibn Sa'd with a different wording, with a good chain (isnad), in al-Tabaqat al-Kabir 3/1/239.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 15:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring us a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: And when the verses of the Book of God, which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, are recited to these polytheists [see the explanation of "recited" (tala) above, 13:502, footnote 3, and the references there] as ﴿clear﴾, plain, indicating the truth ["clear" (bayyinat): see the explanation of bayyinat above in the indexes of language (b-y-n)] = ﴿those who do not expect to meet Us say﴾, meaning: those who do not fear Our punishment, do not believe with certainty in the return to Us, and do not affirm the resurrection [see the explanation of "expectation" (raja') above, p. 34, footnote 2, and the references there] to you = ﴿"Bring us a Qur'an other than this, or change it."﴾, meaning: or alter it [see the explanation of "substitution" (tabdil) above, 11:335 / 12:62, and the indexes of language (b-d-l)] = ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad = ﴿"It is not for me to change it on my own accord,"﴾ that is, from myself [see the explanation of "on my own accord" (tilqa') above, 12:466].

* *

The substitution they asked for, as mentioned, was that the verse of threat be turned into a verse of promise, and the verse of promise into a threat, and that the forbidden be made lawful and the lawful forbidden. So God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to inform them that this is not up to him, and that it belongs to the One whose judgment is not repelled and whose decree is not reviewed. He is only a messenger who conveys and a commanded one who follows.

* *

His saying: ﴿"I only follow what is revealed to me"﴾ means: Say to them: In everything I command you, O people, and forbid you from, I follow only what my Lord sends down to me and commands me [see the explanation of "revelation" (wahy) above in the indexes of language (w-h-y)] = ﴿"Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day."﴾ That is: I fear from God, if I oppose His command, change the rulings of His Book, and alter His revelation, and thereby disobey Him, the punishment of a great day whose terror is immense. That is the day when every nursing mother will forget what she nursed, every pregnant woman will lay down her burden, and you will see people as drunk, though they are not drunk. [This is an embedding of a verse from Surat al-Hajj: 2.]

The Interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Say: "Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you know of it. For I lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May He be exalted, says to His Prophet, providing him with the argument against these polytheists who said to him: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it﴾ — ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad, ﴿"Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you"﴾, meaning: I would not have recited this Qur'an to you, O people, had He not sent it down to me and commanded me to recite it to you. ﴿Nor would He have made you know of it﴾, that is: nor would He have informed you of it. ﴿For I lived among you a lifetime before it﴾, meaning: I remained among you forty years before I recited it to you, and before my Lord revealed it to me. ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ — that if I were fabricating speech that was not mine, I would have fabricated it in the days of my youth and early years, before the time I recited it to you? Had it not been revealed to me and had I not been commanded to recite it to you, I would today have had room and latitude to avoid your enmity, in the state I was in among you before it was revealed to me and I was commanded to recite it to you.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said.

Among those who said so:

17581. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿nor would He have made you know of it﴾: nor would He have informed you of it.

17582. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you nor would He have made you know of it﴾: He means, had God willed, He would not have made you know it.

17583. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿nor would He have made you know of it﴾: He means, "would not have warned you of it."

17584. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say: Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it﴾ — this was the saying of the polytheists of Mecca to the Prophet ﷺ. Then He said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say: Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you know of it. For I lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?﴾ — he lived forty years.

17585. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you know of it﴾: nor would He have informed you of it.

17586. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, that he used to read: ﴿وَلا أَدْرَأْتُكُمْ بِهِ﴾ [wa-la adra'tukum bihi], meaning: nor would I have informed you of it. [[In the manuscript: "wa-la adra'akum", and in the printed edition: "wa-la adra'takum" without hamza; the correct reading is what is recorded here, as stated by Ibn Khalawayh in Shawadhdh al-Qira'at p. 56: "with hamza and taa'", and in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an.]]

17587. Transmitted from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿nor would He have made you know of it﴾: that is, nor would God have made you aware of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This reading attributed to al-Hasan is an error according to the grammarians of Arabic.

* *

Al-Farra' used to say about this: It is reported from al-Hasan that he said: ﴿وَلا أَدْرَأْتُكُمْ بِهِ﴾. He said: If there is a dialect of it other than "daraytu" and "adraytu," then perhaps al-Hasan followed it. As for whether it is derived validly from "daraytu" or "adraytu," it is not, because the yā' and wāw, when the letter before them is open and they are sukūn, remain sound and do not turn into alif, as in "qadaytu" and "da'awtu." Perhaps al-Hasan went by his natural disposition and eloquence and so made it hamza, since it resembles "dara'tu al-hadd" and the like. Arabs sometimes err in a letter when another letter resembling it in the hamza occurs, so they make non-hamzated words hamzated. I heard a woman of Tayy say: "ra'a'tu zawjī bi-abyāt" [I mourned my husband with verses], and they say: "labba'tu bi-l-ḥajj" [I answered the call to Hajj] and "ḥalla'tu al-sawīq" [I stirred the barley-gruel], and they err, because "ḥalla'tu" may be said of driving away thirsty camels, and "labba'tu" means I took it toward "al-laba'" (the first milk of a ewe), and "ra'a'tu zawjī" means I took it toward "ra'a'tu al-laban," when you milk the milk onto the curds, which is "al-ra'itha." [[This is al-Farra's full text in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:459, with slight variations in a few letters.]]

* *

Some Basran grammarians used to say: There is no basis for this reading of al-Hasan, because it would derive from "adrayt" like "a'tayt," except that a dialect of Banu 'Uqayl [[In the printed edition: "lughat Banu 'Uqayl"; the correct form is what is in the manuscript, with the lam.]] says "a'ta'tu," meaning "a'taytu," turning the yā' into alif. The poet said: [[He is Hurayth ibn Inab (with nun) al-Ta'i.]]

Indeed, the people of al-Yamamah have been warned by Tayyi' of a war like the forelock of the famous, noble one.

meaning "kanasiyah"; this was related from al-Mufaddal. Zayd al-Khayl said:

By your life, I do not fear poverty as long as there remains on earth a Qaysi driving camels.

Then he said "baqa," and the poet said: [[He is Labid.]]

I would have restrained a heart that does not heed any reprover, for the one who errs, when forbidden, does not turn back.

meaning "nuhiya." He said: All of this is according to al-Hasan's reading, which is disfavored. He said: Tayy turns every yā' whose preceding letter is kasra into alif, saying "hadhihi jarat" [meaning in "jariyah"]; and in "al-tirqwah" they say "tirqat," and in "al-'arqwah" "'arqat." He said: Some of Tayy said "qad laqat Fazarah," deleting the yā' from "laqiyta," since it could not turn it into alif because of the sukūn of the tā', so two sākin letters would meet. He said: Yunus claimed that "nasa" and "rada" are known dialect forms. The poet said: [[I did not identify his name, nor did I find this line elsewhere.]]

And al-Dhu al-Batn Khalid was made to... nasa, or he forgot to count the clients.

* *

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas another narration regarding the reading of this:

17588. Al-Muthanna related it to us, saying: Al-Mu'alla ibn Asad related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Hanzalah related to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he used to read: ﴿Say: Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would I have warned you of it.﴾

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading that we do not permit ourselves to depart from [[In the printed edition: "la astajiz an tu'adduha"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] is the reading upon which the readers of the regional centers agree: ﴿Say: Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you know of it﴾, meaning: nor would I have informed you of it, nor made you aware of it.

**The commentary on His words, exalted is He: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ (10:17)**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to these polytheists, who attribute to you falsehood regarding what you have brought them from your Lord: Which creature is more transgressing, [[In the printed edition: "which creature is more evil after us," which is a thoroughly corrupt statement. The editor did not read the manuscript well, because it is not clearly transcribed.]] and more presumptuous in speaking out of its proper place, [[See the explanation of "injustice" (ẓulm) above in the linguistic indexes, under (ẓ-l-m).]] than one who invents a lie against God and fabricates falsehood about Him? ﴿Or denies His signs,﴾ meaning His proofs, His messengers, and the signs of His Book? [[See the explanation of "sign" (āyah) above in the linguistic indexes, under ('-y-y).]] He, may His praise be exalted, says to him: Say to them: What you attribute to me is no more astonishing than your lying against your Lord, your fabricating against Him, and your denying His signs. ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed,﴾ meaning: Indeed, those who commit disbelief in this world will not prosper on the Day of Resurrection when they meet their Lord, nor will they attain success. [[See the explanation of "success" (falāḥ) above at 14:415, note 4, and the references there.

And the explanation of "committing crime" (ijrām) above in the linguistic indexes, under (j-r-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 18:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them nor benefit them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ (10:18)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And these polytheists whom I have described to you, O Muhammad, worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them in anything nor benefit them, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. That refers to the gods and idols which they used to worship. ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah."﴾ That is, they used to worship them hoping for their intercession with Allah. [[See the explanation of "intercession" (shafa'ah) above, p. 18, footnote 3, and the references there.]] Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: ﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿"Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"﴾ That is: Do you inform Allah of what does not exist in the heavens or on the earth? [[See the explanation of "naba'" (information/report) in the lexical indices above, under (n-b-a).]] This is because the gods do not intercede for them with Allah in the heavens or on the earth. The polytheists, however, claimed that they interceded for them with Allah. So Allah said to His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: Say to them: Do you inform Allah that what does not intercede in the heavens or on the earth intercedes for you in them? That is falsehood, whose reality and truth He does not know; rather, Allah knows that it is contrary to what you say, and that they do not intercede for anyone, nor benefit nor harm. ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ — that is, exalted and sanctified is Allah above what these polytheists do by associating with Him in worship that neither harms nor benefits, and by their fabricating lies against Him. [[See the explanation of "subhan" above, p. 30, footnote 3, and the references there. And the explanation of "ta'ala" above, vol. 13, p. 317, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 19:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, and they differed. And were it not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been concluded between them concerning that wherein they differ.﴾ (10:19)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Mankind was not but a people of one religion and one creed, and then they differed concerning their religion, so that the paths diverged among them in that. ﴿And were it not for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾ means: were it not that it had already been decreed by God that He would not destroy a people except after the completion of their terms. ﴿It would have been concluded between them concerning that wherein they differ﴾ means: it would have been decided between them by destroying the people of falsehood among them and saving the people of truth. [See the explanation of "qada" (decided) in the preceding indexes of language (qada).]

* *

We have already set out the differences of those who differ regarding the meaning of this in "Surat al-Baqarah," in His saying: ﴿Mankind was one community, then God sent the prophets﴾ (2:213). We explained the correct view on it with its evidences, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. [See what has preceded, 4:275–280.]

17589. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And mankind was not but one community, and they differed﴾, when one of the two sons of Adam killed his brother.

17590. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17591. al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 20:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they say, "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" So say, "The unseen belongs only to Allah, so wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says: And these polytheists say: Why has a sign not been sent down upon Muhammad from his Lord [[See the explanation of "lawla" (why not / if only) in the previous indexes of the discussions of Arabic and grammar and others.]] — meaning: a sign and an indication by which we know that Muhammad is right in what he says? [[See the explanation of "ayah" (sign) in the previous indexes of language (ayy).]] Allah said to him: ﴿So say﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿"The unseen belongs only to Allah."﴾ That is: no one knows who does such a thing except Him, mighty is His praise, because He alone knows the unseen — and it is the hidden and concealed of matters — [[See the explanation of "al-ghayb" (the unseen) in the previous indexes of language (ghayb).]] except Allah. So wait, O people, for Allah's judgment between us, by hastening His punishment upon the wrongdoer among us and by manifesting the truth against him; indeed, I am with you among those who await that. So Exalted is His praise did that, and He judged between them and him by killing them with the sword on the day of Badr.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 21:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold, they scheme against Our signs. Say: "Allah is swifter in planning." Indeed, Our messengers record what you plot.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And when We provide the polytheists who associate others with Allah with relief after distress, and ease after hardship that had befallen them."

It has been said: it refers to rain after drought. "Al-darra'" (adversity) means hardship, and "al-rahma" (mercy) means relief. He says: ﴿behold, they scheme against Our signs﴾, meaning mockery and denial. [[See the explanation of "al-dhawq" (tasting) in what has preceded, vol. 14, p. 230, note 1, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-darra'" (adversity) in what has preceded, vol. 12, p. 573, note 2, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-mass" (touching) in what has preceded, p. 36, note 1, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-makr" (scheming) in what has preceded, vol. 13, p. 502, note 2, and the references there.]] As follows:

17592. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿behold, they scheme against Our signs﴾, he said: "Mockery and denial."

17593. ... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

17594. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Say: "Allah is swifter in planning."﴾ He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who mock Our proofs and evidences: "Allah is swifter in planning," meaning swifter in "mihal" (plotting) against you, and in leading you on gradually and in punishing you, from your scheming against the signs of Allah. [[ "Al-mihal" (with a kasra on the m): scheming and plotting.]]

* *

The Arabs use "idha" (then/behold) as a substitute for "fa'alat" and "fa'alu" (they did), so the verb is omitted after it. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra', vol. 1, pp. 459–460.]] The meaning of the statement is: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them﴾, they scheme against Our signs. So "they scheme" is omitted, and "behold, they have scheming" stands in its place.

* *

As for ﴿Indeed, Our messengers record what you plot﴾, he says: Indeed, Our guardian angels whom We send to you, O people, record against you what you plot against Our signs.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿He it is who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them with a good wind, and they rejoice in it, there comes upon them a violent wind, and the waves come at them from every place, and they think that they are encompassed. They call upon God, making the religion sincerely His, [saying], "If You save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is His remembrance, says: God, He it is who enables you, O people, to travel on land by riding, and on sea in the ships ( = ﴿until when you are in the ship﴾), and these are the boats [[See the explanation of "al-Fulk" (ships) above, 12:502.]] ( = ﴿and they sail with them﴾), meaning: the ships sail with the people ( = ﴿with a good wind﴾), at sea ( = ﴿and they rejoice in it﴾), meaning: the passengers of the ships rejoice in the good wind by which they travel.

* *

The "hā'" in His words "bihā" (in it) refers back to "the good wind."

* *

( = ﴿there comes upon them a violent wind﴾), meaning: a violent wind comes upon the ship, and it is the strong one.

* *

The Arabs say: "rīḥ ʿāṣif" and "ʿāṣifa" (a violent wind), and "aʿṣafat al-rīḥ" and "ʿaṣafat" (the wind blew violently). "Aʿṣafat" is, as it is related, from the Banu Asad. One of the Banu Dubayr said: [[I do not know who said it. "Banu Dubayr" are of the Banu Asad.]]

*Until, when a tempestuous wind blew violently, carrying clouds and thunder whose voice echoes.* [[Maʿānī al-Qurʾān of al-Farrāʾ 1:460: "muzaʿzaʿa" means one that blows fiercely, shaking the trees until it nearly uproots them. "Qiṭār" is the plural of "qaṭr," which is rain. "Raʿd zajil" means a high-pitched thunder, reverberating and loud.]]

* *

( = ﴿and the waves come at them from every place﴾) He, exalted is His remembrance, says: the waves came at the passengers of the ship from every place ( = ﴿and they think that they are encompassed﴾), meaning: they thought that destruction had encompassed them and surrounded them [[See the explanation of "al-Iḥāṭa" (encompassing) above, 14:289, commentary 1, and the references there.]] ( = ﴿they call upon God, making the religion sincerely His﴾), meaning: they made their supplication sincerely to God at that moment, apart from their idols and gods, and their refuge at that time was to God alone, not to them, as follows:

17595. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿They call upon God, making the religion sincerely His﴾, he said: When harm touches them at sea, they make their supplication sincerely to Him.

17596. al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abu ʿUbayda, regarding His words: ﴿making the religion sincerely His﴾, = "hiyā shara hiyā" [[The word came out this way, and I could not determine what it is; it is undoubtedly non-Arabic.]] its explanation: "O Living, O Self-Subsisting."

17597. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, until the end of the verse﴾, he said: These polytheists call upon what they call upon besides God. When harm touches them, they call upon none but God. When He saves them, behold, they associate partners.

* *

( = ﴿If You save us﴾) from this hardship we are in ( = ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾), to You for Your blessings and for Your rescuing us from what we are in, by sincerely worshipping You and devoting obedience to You alone, apart from the gods and rivals.

* *

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His words: ﴿He it is who enables you﴾. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read it: ﴿yusayyirukum﴾ (هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ), from "al-sayr" (travel), with the letter sīn.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar al-Qārī read it: ﴿yanshurukum﴾ (هُوَ الَّذِي يَنْشُرُكُمْ), from "al-nashr" (spreading out), and that is spreading, from the saying of the speaker: "I spread the garment" (nasharat al-thawb), meaning: I unfolded it and spread it out from its folds.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar directed the meaning of that to mean that God raises His servants and spreads them out on land and sea, and it is close in meaning to "al-tasyīr" (causing to travel).

* *

He said: ﴿And they sail with them with a good wind﴾, and He said in another place: ﴿in the laden ship﴾ (Yasin 41), so He used the singular.

* *

"Al-fulk" is a term for the singular and the plural, and it may be masculine or feminine.

[[See Maʿānī al-Qurʾān of al-Farrāʾ 1:460.]]

* *

He said: ﴿And they sail with them﴾, and He had said ﴿He it is who enables you﴾, so He addressed them directly, then returned to speaking of them in the third person. I have explained this in more than one place in this book, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [[See what has passed: 1:154, 196; 3:304, 305; 6:238, 464; 8:447; 11:264, and other places; seek them in the indices of grammar and Arabic and other works.]]

* *

The answer to His words: ﴿until when you are in the ships﴾ is ﴿there comes upon them a violent wind﴾.

* *

As for the answer to His words: ﴿and they think that they are encompassed﴾, it is ﴿they call upon God, making the religion sincerely His﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 23:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when He delivers them, behold, they commit injustice in the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves; [it is] the enjoyment of the worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ (23)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When God delivered those who thought they were encompassed in the sea, from the hardship they were in, they broke their promise to God that they had made to Him, and they committed injustice in the earth, transgressing therein beyond what God had permitted them, by disbelieving in Him and doing His acts of disobedience upon its surface. [See the explanation of "al-baghy" (transgression) above, vol. 12, p. 403, note 2, and the references there.]

God says: O mankind, your transgression that you commit is only against yourselves, and it is against them that you do injustice. And this in which you are = ﴿the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾; He says: that is a provision by which you attain in the hastening of your worldly life. [See the explanation of "al-mata'" (enjoyment) above, vol. 14, p. 340, note 3, and the references there.]

* *

On this interpretation, "al-baghy" (transgression) is in the nominative case, governed by the pronoun referring back to it in His saying "against yourselves." [Our reading in our Qur'an today, in Egypt and elsewhere, is with the accusative of "mata'" (enjoyment), which is the other reading that Abu Ja'far will mention, but he proceeded above in explaining the reading of the nominative.] And His saying ﴿the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ is in the nominative, in the sense of: that is the enjoyment of the worldly life, as He said: ﴿They did not remain but an hour of a day, a notification (balagh)﴾ [Surah al-Ahqaf: 35], meaning: this is a notification.

It may also be possible that the meaning is: your transgression in the worldly life is against yourselves, because by your disbelief you earn for them the anger of God, [it is] the enjoyment of the worldly life. As if He said: your transgression is the enjoyment of the worldly life, so "al-baghy" is nominative by "al-mata'" (the enjoyment), and "against yourselves" is a complement of "al-baghy."

* *

The readers, other than Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq, read "al-mata'" in the nominative. He put it in the accusative, meaning: your transgression against yourselves is an enjoyment in the worldly life, making "al-baghy" nominative by His saying "against yourselves," and "al-mata'" accusative as a circumstantial (ha'l) complement. [See the meanings of the Qur'an by al-Farra' vol. 1, p. 461, on the interpretation of the two readings.]

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then to Us is your return﴾: it means, then to Us after that is your return and your destination, and that is after death = meaning: We will inform you on the Day of Resurrection of what you used to do of the disobedience of God in the world, and We will recompense you for your deeds that preceded from you in the world. [See the explanation of "al-naba'" (information) above, p. 46, note 3, and the references there.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 24:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the example of the worldly life is like water which We sent down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mixed with it grows from which men and cattle eat, until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think that they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who give thought﴾ (24).

Abu Ja'far said: His remembrance, the Exalted, says: Indeed, the example of what you boast of in this world and take pride in, of its adornments and wealth, along with what has been bound up with that of turbidity and disturbance and its passing away by annihilation and death, = is like water which We sent down from the sky, meaning: like rain which We sent down from the sky to the earth = ﴿and the vegetation of the earth mixed with it﴾, meaning: by that rain there grew varieties of plants, mixed with one another, as related:

17598. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the example of the worldly life is like water which We sent down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mixed with it﴾, he said: It mixed, and by the water there grew every kind of what men eat, such as wheat, barley, all the grains of the earth, herbs and fruits, and what cattle and beasts eat of grass and pasturage. [[See the explanation of "al-An'am" above, 13:280, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until when the earth takes on its adornment﴾, it means: its goodness and splendour appear [[See the explanation of "al-zukhruf" above, 12:55, 56.]] = ﴿and is beautified﴾, meaning: and adorns itself = ﴿and its people think﴾, meaning: the people of the earth = ﴿that they have power over it﴾, meaning: over what it has produced.

* *

The report was given about "the earth" while the meaning is the plants, since what is intended is understood from the address.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Our command comes to it by night or by day﴾, it says: Our command, meaning: Our decree of destruction of the plants upon it, came to the earth = whether by night or by day = ﴿and We make it﴾, meaning: and We make what is upon it = ﴿as a harvest﴾, meaning: cut down and uprooted from its roots. [[See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda, 1:277.]]

* *

= Rather, it is "mahsudah" (reaped), turned into "hasid".

* *

= ﴿as if it had not flourished yesterday﴾, meaning: as if those crops and plants had not been standing, sprouting upon the surface of the earth before that, yesterday.

* *

Its origin is from "ghaniya fulan bi-makan kadha, yaghna bihi", when he dwelt in it, as al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani said:

"It flourished through that when they were neighbours to you,
from it, with the inclination of a message and affection."

[[From his Diwan: 65; it will also appear in the commentary at 12:66 (Bulaq) and elsewhere, from his famous qasida in which he describes the unveiled woman; and before it: "In pursuit of a fair one who shot you with an arrow, and it struck your heart, though you did not aim." In the printed edition it read "idh hum li jiratun" ("when they were a neighbourhood to me"); I have restored what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the version in his Diwan.]]

* *

Meaning: thus does annihilation come upon what you boast of in your worldly life and its adornments, so it perishes and destroys it, just as Our command and decree destroyed the plants of this earth after its beauty and radiance, until it became as if it had not flourished yesterday, as if it had not been growing upon its surface before that.

God, His praise be exalted, says: ﴿Thus do We detail the signs for a people who give thought﴾, meaning: just as We have made clear to you, O people, the example of the world and informed you of its judgment and affair, so do We make clear Our proofs and evidences for whoever reflects, takes heed and considers. [[See the explanation of "tafsil al-ayat" above, p. 24, note 1, and the references there.]]

He specified it for the people of reflection, because they are the people who distinguish between matters and investigate the realities of the doubts that arise in the breasts.

* *

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

17599. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿until when the earth takes on its adornment﴾, the verse: That is, by God, if one clings to the world and is greedy for it, the world is about to spit him out and be finished with him.

17600. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿and is beautified﴾, he said: it grew and became beautiful.

17601. Al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna related to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, who said: I heard Marwan reading this verse on the pulpit: ﴿until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think that they have power over it, and God would not destroy it except for the sins of its people﴾. He said: I have read it, and it is not in the mushaf. 'Abbas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Abbas said: Thus did Ibn 'Abbas read it. So they sent to Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: Thus did Ubayy ibn Ka'b recite it to me. [[The report 17601: "al-Harith" is al-Harith ibn Abi Usama, trustworthy, mentioned many times before.

"'Abd al-'Aziz" is 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Aban al-Umawi, a liar, wicked, a fabricator of hadith, mentioned many times before, the last at no. 14333.

As for "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham", I have not found mention of him in the books of biography.

His father "Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman" was "the monk of Quraysh", trustworthy, learned, intelligent, generous, a prolific narrator, one of the seven jurists of Medina. Ibn Hajar mentioned him in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 5:153, and al-Zubayri in Nasab Quraysh: 303, 304. Ibn Sa'd mentioned his children and said: "Abu Bakr's sons: 'Abd al-Rahman, who has no descendants, and 'Abd Allah, and 'Abd al-Malik, and Hisham..." Al-Zubayri did not mention this in Nasab Quraysh, but he mentioned a story which begins with "he said to his son 'Abd Allah: go to your uncle al-Mughira ibn 'Abd al-Rahman..." Then he said in the same story a little later: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman went", and Ibn Sa'd named him 'Abd al-Rahman when he counted the children of Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. However, the text of Ibn Sa'd contradicts what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said, so they are undoubtedly two different men. I have not found sufficient reports to resolve this discrepancy. "'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman" is not trustworthy. "Marwan" is Marwan ibn al-Hakam. This report, as you see, is defective in its chain from every side. The reading in it, if it is authentic through other than this defective route, is a reading of interpretation, as is well known, and as we have pointed out many times regarding similar cases. It is not permissible for a reader to recite with its like as the text of recitation, due to its irregularity and its contradiction of the orthography of the mushaf by addition, without a proof which must be accepted.]]

17602. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿as if it had not flourished yesterday﴾, he said: as if it had not lived, as if it had not enjoyed.

17603. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Usama related to us, from Isma'il, who said: I heard Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman say: In the reading of Ubayy: ﴿as if it had not flourished yesterday, and We did not destroy it except for the sins of its people. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who give thought﴾. [[The report 17603: "Abu Usama" is Hammad ibn Usama ibn Yazid al-Qurashi, trustworthy, narrated by the group, mentioned many times before.

"Isma'il" is Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid al-Ahmasi, trustworthy, narrated by the group, mentioned many times before. As for "Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman", he did not hear from Ubayy ibn Ka'b. So this is a mursal chain.]]

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿and is beautified﴾.

The majority of the readers of the Hijaz and Iraq recited it: ﴿wazzayyanat﴾, meaning: and adorned itself, but they assimilated the taa' into the zay because their articulation points are close, and they added an alif so that it could be reached in recitation, since the taa' had become quiescent, and a quiescent letter cannot be begun with.

* *

It is related from Abu al-'Aliya, Abu Raja', al-A'raj, and other groups besides them, that they recited it: ﴿wa-azyanat﴾ on the pattern of "af'alat".

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this is: ﴿wazzayyanat﴾, because the authoritative readers agree upon it.

**Commentary on the Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah calls to the Abode of Peace, and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ (25)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His servants: O people, do not seek the world and its adornment, for its end is to perishing and vanishing, just as the plant which Allah has struck as an example for it ends in destruction and ruin. Rather, seek the everlasting Hereafter, act for it, and seek what is with Allah by obeying Him. For Allah calls you to His abode, which is His gardens that He has prepared for His friends, so that you may be safe from worries and sorrows therein, and secure from the perishing of the bounties and honors in it which He has prepared for whoever enters it. He guides whom He wills of His creation, granting them success in reaching the straight path, which is Islam. He, exalted is His praise, made it a means to attain His pleasure and a way for whoever rides it and travels upon it to His gardens and His honor. [[See the explanation of "guidance" and "the straight path" in the preceding lexical indexes under (hadha), (sarata), (qawama).]] As follows:

17604. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "Allah" is the Peace (al-Salam), and His abode is Paradise.

17605. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And Allah calls to the Abode of Peace﴾, he said: "Allah" is the Peace, and His abode is Paradise.

17606. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It was said to me: 'Let your eye sleep, let your heart understand, and let your ear listen.' So my eye slept, my heart understood, and my ear listened. Then it was said: 'A lord built a house, then prepared a feast, then sent a summoner. Whoever answers the summoner enters the house, eats from the feast, and the lord is pleased with him. And whoever does not answer the summoner does not enter the house, does not eat from the feast, and the lord is not pleased with him.'" So Allah is the Lord, the House is Islam, the feast is Paradise, and the summoner is Muhammad (ﷺ). [[The report: 1760six. "Abu Qilabah" is 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Jarmi, one of the leading Successors, who has passed previously several times. This is a mursal report (one in which the Successor relates directly from the Prophet without naming the Companion), and something similar will come connected in the takhrij of report no. 1760nine.]]

1760 7. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: ﴿And Allah calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾, he said: It has been reported to us that in the Torah it is written: "O seeker of good, come forward; O seeker of evil, desist."

1760 8. al-Husayn ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabshah narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Khulayd al-'Asri narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no day on which its sun rises except that on either side of it there are two angels calling out, which all of Allah's creation hears except the two jinn and humankind: 'O people, come to your Lord, for what is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and distracting.'" He said: And this was revealed in the Qur'an in His words: ﴿And Allah calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾. [[The word "janbah" (with a fatha on the jim and nun, or fatha on the jim with sukun on the nun) means "side" or "direction." Transmitters of hadith pronounce it with two fathas, while the lexicographers prefer the sukun on the nun, and they cite as evidence the verse of Abu Sa'tarah al-Bulani:

"Not a drop of rain-water's seed that was flung
by the two sides of al-Judi, while the night was dark,

with the finest of what is in it, and I have not tasted its flavor,
but I, as the eye perceives, am a rider (faris)."

What the hadith scholars have transmitted is sound and authentic.]] The report: 1760 8. "al-Husayn ibn Salamah ibn Isma'il ibn Yazid ibn Abi Kabshah al-Azdi al-Tahhan," the teacher of al-Tabari, is trustworthy. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah and others narrated from him; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim mentions him at 1/2/54. "'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr" is Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi, trustworthy, who has passed many times, the last at no. 12795. "'Abbad ibn Rashid al-Tamimi" is trustworthy but not strong; al-Bukhari narrated from him in conjunction with others (muqarran), and he has passed at nos. 11060 and 12527. "Khulayd ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Asri" narrated from Abu al-Darda; Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and it is said that he was a client (mawla) of Abu al-Darda. Al-Bukhari in al-Kabir and Ibn Abi Hatim distinguished between "Khulayd, client of Abu al-Darda" and "Khulayd ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Asri." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/181, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/383. This report has a sound chain. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad at length, 5:197, through the route of Hammam, from Qatadah, from Khulayd al-'Asri. Its addition is: "And never does the sun set except that on either side of it there are two angels calling out, making the people of the earth hear, except the two jinn and humankind: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement, and give the one who withholds destruction.'" al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:304, at length, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

1760 9. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Layth ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us one day and said: "I saw in a dream as if Jibril was at my head and Mika'il at my feet, and one of them said to the other: 'Strike for him an example!' So the other said: 'Listen, may your ear hear; understand, may your heart understand. Your example and the example of your community is like the example of a king who took a house, then built in it a dwelling, then made in it a feast, then sent a messenger calling people to his food. Some of them answered the messenger, and some of them abandoned him.'

So Allah is the King, the House is Islam, the dwelling is Paradise, and you, O Muhammad, are the Messenger. Whoever answers you enters Islam, whoever enters Islam enters Paradise, and whoever enters Paradise eats of what is in it." [[The report: 1706 9 (as numbered). "Khalid ibn Yazid al-Jumahi al-Misri," trustworthy, has passed many times, the last at no. 13377. "Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal al-Laythi al-Misri," trustworthy, has passed many times, the last at no. 17429; his narration from Jabir is mursal, and his hadith from Jabir was cited by al-Bukhari as a mu'allaq (suspended) report used as a supporting narration (mutaba'ah). In al-Tirmidhi: "Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal did not meet Jabir." So this is a mursal report from Jabir, which al-Hakim connected in al-Mustadrak 2:338, through the route of "'Abd Allah ibn Salih, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and he recited this verse: ﴿And Allah calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾, and said: Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to me." Then al-Hakim said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:304, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, with the wording and chain of al-Hakim. In the printed edition it read "akala minha" (ate from it), which agrees with the other sources; I have adopted what is in the manuscript, because it is clear and has no ambiguity in its reading or meaning.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 26 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and extra﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, means: For those who worshipped Allah well in this world, among His creatures, obeying Him in what He commanded and forbade, ﴿is the best [reward]﴾.
* *
Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of "al-husna" (the best [reward]) and "al-ziyada" (the extra) which He promised to the good-doers among His creatures.

Some of them said: "Al-husna" is Paradise, which Allah made the reward for the good-doers among His creatures, and "the extra beyond it" is looking upon Allah.

Those who said this:

17610. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and extra﴾, he said: Looking at the face of their Lord. [[Report 17610: 'Amir ibn Sa'd al-Bajali, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i) who has one hadith in the Sahih, and his narration from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq is mursal (broken-chained). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/321. This report was also transmitted by al-Ajurri in al-Shari'a p. 257, through several routes, as a mursal report.]]

17611. Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Qays, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Nimran, from Abu Bakr: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and extra﴾, he said: Looking at the face of Allah. [[Report 17611: Sa'id ibn Nimran al-Na'ti, who narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and from whom 'Amir ibn Sa'd al-Bajali narrated. Sa'id ibn Nimran al-Na'ti was one of the companions of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib; he attached him to 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib when the latter was appointed governor of Yemen, and he witnessed al-Yarmuk. His son Musafir ibn Sa'id ibn Nimran was one of al-Mukhtar's companions. He is biographed in al-Kabir 2/1/473, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/68, Ibn Sa'd 6:56. al-Bukhari said "he heard Abu Bakr," but it is strange that Ibn Hajar biographed him in Lisan al-Mizan 3:46 and said "majhul" (unknown), and al-Dhahabi likewise said so in Mizan al-I'tidal 1:392. I fear that this is an oversight by al-Dhahabi and Ibn Hajar, and that by "majhul" they meant that the state of his narration and hearing from Abu Bakr is unknown, not Sa'id ibn Nimran himself. Otherwise how could he be unknown when he is biographed and mentioned, and al-Tabari mentions him in his History 4:126 under the events of the year 14, at the conquest of al-Yarmuk, and again in the year 17 (4:194) in the report about Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that Sa'd "sent to a group of the genealogists of the Arabs and their men of opinion and intellect, among them Sa'id ibn Nimran and Mash'alah ibn Nu'aym." In the section on the mention of the scribes from the beginning of Islam (History 7:198): "Sa'id ibn Nimran al-Hamdani used to write for 'Ali, then he was appointed judge of Kufa by Ibn al-Zubayr." Wakī' also mentioned him in Akhbar al-Qudat 2:396, 397, and said: "When 'Ali came to Kufa, he appointed Sa'id ibn Nimran al-Hamdani, then dismissed him and appointed 'Ubayda al-Salmani in his place," then said on p. 397: "Ibn al-Zubayr appointed Sa'id ibn Nimran al-Hamdani as judge, and he judged for three years." al-Jahshiyari in al-Wuzara' wa-al-Kuttab p. 23 also mentioned his writing for 'Ali. Thus it is established that he is known and famous; as for "unknown," it refers to the state of his hearing from Abu Bakr, were it not for al-Bukhari's statement that he heard Abu Bakr.
Whatever the case, this report has a problem in its isnad. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:306, adding its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Daraqutni, Ibn Mandah in al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyya, al-Lalaka'i, al-Ajurri, and al-Bayhaqi, all of them on the vision (of Allah).]]

17612. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and extra﴾, he said: Looking at the face of their Lord.

17613. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd, who said regarding this verse: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and extra﴾, he said: "The extra" is looking at the face of the Most Merciful.

17614. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Muslim ibn Nudhayr, from Hudhayfah: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and extra﴾, he said: Looking at the face of their Lord. [[Report 17614: Muslim ibn Nudhayr al-Sa'di, also said to be Muslim ibn Yazid, and it is said that "Yazid" was his grandfather. He narrated from Hudhayfah, and Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i narrated from him. He was from the people of Kufa, rarely narrated hadith, and it is mentioned that he believed in the return (raj'ah). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/273, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/197, 199 under "Muslim ibn Yazid al-Sa'di," and Ibn Sa'd 6:159. "Nudhayr" is with a dammah on the nun, as a diminutive.]]

17615. Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq say regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿and extra﴾, he said: Looking at the face of the Most Merciful.

17616. 'Ali ibn 'Isa narrated to me, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi narrate from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will send to the people of Paradise a herald who calls out: "Has Allah fulfilled for you what He promised you?" They will look at the honor Allah has prepared for them, and they will say: Yes! Then He says: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and extra﴾: looking at the face of the Most Merciful. [[Report 17616: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali is extremely weak (dha'if bi-marrah), as mentioned several times, the last being no. 14690. Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi is Tarif ibn Mujalid, a trustworthy Successor. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/356, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/492. This report is weak in its isnad, and it will come in the two following reports.]]

17617. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi informed us, who said: I heard Abu Musa al-Ash'ari preaching from the pulpit of Basra, saying: Allah will send on the Day of Resurrection an angel to the people of Paradise, who says: "O people of Paradise, has Allah fulfilled for you what He promised you?" They will look, [[In the printed edition: "They will look, at the honor Allah has prepared for them, and they will see," adding to the manuscript what is not in it; I think the editor did this following what came in the earlier report.]] and they will see the ornaments, the garments, the fruits, the rivers, and the pure spouses, and they will say: "Yes, Allah has fulfilled for us what He promised us!" Then the angel says: "Has Allah fulfilled for you what He promised you?" three times, and they lose nothing of what they were promised, and they say: "Yes!" He says: "There remains something for you. Allah says: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and extra﴾. Indeed the best [reward] is Paradise, and the extra is looking at the face of Allah."
