[[Report 17618: Shabib ibn Sa'id al-Taymi al-Habati, whose hadiths are sound, and it has passed as no. 6613 and 12085; however, Ibn Wahb narrated from him some strange (munkar) hadiths. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 26 (part 2 of 2):

Others said: "al-Husna" is one good deed rewarded with one, and "al-ziyadah" (the increase) is the multiplication up to the full ten.

He said: It is like His words: ﴿And with Us is more﴾ [Qaf 35]. He means: He will repay them for their deeds and increase them from His bounty. And He said: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged﴾ [al-An'am 160].
١٧٦٣٨- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Alqamah ibn Qays, regarding: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward, and more﴾. He said: I said: This is the best reward; so what is the increase? He said: Did you not see that Allah says: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾?
١٧٦٣٩- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say regarding this verse: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward, and more﴾. He said: The increase is: for a good deed, ten times its like, up to seven hundred fold.
* *
Others said: "al-Husna" is one good deed like another good deed, and "al-ziyadah" is the increase of forgiveness and good pleasure from Allah.
Those who said this:
١٧٦٤٠- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward﴾: its like is a good reward, "and more": forgiveness and good pleasure.
* *
Others said: "al-ziyadah" is what they were given in this world.
Those who said this:
١٧٦٤١- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward, and more﴾: He said: "al-husna" is Paradise, and "and more" is what He gave them in this world, which He will not call them to account for on the Day of Resurrection. And they recited: ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾ [al-Ankabut 27]. He said: what He gave him of what he loved in this world; his reward was hastened for him therein.
* *
Ibn Abbas used to say, regarding His words: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward﴾, that:
١٧٦٤٢- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward﴾, he means: for those who bore witness that there is no god but Allah.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings, in terms of truth, is to say: Allah, blessed and exalted, promised the good-doers among His servants the best reward for their good conduct, that He would reward them for their obedience to Him with Paradise, and that their faces would be made bright; and with the best reward He promised them more beyond it. Among the increase beyond their admission to Paradise is that He honours them by looking at Him, that He gives them chambers of pearls, and that He increases them in forgiveness and good pleasure. All of this is among the increases of Allah's bounty to them beyond the best reward which Allah has made for the people of His gardens. Our Lord, exalted is His praise, by His words ﴿and more﴾ generalised the increases beyond "the best reward", and did not specify any of them over any other. It is not improbable of Allah's grace that He should gather all of that for them; rather, all of it is gathered for them, if Allah wills. So the most correct of these sayings is that it be generalised, as He, mighty is His mention, generalised it.
* *
On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And neither dust nor humiliation will cover their faces. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever﴾ (26).
Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His praise, ﴿And neither dust nor humiliation will cover their faces﴾, He means: no gloom or darkness will cover their faces, such that from grief they become as though dust had settled upon them.

١٧٦٤٥- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And neither dust will cover their faces﴾, he said: the blackness of the faces.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 27:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Those who have earned evil deeds - the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent, and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His, the Exalted's, remembrance means: Those who did evil deeds in this world, disobeying Allah therein and disbelieving in Him and His Messenger [[See the explanation of "kasaba" (earned) in the earlier lexical indices, under (k-s-b) and (s-w-').]] = ﴿the recompense of an evil deed﴾, for their evil action which they did in this world = ﴿is its equivalent﴾, of the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter = ﴿and humiliation will cover them﴾, meaning: disgrace and abasement will overwhelm them, through the punishment of Allah upon them [[See the explanation of "rahaq" above, p. 72, and the explanation of "dhillah" above, p. 72, note 3, and the references there.]] = ﴿They will have no protector from Allah﴾, meaning: they will have no one from Allah to prevent them, when He punishes them, who could come between Him and them.

* *

In accordance with what we have said is the statement regarding "and humiliation will cover them": the people of interpretation said:

Those who said this:

17646- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿and humiliation will cover them﴾, he said: Humiliation and hardship will overwhelm them.

* *

The grammarians differed concerning what makes "al-jaza'" (the recompense) nominative.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: it is raised by an implied "lahum" (for them), as if it were said: "and for them is the recompense of an evil deed, its equivalent," just as He said: ﴿So a fast of three days during the Hajj﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 196], meaning: "then upon him is a fast of three days." He said: "If you wish, you may raise al-jaza' by the bi' in His words: ﴿and the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent﴾."[[This is the view of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 461. In the printed edition it reads "wa-jaza'" with a waw, while in al-Farra's Ma'ani it reads "fa-jaza'" with a fa'; I do not find in the Qur'an a verse with such a form with waw or fa', and he meant this very verse.]]

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "al-jaza'" is nominative as the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is ﴿bi-mithliha﴾ (by its equivalent). He said: the meaning of the sentence is: "a recompense of an evil deed like it," and the "ba'" was added, as it was added in His words: "bi-hasbika qawl al-su'" (your sufficiency is an evil saying).

Some of them denied this view, saying: It is permissible that the "ba'" in "hasb" [is extra [[The parenthetical addition is necessary for the sentence to be sound.]]]

because the interpretation is: "if you say evil, then it suffices you." So when it did not enter the predicate, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "did not enter the recompense," which is an error beyond doubt.]] it was introduced into "hasb": "bi-hasbika an taqum" (it suffices you that you stand), meaning: if you stand, then it is sufficient for you. [[I fear that some part of the sentence has fallen out.]] If what follows "hasb" is praised, the "ba'" is introduced into what follows it, as in your saying: "hasbuka bi-Zayd" (Zayd is sufficient for you), and it is not permissible to say "bi-hasbika Zayd," because Zayd is the one praised, so it is not an interpretation of a predicate. [[In the printed edition and manuscript at this place too: "it is not an interpretation of a recompense," which is a corruption beyond doubt.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these statements in my view is that "al-jaza'" is nominative by an implied element, meaning: "so for them is the recompense of an evil deed, its equivalent," because Allah said in the verse before it: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾, describing what He has prepared for His friends, then followed it with the report of what Allah has prepared for His enemies. The more fitting way of the speech is to say: "and for those who earned evil deeds is a recompense of evil deeds," and when this is understood in this sense, the "ba'" is a complement of "al-jaza'."

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿As if their faces had been covered with pieces of the night, dark. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ (27)

Abu Ja'far said: His, the Exalted's, remembrance means: As if the faces of those who earned evil deeds had been clothed [[See the explanation of "al-ighsha'" (covering) above, 12: 483, note 2, and the references there.]]

= ﴿pieces of the night﴾, and "qit'a" is the plural of "qit'ah" (a piece).

* *

Qatadah used to say concerning the interpretation of this:

17647- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding: ﴿As if their faces had been covered with pieces of the night, dark﴾, he said: a darkness of the night.

* *

The reciters differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿qit'an﴾. The majority of the reciters of the metropolitan cities read it ﴿qit'an﴾ with a fatha on the ta', in the sense of the plural of "qit'ah," and the meaning of the interpretation is: as if the face of each person among them had been covered by a piece of the darkness of the night; then it was made plural, so it was said: "as if their faces had been covered with pieces of darkness," since "wajh" (face) was made plural.

* *

Some later reciters read it "qit'an" with a sukun on the ta', meaning: as if their faces had been covered with darkness of the night, and a remnant of the night, an hour of it, as He said: ﴿So travel with your family during a portion of the night﴾ [Surah Hud: 81 / Surah al-Hijr: 65], that is, with a remnant that remains of it.

And the reading in this form is supported by its appearing in the codex of Ubayy: ﴿wa-yaghsha wujuhahum qit'un mina al-layli muzlim﴾. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 462.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading that is not permissible to oppose in my view is the reading of those who read it with a fatha on the ta', due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters of the metropolitan cities upon its correctness, and the anomaly of anything other than it. And the proof of the corruption of the other reading suffices in the departure of its reciter from what the reciters of the Muslim cities upheld. [[In the printed edition: "the people of the cities and Islam," which is a foolish mistake.]]

* *

If someone says to us: If the correct reading is what I have said, what is the reason for the masculine form and singular of "muzlim" (dark), when it is an adjective of "qit'a" and "qit'a" is a plural of a feminine noun?

It is said: There are two explanations for this masculine form: [[In the printed edition: "in its masculinity," with a possessive pronoun, which is also a mistake.]]

One is that "qit'an" is the accusative of circumstance from "al-layl" (the night), as explained many times before, see what was said earlier at 11: 455 / 12: 477 and the indices of terms. Al-Tabari has explained the meaning of "qit'" most clearly at this place, and our discussion of it has preceded many times. And if it is an adjective of "al-layl," then since it is indefinite and "al-layl" is definite, it is put in the accusative as a qit'. The meaning of the sentence then is: as if their faces had been covered with pieces of the dark night; then the alif and lam were removed from "muzlim," and since it became indefinite while being an adjective of "al-layl," it was put in the accusative as a qit'. The people of Basra call such a case "hal" (circumstantial state), and the Kufans call it "qat'" (qit').

The other explanation is in the manner of the poet's saying: [[He is Abu Dhu'ayb.]]

"Had the praise of a living man raised anyone * [[In his Diwan, p. 113, at the end of one of his poems, the Diwan's version reads: "Had the praise of a living man raised anyone ... the lofty praises revived your fathers' glory." This has no evidence in it, and it is also transmitted as: "Had the praise of a living man raised anyone." And this is the evidence.]]

And the first explanation is the better of the two.

As for His words: ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire﴾, meaning: these are the ones whose description I have given you, the people of the Fire who are its inhabitants [[See the explanation of "ashab al-nar" (companions of the Fire) above, under the lexical indices (s-h-b).]]

= ﴿they will abide therein eternally﴾, meaning: they will remain therein. [[See the explanation of "al-khulud" (eternity) above, under the lexical indices (kh-l-d).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 28:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Stay in your place, you and your partners." Then We will separate them, and their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted remembrance says: On the day We gather all of creation together for the standing place of reckoning [see the explanation of "al-hashr" (gathering) above, vol. 13, p. 529, note 4, and the references there]. Then We will say at that time to those who associated others with Allah, taking gods and rivals: ﴿Stay in your place﴾, meaning: remain in your place, stand in your position, you, O polytheists, and your partners whom you used to worship besides Allah, the gods and idols. ﴿Then We will separate them﴾, meaning: We will divide between the polytheists who associated others with Allah and those whom they associated with Him.

* *

[From their saying: "zilt al-shay' uzīluhu" (I separated the thing), when you separate it from something else and cut it off from it.] [This addition between brackets is a clarification from the wording of the lexicon, which is necessary; in the manuscript the text ran as one continuous sequence, and this is a copyist's error. See also al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Quran, vol. 1, p. 492.] He said: "fazayyalna" is intended to express the repetition and multiplication of the act, and he did not say "fazilna baynahum."

* *

It has been reported from some of them that he used to read it: ﴿fa-zayalna baynahum﴾, as it is said: ﴿wa la tusa''ir khaddaka﴾ [Surah Luqman: 18]. The Arabs often do this with the form "fa''ala", sometimes adding an alif in place of the doubling, so they say "faa'ala" when the verb has one subject. When it concerns two parties, they almost always say only "faa'ala." [See also the explanation of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Quran, vol. 1, p. 492; it is similar to it.]

* *

﴿And their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us."﴾ This is when ﴿those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their bonds are cut off﴾, when it is said to the polytheists, "Follow what you used to worship besides Allah," and their gods are set up for them, they say, "We used to worship these!" Then the gods say to them: "You did not used to worship us," as follows:

17648. I was told, from Muslim ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: On the Day of Resurrection there will be an hour in which there is great hardship. The gods that they used to worship will be set up for them, and it will be said: "These are what you used to worship besides Allah." The gods will say: "By Allah, we did not hear, nor see, nor understand, nor did we know that you were worshipping us!" They will say: "By Allah, it was you whom we used to worship!" Then the gods will say to them: ﴿Allah suffices as a witness between us and you. Indeed we were unaware of your worship.﴾

17649. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And on the Day We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Stay in your place, you and your partners." Then We will separate them﴾, he said: We divided them. ﴿And their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us."﴾ They will say: "Yes, indeed we used to worship you!" Then they will say: ﴿Allah suffices as a witness between us and you; indeed we were unaware of your worship﴾, "We did not hear, nor see, nor speak!" Then Allah says: ﴿There, every soul will be tested for what it has sent before﴾, to the end of the verse.

* *

It has been related from Mujahid that he interpreted "al-hashr" (gathering) in this place as death.

1765. Ibn Wakf'i related to us, saying: My father related to us, from al-A'mash, who said: I heard them mention from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And on the Day We will gather them all together﴾, he said: The gathering is death.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What we have said about this is more fitting as its interpretation, because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, informed that He will say on that day to those who associated others with Allah what He mentioned He will say to them, and it is known that this does not occur in the grave; rather it is a report of what will be said to them, and what they will say, at the standing place after the resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 29:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah suffices as a witness between us and you; indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, says, reporting the statement of the associates of the polytheists, from among the deities and idols, to them on the Day of Resurrection, when the polytheists who ascribed partners to Allah said to them: "It is you we used to worship." ﴿So Allah suffices as a witness between us and you﴾, meaning: they say, "Allah is sufficient as a witness between us and you, O polytheists, for He knows that we did not know what you say." ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾, meaning: we were never unaware of your worship of us, apart from Allah, [but rather] we were not conscious of it and did not know it. [See the explanation of "ghafla" (heedlessness) above, p. 25, footnote 2, and the references there.] As follows:

17651 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾, he said: "Everything that is worshipped besides Allah." [In the printed edition: "He said that, everything," adding "that"; I have retained what is in the manuscript, and it is acceptable.]

17652 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

17653 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾, he said: "That is said by everything that was worshipped besides Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 30:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿There every soul will be tested for what it earlier sent forth, and they will be returned to God, their true Master, and what they used to fabricate will forsake them﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿There every soul will be tested (tabluu)﴾, with the letter ba', meaning: at that time every soul will be tested for what it sent forward of good or evil. [[In the printed edition: "bima qaddamat" with ba', which is not a good reading of the manuscript. And see the explanation of "al-ibtila'" (testing) in the earlier vocabulary indexes under (b-l-w).]]

Mujahid also recited it and interpreted it in this way.

17654- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿There every soul will be tested for what it earlier sent forth﴾, he said: it will be tested.

17655- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

17656- Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

A group of the people of Kufa and some of the people of the Hijaz recited it: ﴿tatlu kullu nafsin ma aslafat﴾, with the letter ta'. [[See this reading and its explanation earlier, 2:411.]]

* *

The readers who recited it this way also differed over its interpretation.

Some of them said: its meaning and interpretation is: there every soul will follow what it sent forward in the world for that Day. [[See the explanation of "yatlu" in the earlier vocabulary indexes (t-l-w).]]

A report similar to this has been related from the Prophet ﷺ, through a route and chain that is not approved, that he said: On the Day of Resurrection, for every people will be displayed what they used to worship besides God, and they will follow them until they lead them into the Fire. He said: Then the Messenger of God ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿There every soul will follow what it earlier sent forth﴾. [[I have not found the text of this report in any place other than this, either with or without a chain.]]

* *

Others said: rather, its meaning is: it will read the book of its good deeds and its bad deeds, meaning it will read it, as He, great is His praise, said: ﴿And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find laid open﴾ [Surah al-Isra: 13].

* *

Others said: "tatlu" means "ta'ayana" (to witness directly). [[In the printed edition, in all these places, it is "tabluu" with ba', whereas in the manuscript it is undotted; the correct reading is with ta', as is also clear from the context of the interpretation of this reading.]]

Mention of those who said that:

17657- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿There every soul will follow what it earlier sent forth﴾, he said: what it did. "Tatlu": it witnesses it directly.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is to say: these are two well-known readings, each of which has been recited by leading readers, and their meanings are close. This is because whoever follows in the Hereafter what he sent forward of deeds in the world will be brought by it to its destination, so there he will learn what he sent forward of good or evil in the world; and whoever learns from the one who sent forward his deeds in the Hereafter, he only learns, after his arrival at the place where it has settled him, what he sent forward of his deeds in the world. So in both states he is following what he sent forward of his deeds and is being tested by it. Thus whichever of the two readings the reader adopts, as we have described, he has hit the truth in this matter.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and they will be returned to God, their true Master﴾, He says: these polytheists will return on that Day to God, who is their Lord and Owner, the Truth about whom there is no doubt, rather than what they used to claim as lords for themselves among the gods and rivals; ﴿and what they used to fabricate will forsake them﴾, He says: what they used to invent of falsehood and lies against God, by their claim that their idols are partners of God and that they bring them near to Him in nearness, will vanish from them. [[See the explanation of the terms of this verse in the earlier vocabulary indexes.]] As:

17658- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿and they will be returned to God, their true Master, and what they used to fabricate will forsake them﴾, he said: what they used to invoke besides Him of rivals and gods; what they used to fabricate was the gods, for they made them rivals and gods alongside God as a fabrication and a lie.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 31:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living? And who manages the affair?" They will say, "Allah." So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate idols and images with Allah: ﴿Who provides for you from the heaven﴾, the rain and the downpour, and causes its sun to rise for you, and darkens its night, and brings forth its forenoon; ﴿and from the earth﴾, your sustenance and your food, which He causes to grow for you, and the fruits of its trees. ﴿Or who controls hearing and sight?﴾ That is: Or who is it that controls your hearing and your sight, with which you hear, to increase their strength or to take them from you, making you deaf, and your sight, with which you see, to illuminate and brighten it for you, or to take away its light, making you blind, unable to see? ﴿And who brings forth the living from the dead﴾, meaning: and who brings forth the living thing from the dead? ﴿And brings forth the dead from the living﴾, meaning: and brings forth the dead thing from the living?

* *

We have already mentioned the disagreement of those who differ among the people of interpretation, and the correct view in this matter according to us, with the proofs that indicate its soundness, in "Surat Al 'Imran," in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [[See what preceded: 6: 304 - 312.]]

* *

﴿And who manages the affair?﴾ And say to them: Who manages the affair of the heaven and the earth and whatever is in them, and your affair, and the affair of creation? [[See the explanation of "managing the affair" in what preceded, pp. 18, 19.]] ﴿They will say, "Allah."﴾ His exalted praise says: They will answer you by saying: The One who does all of that is Allah. ﴿So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ That is: Do you not fear the punishment of Allah for your polytheism and your claim of a lord other than the One who has this attribute, and your worship alongside Him of one who does not provide for you anything, nor controls for you any harm or benefit, nor does any act?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 32:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So that is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. Then what is there after the truth except error? So how are you turned away?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His creatures: O people, this One who does these deeds, who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, who owns hearing and sight, who brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, and who manages the affair, = ﴿Allah is your Lord, the Truth,﴾ without any doubt = ﴿Then what is there after the truth except error?﴾ He means: what is there other than the truth except error, which is deviation from the right path? [[See the explanation of "ḍalāl" (error) in the earlier lexical indexes, under (ḍ-l-l).]]

He means: since the truth is this, then your claiming that other than Him is a god and a lord is error and departure from the truth, without doubt. = ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾ He means: in what direction are you turned away from guidance and truth, and what other path do you take, while you yourselves acknowledge that what you are turned away from is the truth? [[See the explanation of "ṣarf" (turning away) in the earlier volumes, vol. 14, p. 582, note 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 33:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus has the word of your Lord been justified against those who defiantly disobeyed, that they will not believe﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Just as these polytheists have been turned away from the truth toward error, ﴿thus has the word of your Lord been justified﴾, meaning: His decree and judgment concerning what was previously in His knowledge has become binding upon them, ﴿against those who defiantly disobeyed﴾, meaning they departed from the obedience of their Lord into His disobedience and disbelieved in Him [[See the explanation of "fisq" (defiant disobedience) in the earlier word indices of the language section (fasaqa).]], ﴿that they will not believe﴾, meaning: they will not affirm the oneness of God nor the prophethood of His Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?" Say: "It is Allah who originates creation and then repeats it. So how are you turned away?"﴾ (10:34)

Abu Ja'far said: God, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿"Is there any of your partners"﴾, meaning of the gods and idols, ﴿"who originates creation and then repeats it"﴾, meaning: who brings into being a thing from no prior origin, creating it anew, ﴿and then repeats it﴾, meaning: then causes it to perish after bringing it into being, and then restores it as it was before it perished. For they are not able to claim that for them. In this there is a decisive proof and a clear indication that they, in their claim that these are lords and are associates of Allah in worship, are liars and fabricators.

So say to them then, O Muhammad: Allah originates creation, bringing it into being from nothing and creating it from no origin, then He causes it to perish when He wills, then He restores it when He desires, as it was before perishing. ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾ meaning: In what direction are you diverted and turned away from the right course and the path of guidance?

[[See the explanation of "al-Afk" (turning away, perversion) in what has preceded: 10:486 / 11:554 / 14:208.]] As it was narrated:

17659: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾, he said: "How are you diverted?"

* *

We have already explained the disagreement of those who differ regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿How are you turned away?﴾, and the correct view on that in our opinion, with its evidences, is in "Surat al-An'am." [[See what has preceded, 11:554, and his statement that he mentioned it in Surat al-An'am. These are from Abu Ja'far's own words, for he did not clarify the meaning of "al-Afk" except in Surat al-Ma'idah (10:485, 468). He never mentioned the disagreement of those who differ in its interpretation. I fear this text indicates that Abu Ja'far had spread out the parts of his tafsir widely, so that he sometimes forgot the place where he had explained a matter; indeed, this may also indicate that he had begun the tafsir at length, as is mentioned in his biography, and then abridged it to this degree. It also indicates, if what I have said is correct, that he had fully prepared the material of his book and then made major revisions in writing his tafsir, so he did not retain everything he had prepared for it. And Allah knows best.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 35:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Is there any among your partners who guides to the truth?﴾ Say: ﴿Allah guides to the truth.﴾ ﴿Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ (35)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: ﴿Is there any among your partners﴾ that you invoke besides Allah, meaning their gods and idols, ﴿who guides to the truth﴾? That is, who guides one who is astray from his straying to the straight path, and sets right one who deviates from guidance to the clear, upright way? For they cannot claim that their gods and idols guide the lost or direct the deviant. Indeed, if they claimed that for them, observation would refute them, and direct testing with their own eyes would make clear their inability to do so. So when they say "No" and acknowledge that, then say to them: ﴿Allah guides the one who is astray from guidance to the truth.﴾ ﴿Is He who guides﴾, O people, the one who leads the astray to the truth, and the one who deviates from right direction to right direction, ﴿more worthy to be followed﴾ in what He calls to? ﴿Or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided?﴾

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina recited: ﴿أَمَّنْ لا يَهْدِّي﴾ with the hā' unvocalized (sukūn) and the dāl doubled (shaddah), thereby combining two unvocalized letters [[See what he said about the similarity of this reading earlier, 9: 362.]]. It seems that what led them to this is that they took the original form of the word to be: "or who does not find guidance" (أم من لا يهتدي), and they found it in the script of the Qur'an differing from what they recited. The tā' was dropped when it was assimilated into the dāl, so they kept the hā' unvocalized as it originally was, and doubled the dāl to accommodate the assimilation of the tā', so the sukūn of the hā' and the dāl came together. They did the same with His words: ﴿And We said to them: Do not transgress in the Sabbath﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 154] [[See what has preceded regarding this reading, 9: 362.]], and with His words: ﴿they are disputing﴾ [Surah Ya-Sin: 49] [[See what will follow regarding this reading, 23: 11 (Bulaq edition).]].

* *

Some readers of Mecca, Syria and Basra recited it: ﴿يَهَدِّي﴾ with a fatḥah on the hā' and a doubled dāl. They intended what the Medinans intended from the word, except that they moved the vowel of the tā' of "yahtadī" onto the unvocalized hā', so it took its vowel, and they assimilated the tā' into the dāl and doubled it.

* *

Some readers of Kufa recited it: ﴿يَهِدِّي﴾ with a fatḥah on the yā', a kasrah on the hā', and a doubled dāl, close to what the Medinans intended, except that he gave the hā' a kasrah because of the kasrah of the dāl of "yahtadī", finding a fatḥah followed by a kasrah in a single letter too heavy.

* *

Then the majority of the Kufan readers recited: ﴿أَمْ مَنْ لا يَهْدِي﴾ with the hā' unvocalized and the dāl lightened (without shaddah). They said: the Arabs say "hadaytu" meaning "ihtadaytu" (I was guided), so the meaning of His words ﴿or who does not find guidance﴾ is: or who does not become guided unless he is guided.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct recitation in this matter is the recitation of the one who recites: ﴿أَمْ مَنْ لا يَهَدِّي﴾ with a fatḥah on the hā' and a doubled dāl, because of the reason we have described for the one who recites it thus, and because no one knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs denies its soundness, though among them is one who rejects it. The most worthy speech to be recited is in the most eloquent of the dialects in which the speech of Allah was revealed.

* *

The interpretation of the statement, therefore, is: Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who is not guided to anything unless he is guided?

* *

Some of the interpreters claimed that the meaning of this is: or he who cannot move from his place unless he is moved.

* *

Mujahid used to say concerning its interpretation:

17660- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided﴾, he said: the idols. Allah guides from among them and from others whom He wills, to whom He wills.

17661- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid concerning His words: ﴿Or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided﴾, he said: the idol.

* *

As for His words: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾, do you not know that he who guides to the truth is more worthy to be followed than he who finds no guidance to anything unless another guide guides him to it, so that you abandon following and worshipping one who finds no guidance to anything, and follow Him who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea, and make your worship sincerely for Him, singling Him out with it alone, apart from what you associate with Him of your gods and idols?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 36:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ (10:36)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And most of these polytheists follow nothing but conjecture, meaning: nothing but that of which they have no knowledge of its reality and soundness, rather they are in doubt and suspicion about it [[See the explanation of "conjecture" (zann) in the preceding lexical indices, under (ẓ-n-n).]] = ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾, meaning: indeed, doubt avails nothing against certainty, nor does it stand in its place in anything, nor is it of benefit where certainty is needed [[See the explanation of "avail" (aghnā) in the preceding volume, 14:179, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾. He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, Allah has knowledge of what these polytheists do, of their following conjecture and their denial of the certain truth, and He is lying in wait for them, where their conjecture will avail them nothing against Allah. [[See the explanation of "Knowing" (ʿalīm) in the preceding lexical indices, under (ʿ-l-m).]]

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, Words: ﴿And it is not [possible] for this Qur'an that it be fabricated apart from Allah, but [it is] a confirmation of what is before it and a detailed explanation of the Book, there is no doubt in it, [it is] from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [10:37]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His, the exalted's, remembrance says: It is not fitting for this Qur'an to be fabricated apart from Allah, meaning: it is not fitting that anyone invent it from other than Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-iftira'" (fabrication) in the earlier lexical indexes under (f-r-y).

= And the explanation of "ma kana" (it is not) earlier: 7:353 / 14:509-514, 561, 565.]] This is similar to His words: ﴿And it is not [fitting] for a Prophet that he should defraud (yughalla)﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 161], [[This is the reading of the people of Madina and Kufa, with a damma on the ba' and a fatha on the 'ayn, in the passive voice, and it differs from our reading in our copy of the Qur'an. Its explanation, the wording of the scholars on it, and the disagreement of those who differ over it have been mentioned earlier: 7:353, 354. See also Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:464.]] meaning: it is not fitting for a Prophet that his companions defraud him.

This is only a report from Allah, may His praise be mentioned, that this Qur'an is from Him, sent down to Muhammad, His servant, and a refutation from Him of the polytheists who said: "It is poetry and soothsaying," and those who said: "Muhammad is only taught it by Yahnas the Roman." [[In the printed edition: "Ya'ish al-Rumi," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, and that alteration is not good.]]

His, the exalted's, remembrance says to them: This Qur'an would not be invented by anyone from other than Allah, because no one among the creation is able to do that. ﴿But a confirmation of what is before it﴾, meaning: His, the exalted's, remembrance says: rather it is from Allah, He sent it down confirming what is before it, that is, what came before it of the books sent down to the prophets of Allah, such as the Torah and the Gospel and other books of Allah which He sent down to His prophets. ﴿And a detailed explanation of the Book﴾, He says: and a clarification of the Book which Allah wrote for the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, and His obligations which He imposed on them from His earlier knowledge. He says: ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾, without doubt that it is a confirmation of what is before it of the Book and a detailed explanation of the Book, from the Lord of the worlds, not a fabrication from other than Him nor an invention. [[See the explanation of "tafsil" (detailed explanation) earlier, p. 57, note 1, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "rayb" (doubt) earlier: 14:459, note 1, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-'alamin" (the worlds) earlier: 13:84, note 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 38:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it." Say, "Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides God, if you should be truthful."﴾ (38)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Or do these polytheists say: Muhammad fabricated this Qur'an from himself, invented it and forged it? Say, O Muhammad, to them: If it is as you claim, that I invented it and fabricated it, then you are like me among the Arabs, and my tongue is like your tongue, and my speech [is like your speech], [[In the manuscript: "and my tongue is like your tongue, and my speech then bring"; I dropped from the speech what I placed between the brackets, based on inference. As for the printed edition, it made it: "and my tongue and my speech are like your tongue," and erred.]] so bring a surah like this Qur'an.

* *

The pronoun in His saying "mithlihi" (like it) refers to the Qur'an.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of that is: Say, "Then bring a surah like its surah," then "surah" was omitted and the word "mithl" (like) was attributed to what "surah" had been attributed to, as in His saying: ﴿And ask the town﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 82], meaning: and ask the people of the town.

* *

Some of them rejected this from his statement, and claimed that its meaning is: Then bring a Qur'an like this Qur'an.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that "surah" is only a surah of the Qur'an, and it is Qur'an, even if it is not the whole Qur'an. So it was said to them: ﴿Then bring a surah like it﴾, and it was not said "like her," because the pronoun was brought in agreement with the meaning, meaning the meaning of "surah", not its wording, for if it had been brought in agreement with its wording it would have been said "then bring a surah like her."

* *

= ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides God﴾: He says: and call upon, O polytheists, to bring a surah like it, whoever among your helpers and partners you are able to call upon for that; ﴿besides God﴾, that is: from other than God. So unite upon that and strive, for you will never be able to bring a surah like it, ever.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿if you should be truthful﴾, He says: if you are truthful in claiming that Muhammad fabricated it, then bring a surah like it from all those who help you to bring it. If you do not do that, then there is no doubt that you are liars in your claim that Muhammad fabricated it, for Muhammad cannot be anything other than a human like you. So when all of creation is unable to bring a surah like it, the single one among them is even more unable to bring all of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 39:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, they denied that which they had not encompassed in knowledge, and its interpretation had not yet come to them. Likewise denied those before them. So look how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ (39)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, says: It is not your denial, O Muhammad, that is the matter with these polytheists; rather, it is they who deny that which they have not encompassed in knowledge of what Allah has sent down to you in this Qur'an [see the explanation of "ihata" (encompassing) earlier, p. 51, note 3, and the references there], namely its threat of punishment for their disbelief in their Lord. ﴿And its interpretation had not yet come to them﴾, meaning: the clarification of what that threat, which Allah has warned them of in this Qur'an, will lead to has not yet come to them [see the explanation of "ta'wil" (interpretation/outcome) earlier, vol. 12, p. 478, note 1, and the references there]. ﴿Likewise denied those before them﴾: Exalted is He says: just as these polytheists, O Muhammad, denied the warning of Allah, so too did the nations that passed before them deny Allah's warning to them, because of their denial of their messengers and their disbelief in their Lord. ﴿So look how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾: Exalted is He says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So look, O Muhammad, at how the outcome was for those who disbelieved in Allah. Did We not destroy some of them with the quake, some with the sinking into the earth, and some with drowning? [see the explanation of "'aqibah" (end/outcome) earlier, vol. 13, p. 43, note 1, and the references there]. That is to say: the outcome of these who deny you and reject My signs from your people's disbelievers will be like the outcome of those before them from the disbelieving nations, if they do not turn back from their disbelief and hasten to repentance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verses 40–41:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And among your people, O Muhammad, among the Quraysh, are those who will believe in it," meaning: those who will affirm the Qur'an and acknowledge that it is from God. ﴿And among them are those who do not believe in it﴾ ever; meaning: and among them are those who will never affirm it or acknowledge it. ﴿And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters﴾ means: God is most knowing of those among them who deny it, who will never affirm it, from every person, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is beyond His punishment. As for those among them for whom I have decreed that they will believe in it, I will indeed turn to them in forgiveness. [[See the explanation of "corruption" (al-fasad) above, 14:86, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my work, and for you is your work. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And if these polytheists deny you, O Muhammad, and reject what you have brought them from your Lord, then say to them: 'O people, for me is my religion and my work, and for you is your religion and your work. Your work does not harm me, and my work does not harm you, and each worker is only recompensed for his work.'" ﴿You are free of what I do﴾, meaning: you will not be held accountable for its wrongdoing. ﴿And I am free of what you do﴾, meaning: I will not be held accountable for the wrongdoing of your deeds. [[See the explanation of "bari'" (free of, innocent) above, 14:12, footnote 1, and the references there.]] This is like His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Say: "O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshipers of what I worship"﴾ [Surah al-Kafirun: 1–3].

* *

It has been said: this verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by jihad and the command to fight.

Mention of those who said this:

17662 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying, ﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my work, and for you is your work"﴾, the verse: He commanded him with this, then abrogated it and commanded him to fight them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 42:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you. Can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And among these polytheists are those who listen to your speech — ﴿Can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?﴾ That is: Can you create hearing for them, when they have no hearing by which they understand — or do I?

This is only an announcement from God to His servants that guidance to belief in Him is in His hand, not in the hand of anyone other than Him. He says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Just as you cannot make hear, O Muhammad, one whom He has deprived of hearing, so too you cannot make understand My command and My prohibition a heart whom He has deprived of the understanding of that, because I have sealed upon it that it will not believe.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verses 43–44:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among them are those who look at you. Then will you guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And among these polytheists, the polytheists of your people, are those who look at you, O Muhammad, and see your signs and your proofs for your prophethood, but God has withdrawn from him success (tawfiq), so he is not guided, and you cannot guide him, just as you cannot give sight to a blind man so that he might be guided by it. ﴿Then will you guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾ He means: Will you, O Muhammad, give sight to those who look at you and at your proofs and arguments, so that they are granted the ability to believe in you, even though they are blind and would be guided by it and see? Just as you are not able to do that, and neither is anyone else able to do it, and no one is able to do it except Me, so likewise you cannot show them the path of rectitude, neither you nor anyone other than Me, because that is in My hand and returns to Me.

This is from God, exalted is His remembrance, as a consolation to His Prophet ﷺ regarding a group of his people who disbelieved in him, turned away from him, and denied him, and as a condolence for him concerning them, and a command to lower his hope of their turning back in repentance to belief in God.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, God does not wrong people at all, but it is people who wrong themselves.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed God does not do to His creatures what they do not deserve from Him; He punishes them only for their disobedience to Him, and He torments them only for their disbelief in Him. ﴿But it is people﴾, he says: rather, it is people who wrong themselves, by committing what brings upon themselves the anger and wrath of God.

This is only an announcement from God, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and to those who believe in him, that He has not taken away the belief of those whom He, majestic is His praise, informed us would not believe, as a starting point from Him without a prior crime committed by them; and an announcement that He only deprived them of that because they deserved to be deprived of it, due to sins they had earned, so the word of their Lord was fulfilled against them, and He sealed their hearts.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 45:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them, [it will be] as if they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of the day, recognizing one another. Those will have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not [rightly] guided.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And [mention] the Day We will gather these polytheists and assemble them at the place of reckoning. [See the explanation of "al-hashr" (gathering) earlier, p. 77, footnote 5, and the references there.] It will be as if they had not remained before that except an hour of the day, recognizing one another among themselves [see the explanation of "al-labth" (remaining) earlier, p. 41], then the recognition will cease and that hour will have passed. Allah says: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not [rightly] guided.﴾ Those who denied the reward and punishment of Allah and their share of good have been defrauded and have perished. [See the explanation of "al-khusran" (loss) earlier, vol. 14, p. 344, footnote 2, and the references there.] ﴿And they were not [rightly] guided﴾ means: and they were not granted success in reaching right guidance by what they did of denying the meeting with Allah, because that brought upon them what they had no power to bear of the punishment of Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 46:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), to Us is their return; then Allah is Witness over what they do﴾ (10:46).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Whether We show you, O Muhammad, during your lifetime, some of the punishment with which We threaten these polytheists of your people" — ﴿or We take you (in death)﴾ before We show you that among them — ﴿to Us is their return﴾, meaning: their destination in every case is to Us, and their final turning-place (see the explanation of "tawaffi" (taking in death) above, vol. 14, pp. 15, footnote 4, and the references there; and the explanation of "marji'" (return) above, p. 54, footnote 3, and the references there) — ﴿then Allah is Witness over what they do﴾. He, may His praise be exalted, says: "Then I am Witness over their deeds which they used to do in this world, and I know them, nothing of them being hidden from Me, and I will requite them for them when they come to Me and return to Me, with the recompense they deserve," (see the explanation of "shahid" (witness) above in the lexical indices, under the root sh-h-d), as:

17663 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾, of the punishment, during your lifetime — ﴿or We take you (in death)﴾, before that — ﴿to Us is their return﴾.

17664 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17665 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 10, verses 47–48:

The explanation of His saying, ﴿And for every nation there is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, judgment will be made between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ (10:47)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, may He be remembered, means: "And for every nation that passed before you, O people, there was a messenger whom I sent to them, just as I sent Muhammad to you, calling those to whom I sent them to the religion of God and to obeying Him." ﴿So when their messenger comes﴾ means: in the Hereafter, as related:

17666 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And for every nation there is a messenger. So when their messenger comes﴾: he said, "It is the Day of Resurrection."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿judgment will be made between them with justice﴾, it means: judgment will then be made between them with justice [[See the explanation of "al-qist" (justice) above, p. 21, note 4, and the references there.]]. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ means: they will not be deprived of any of the reward of their deeds; rather, the one who does good will be rewarded for his good. As for the one among the people of faith who does evil, God will either punish him or pardon him. The disbeliever will abide forever in the Fire. This is God's judgment between them with justice, and it is without doubt justice, not injustice.

17667 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿judgment will be made between them with justice﴾: he said, "With justice."

* *

The explanation of His saying, ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ (10:48)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, may He be remembered, is addressed to His Prophet ﷺ: "And these polytheists of your people say, O Muhammad, ﴿When is this promise﴾ which you promise us will come from God?" That refers to the establishment of the Hour. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ means: you and those who follow you, in what you threaten us with of that.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Say: I possess not for myself any harm or benefit, except what Allah wills. For every nation is a term; when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾ (10:49)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says, "Say" (O Muhammad) to those who hasten you toward the threat of Allah, who say to you, "When will this promise that you make come to us, if you are truthful?" ﴿I possess not for myself﴾ (O people), meaning: I have no power over harm or benefit for myself in this world or in the religion [[See the explanation of "possession" (al-mulk) above, 13:302, footnote 1, and the references there.]] ﴿except what Allah wills﴾, that I should possess it, so that I bring it to myself by His permission.

The Exalted says to His Prophet ﷺ: Say to them: since I have no power over that except by His permission, then I am incapable and powerless in regard to attaining knowledge of the unseen and knowing when the Hour will be established, except by His will and His permission to me in that. ﴿For every nation is a term﴾, meaning: for every people there is an appointed time for the expiry of their duration and term; so when the time of the expiry of their term and the end of their lifespans comes [[See the explanation of "nation" (ummah) above in the lexical indexes under (a-m-m), and the explanation of "term" (ajal) above, p. 33, footnote 3, and the references there.]]

﴿they cannot delay it an hour﴾ from it, so that they are granted respite or deferred, ﴿nor can they advance it﴾ before that, because Allah has decreed that this shall not come forward before the appointed time which He has measured and decreed. [[See the explanation of "to delay" (ista'khara) and "to advance" (istaqdama) above, 12:404, 405.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 50–51:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if His punishment comes to you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals seek to hasten?"﴾ (50)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists of your people: "Have you considered if the punishment of God comes to you by night (bayatan), meaning at night or by day," [[See the explanation of "bayat" (overnight attack) above, 12:299, note 4, and the references there.]]

and the Hour arrives and the Resurrection takes place, can you then ward off that from yourselves? God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: What is it that the criminals who disbelieved in God seek to hasten of the descent of the punishment, [[See the explanation of "istih'jal" (hastening) above, p. 33.]] those who are the ones who will roast in its heat and no others, and then they will not be able to ward it off from themselves?

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then, when it has come to pass, will you believe in it? Now? And you used to seek to hasten it!﴾ (51)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Then, when the punishment of God has befallen you, O polytheists, "will you believe in it?", meaning: will you affirm it at a time when affirmation will not benefit you, and it will be said to you at that moment: "Do you now affirm it, when before now you used to seek to hasten it, and you were denying its descent?" "Taste now what you used to deny."

* *

As for the meaning of His saying ﴿thumma﴾ (then/there) in this place, it means: "then there" (ahnalika), and this "thumma" here is not the one that comes in the sense of conjunction (ataf). [[See the explanation of "thumma" above, 2:535, which includes the explanation of "thumma" with a fatha, meaning "there." Al-Tabari said in his tafsir 8:351: "It is said that 'thumma' here means 'thumma' with a fatha on the ta', making it an adverb of place, and the meaning is 'ahnalika,' which is the view of al-Tabari." Abu Hayyan said in his tafsir 5:167: "Al-Tabari said regarding His saying, 'athumma,' with a damma on the tha', that its meaning is 'ahnalika,' and that this 'thumma' here is not the one that comes in the sense of conjunction, and what al-Tabari said is a claim."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 50–51:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if His punishment comes to you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals seek to hasten?"﴾ (50)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists of your people: "Have you considered if the punishment of God comes to you by night (bayatan), meaning at night or by day," [[See the explanation of "bayat" (overnight attack) above, 12:299, note 4, and the references there.]]

and the Hour arrives and the Resurrection takes place, can you then ward off that from yourselves? God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: What is it that the criminals who disbelieved in God seek to hasten of the descent of the punishment, [[See the explanation of "istih'jal" (hastening) above, p. 33.]] those who are the ones who will roast in its heat and no others, and then they will not be able to ward it off from themselves?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verses 52–53:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Then it will be said to those who did wrong, "Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?"﴾ (10:52)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Then it will be said to those who did wrong﴾ — to themselves, by their disbelief in Allah — ﴿"Taste the punishment of eternity"﴾ — swallow the punishment of Allah, which is lasting for you forever, which has no end and no cessation. [[See the explanation of "dhawq" (tasting) earlier, p. 49, note 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "khuld" (eternity) earlier in the language indexes (kh-l-d).]] ﴿"Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?"﴾ — he says: it will be said to them: "Consider whether you are being recompensed," i.e., whether you are being rewarded. ﴿Except for what you used to earn﴾ — he says: except for what you used to do in your life before your death of the disobediences to Allah. [[See the explanation of "jaza'" (recompense) earlier in the language indexes (j-z-y), and (k-s-b).]]

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you will not escape."﴾ (10:53)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And these polytheists from your people, O Muhammad, ask you for information [[See the explanation of "naba'" (news/tidings) earlier, p. 54, note 4, and the references there.]]

and say to you: Is what you say true, and what you threaten us with of the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter as a recompense for what we used to earn of disobedience to Allah in this world? Say to them, O Muhammad: "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true," without any doubt about it, and you will not be able to escape Allah if He wills that for you, by fleeing or by refusing, but rather you are in His grasp, His authority and His dominion, when He wills to do that to you. So fear Allah regarding your own souls. [[See the explanation of "i'jaz" (rendering incapable/escaping) earlier, vol. 14, p. 131, note 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 54–55:

The interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And if every soul that had wronged had everything on earth, it would surely offer it as ransom. And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment. And it will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ (10:54).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And if every soul that disbelieved in God—and "wronged" it (ẓalamat), in this place, means worshipping other than the One who deserves to be worshipped, and abandoning obedience to the One whose obedience is obligatory upon it [[In the printed edition: "min yastahiqqu ʿibādah", which differs from what is in the manuscript.]]—had whatever is on the earth, of little or much, ﴿it would surely offer it as ransom﴾, meaning: it would ransom itself with all of that from the punishment of God when it witnessed it [[See the explanation of "al-iftidāʾ" (ransoming) in the earlier lexical indexes under (fdy).]]. As for His saying: ﴿And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment﴾, it means: the leaders of these polytheists concealed the regret from their followers and lowly ones when they saw the punishment of God encompassing them and became certain that it would befall them. ﴿And it will be judged between them with justice﴾, meaning: God will judge that Day between the followers and their leaders with justice [[See the explanation of "al-qisṭ" above, p. 99, note 1, and the references there.]]. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: this is because He does not punish any of them except for his own misdeed, nor does He hold anyone accountable for another's sin, and He does not punish anyone except one to whom He has given excuse in the world, warned, and followed up the proofs against him.

* *

The interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Unquestionably, the promise of God is true, but most of them do not know﴾ (10:55).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, great is His remembrance, says: Unquestionably, everything that is in the heavens and everything on the earth, of any thing, belongs to God in ownership; nothing in it belongs to anyone besides Him. He means: on that Day, this disbeliever in God has no thing that he owns with which he could ransom himself from the punishment of his Lord; all things belong only to the One to whom his punishment is due. Even if the things that are on the earth were his, and he ransomed himself with them, it would not be accepted from him as a substitute for his punishment, so as to turn the punishment away from him by them. How much more so when he has nothing to ransom himself with from it, and the punishment of God has become binding upon him? God, whose praise is exalted, says: ﴿Unquestionably, the promise of God is true﴾, meaning: His punishment, which He threatened these polytheists for their disbelief, is true, so there is no harm for them that they do not hasten it, for it will certainly befall them without doubt. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, meaning: but most of these polytheists do not know the reality of its befalling them, and so, because of their ignorance of it, they are deniers.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned﴾ (56)

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, means: Indeed Allah is the One who gives life and causes death. Nothing hinders Him from doing what He wills, whether bringing these polytheists back to life when He wills to revive them after their death, or causing them to die when He wills that. And they will return to Him after their death, so they will witness what they used to deny of Allah's threat and punishment.

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a cure for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers﴾ (57)

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says to His creation: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord﴾, meaning: a reminder that recalls to you Allah's punishment and warns you of His threat [[See the explanation of "al-mawi'ah" (admonition) above, 8:528, footnote 3, and the references there.]]. ﴿From your Lord﴾ means: from the presence of your Lord. Muhammad (ﷺ) did not fabricate it, and no one invented it, so that you might say: "We cannot be sure it is not without any truth." Rather, by this He, the Majestic and Praised, means the Qur'an, which is the admonition from Allah.

As for His words ﴿and a cure for what is in the breasts﴾, it means: a remedy for the ignorance that is in the breasts, by which Allah cures the ignorance of the ignorant, healing their disease through it, and by it guides whomever of His creation He wills to guide. ﴿And guidance﴾ means: it is an explanation of Allah's lawful and unlawful, and an indication of obedience to Him and disobedience to Him. ﴿And mercy﴾: He shows mercy through it to whomever of His creation He wills, rescuing him through it from error to guidance and delivering him through it from destruction and perdition. The Blessed and Exalted made it a mercy for those who believe in it and not for those who disbelieve in it, because whoever disbelieves in it, blindness is upon him, and in the Hereafter his recompense for disbelieving in it is eternal abiding in the Blaze.
