Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 58:

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these deniers of you and of what was sent down to you from your Lord [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "to these polytheists who associate others with you," which is utterly corrupt. I judged the correct reading to be what I have recorded.]], ﴿In the bounty of Allah﴾, O people, which He has bestowed upon you, and that is Islam, so He made it clear to you and invited you to it; ﴿and in His mercy﴾, by which He showed you mercy, sending it down to you, so He taught you what you did not know of His Book, and made you see through it the landmarks of your religion; and that is the Qur'an. ﴿In that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾: that is, Islam, to which He invited them, and the Qur'an, which He sent down to them, are better than what they accumulate of the trash of this world, its wealth and its treasures.

* *

Some people of ta'wil (interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Among those who said that:

17668. Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi told me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, regarding His words: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice﴾, he said: "The bounty of Allah" is the Qur'an, and "His mercy" is that He made you among its people. [[The report 17668: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi is a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned earlier under no. 10258, and we have not found a biography of him. In the printed edition here it reads "ibn al-Husayn," which is an error; a similar error occurred in our marginal note on the same report, vol. 9, p. 98, note 1.]]

17669. Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i told me, saying: Fudayl narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf: ﴿In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice﴾, he said: "By Islam, which guided you, and by the Qur'an, which taught you."

17670. Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf: ﴿In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy﴾, he said: "By Islam and the Qur'an"; ﴿in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾, from gold and silver.

17671. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, regarding His words: ﴿In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy﴾, he said: "The bounty of Allah" is Islam, and "His mercy" is the Qur'an.

17672. Ali ibn Sahl told me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, regarding His words: ﴿In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy﴾, he said: Islam and the Qur'an.

17673. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Nu'aym and Qabisa narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, the like of it.

17674. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal, the like of it.

17675. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice﴾; as for His bounty, it is Islam, and as for His mercy, it is the Qur'an.

17676. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy﴾, he said: His bounty is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an.

17677. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy﴾, he said: the Qur'an.

17678. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and in His mercy﴾, he said: the Qur'an.

17679. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His words: ﴿it is better than what they accumulate﴾, he said: "The wealth and other things."

17680. Ali ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih told me, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy﴾, he says: His bounty is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an.

17681. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice﴾, he said: "With the Book of Allah and with Islam"; ﴿it is better than what they accumulate﴾.

* *

Others said: Rather, "the bounty" is the Qur'an, and "the mercy" is Islam.

Among those who said that:

17682. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾, he said: "The bounty of Allah" is the Qur'an, and "His mercy" is that He made them among the people of the Qur'an.

17683. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "The bounty of Allah" is the Qur'an, and "His mercy" is Islam.

17684. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy﴾, he said: "The bounty of Allah" is the Qur'an, and "His mercy" is Islam.

17685. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice﴾: My father used to say: His bounty is the Qur'an, and His mercy is Islam.

* *

The readers differed over the recitation of His words: ﴿in that let them rejoice﴾.

The majority of the readers of the major cities recited it as ﴿فَلْيَفْرَحُوا﴾ with the yā' (third person masculine plural), and ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾ also with the yā', in accordance with the interpretation we have adopted, namely that it is a report about the people of polytheism (shirk) in Allah. The meaning is: by Islam and the Qur'an to which He invited them, let these polytheists rejoice, not by the wealth they accumulate, for Islam and the Qur'an are better than the wealth they accumulate. Likewise:

17686. It was related to me from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata, from Harun, from Abu al-Tayyah: ﴿in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾, meaning the disbelievers.

* *

It is reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b concerning this what follows:

17687. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Aslam al-Minqari, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: that he used to recite: ﴿فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْتَفْرَحُوا هُوَ خُيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾, with the tā' (second person).

17688. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from al-Ajlah, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, the like of that.

* *

Al-Hasan al-Basri used to say likewise, except that it is reported from him that he recited ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾ with the yā'; the first (فَلْتَفْرَحُوا, i.e., the verb) in the mode of address, and the second in the mode of report about an absent party.

* *

Abu Ja'far the reciter (al-Qari') used to recite it, as reported from him, in a manner close to the recitation of Ubayy, with tā' throughout.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter is what the readers of the major cities hold, reciting both words with the yā': ﴿فَلْيَفْرَحُوا هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾, for two reasons:

The first: the consensus of the authoritative readers (hujjah) upon it.

The second: its soundness in Arabic. The Arabs hardly ever command the addressee with the lam and the tā'; rather, they command by saying: "Do" (افعل) and "Do not" (لا تفعل).

Furthermore, I know of no one among the grammarians of Arabic who does not consider the command to the addressee with the lam to be inferior, regarding it as a dispreferred dialect, except al-Farra', for he used to claim that the lam in the imperative [is the form it was created for], whether one addresses the person or not, except that the Arabs dropped the lam from the verb of the commanded addressee because the imperative is very frequent in their speech especially, just as they dropped the tā' from the verb. He said: "You know that the jussive and the accusative particles only come upon a verb that begins with yā', tā', nūn, or alif. When the tā' was dropped, the lam was dropped too, and an alif was introduced in your saying ﴿اضرب﴾ "strike" and ﴿افرح﴾ "rejoice," because the initial letter is sukūn (vowelless), so it was not possible to begin with a vowelless letter; so they inserted a light alif through which the beginning is made," just as He said: ﴿ادَّارَكُوا﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 38] [[In the printed edition: "idarakatum." In the manuscript: "qalu: idaraku wa-ithaqaltum." I have adopted al-Farra's text.]] and ﴿اثَّاقَلْتُمْ﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 38]. [[This is all the text of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, vol. 1, p. 469.]]

But this argument with which al-Farra' justified it is against him, not for him. For if the Arabs dropped the lam in addressing the second person and left it out, it is not permissible for anyone else, while speaking their language, to introduce into it what is not part of it, so long as he speaks in their dialect. If he does so, he has gone outside their language, while the Book of Allah, which He sent down to Muhammad in their tongue [[In the printed edition: "the speech of Allah." The manuscript reading is the better one.]], may only be recited in the most eloquent of their speech. Even if some of that is known from the dialect of some of them, how much more so is it when it is not known from the dialect of any living tribe or clan among them? It is merely an assertion by which no authoritative proof (hujjah) or soundness is established. [[In the printed edition: "la thubut bihi wa-la hujjah." In the manuscript: "la tathbutu bihi wa-la sihhah." I added "hujjah" between the brackets, as the context requires it.]]

**The explanation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made of it lawful and unlawful?" Say: "Has God permitted you, or do you invent [lies] against God?"﴾ (10:59)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: ﴿Have you considered﴾, O people, ﴿what God has sent down to you of provision﴾, meaning: what God has created for you of provision and bestowed upon you, which is what you feed on of foods. ﴿And you made of it lawful and unlawful﴾, meaning: you made lawful for yourselves some of it and prohibited for yourselves some of it. This is like their prohibition of the crops and livestock that they used to dedicate to their idols, as God described them when He said: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has produced of crops and livestock, and they say, "This is for God," by their claim, and "This is for our partners"﴾ [Al-An'am: 136].

Among the livestock were those that they prohibited through *al-tabhir* (slitting the ear) and *al-tasyib* (letting loose), and similar things, which we have mentioned earlier in this book of ours. [[See what has preceded, 11:116–134.]]

God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿Has God permitted you﴾ to prohibit what you have prohibited of it? ﴿Or do you invent against God﴾, meaning: do you speak falsehood and lie? [[See the explanation of "*al-iftira'*" (invention) in the earlier linguistic indexes under the root (f-r-y).]]

* *

Those who engage in *ta'wil* (interpretation) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

**Those who said this:**

17689- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The people of the Jahiliyya used to prohibit things that God had made lawful, of garments and other things, and this is God's saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made of it lawful and unlawful﴾, and this is it. Then God, the Exalted, sent down: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants?﴾ [Al-A'raf: 32], to the end of the verse.

17690- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made...﴾ to His saying: ﴿...or do you invent against God?﴾ He said: They are the people of polytheism.

17691- Al-Qasim related to me, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And you made of it lawful and unlawful﴾, he said: The crops and the livestock. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: *al-bahair* and *al-sayyib*.

17692- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Huthayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And you made of it lawful and unlawful﴾, he said: concerning the *bahira* and the *sa'iba*.

17693- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made of it lawful and unlawful﴾, the verse, he says: Every provision of which I did not prohibit, you prohibited for yourselves, of your women, your wealth, and your children. ﴿Has God permitted you in what you have prohibited of that, or do you invent against God?﴾

17694- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made of it lawful and unlawful﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿or do you invent against God?﴾ And he recited: ﴿And they say, "What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males, and forbidden to our wives"﴾ [Al-An'am: 139], and he recited: ﴿And they say, "These are livestock and crops, forbidden"...﴾ until he reached: ﴿they do not mention the name of God over them﴾ [Al-An'am: 138]. Then he said: This is His saying: He gave them provision, so they made of it lawful and unlawful, and prohibited some of it and made lawful some of it.

And he recited: ﴿Eight mates: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful. Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you?﴾ — meaning: which of these two has He prohibited to these people who say it, and made lawful to those — to the end of the verses [Al-An'am: 143–144].

17695- It was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made of it lawful and unlawful﴾, that it is what God mentioned: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has produced of crops and livestock﴾, to His saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾ [Al-An'am: 136].

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And what will those think who fabricate lies against Allah on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of them are not grateful.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: What do those think who invent lies about Allah, attributing to Him the prohibition of provisions and sustenance that He has not prohibited for them, the means of nourishment that Allah made for them, that Allah will do with them on the Day of Resurrection because of their lying and fabrication against Him? Do they suppose that He will overlook them and forgive them? No indeed; rather He will roast them in the Blaze, abiding therein forever. ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, meaning: Indeed, Allah is full of favor toward His creation by withholding from the one who fabricates lies against Him the immediate punishment in this world, and by granting him respite until he arrives at it on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾, meaning: But most people do not thank Him for His favor toward them in this, and for His other blessings.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 61:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor do you recite any part of the Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or anything smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear record.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And you are not⦆ — O Muhammad — ﴿engaged in any matter﴾, meaning: in any of the affairs [or deeds] ﴿nor do you recite any part of it of the Qur'an﴾, meaning: nor do you recite any part of the Book of God, of the Qur'an [[See the explanation of "al-tilawah" (recitation) in the earlier lexical indexes under (t-l-w).]].

﴿Nor do you do any deed﴾, meaning: nor do you, O people, do any deed, whether good or evil ﴿except that We are witnesses over you﴾, meaning: except that We are witnesses to your deeds and affairs when you do them and engage in them. [[See the explanation of "al-ifadah" (rushing into/engaging) in the earlier volume 4: 170.]]

* *

The same as what we have said about this has been related from Ibn 'Abbas and a group [of others].

Those who said this:

17696- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿when you engage in it﴾, he said: meaning, when you do [it].

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: when you spread falsehood about the Qur'an.

Those who said this:

17697- It was related to me from al-Musayyab ibn Shurayk, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak: ﴿when you engage in it﴾, meaning: you spread falsehood about the Qur'an. [[In the printed edition: "fa-tushi'un" with fa', which does not reflect the manuscript's reading correctly.]]

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: when you engage in the truth.

Those who said this:

17698- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿when you engage in it﴾, in the truth, whatever it was.

17699- ... he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

17700- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We chose the view we chose because He, the Exalted, informed that He does not make His servants do any deed except that He is a witness to it, and then He linked that to His saying: ﴿when you engage in it﴾. So it is known that His saying ﴿when you engage in it﴾ is only a report from Him about the time of the workers' deeds, that He witnesses it — not about the time of the Prophet ﷺ reciting the Qur'an. For if it were a report about His witnessing, the Exalted, the time of the people's engagement in the Qur'an, then the reading with the yā' would be: "idh yufidūna fīhi" (when they engage in it), a report from Him about the deniers concerning it.

If someone says: That is not a report about the deniers, but an address to the Prophet ﷺ, [[In the printed edition: "wa-lakin khitab", without the hā'; I have restored it from the manuscript.]] that He witnessed him when he recited the Qur'an.

— If that were so, the revelation would be ﴿idh tufīdūna fīhi﴾ (when you engage in it), because the Prophet ﷺ is one, not plural, as He said: ﴿and you do not recite any part of it of the Qur'an﴾, addressing him in the singular. But in its beginning the address to him ﷺ is in the singular, then it turns to address the plural, similar to His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ [Surah al-Talaq: 1]. For in His saying: ﴿when you divorce women﴾ there is clear evidence that the address is turned to the community of Muslims together with the Prophet ﷺ and together with the rest of the people, since He began His address and then turned the address to the community of people, with the Prophet ﷺ among them.

— And it is a report that none of His servants does any deed except that He is a witness to it, who records it and knows it, as He said: ﴿And not absent from your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, is the deed of His creation, and the knowledge of anything is not hidden from Him wherever it is, on earth or in heaven.

* *

Its root is from "'uzūb al-rajul 'an ahlihi fī māshiyatihi" (a man's absence from his family while tending his livestock), that being his absence from them in it. It is said from it: "'azaba al-rajul 'an ahlihi ya'zubu wa-ya'zibu" (the man was absent from his family).

* *

Both are eloquent dialects, and a group of readers recited with each of them. Whichever of them the reader recites is correct, because their meanings agree and are widely used in Arabic speech; however, I incline toward the pronunciation with a ḍammah in it, because it is more prevalent among the well-known readers.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿from an atom's weight﴾, it means: from the weight of a small ant.

* *

It is related from the Arabs: "Take this, for it is lighter in mithqal than that," meaning: lighter in weight. [[See the explanation of "al-mithqal" in the earlier volume 8: 360, and Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 278, which is his exact wording.]]

* *

"Al-dharrah" is singular of "al-dharr" and "al-dharr," small ants. [[See the explanation of "al-dharrah" in the earlier volume 8: 360, 361.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: That is a report that nothing is hidden from Him, majestic is His majesty, not the smallest things, even if they are extremely light in weight, nor their measures and extent, and not the greatest, even if they are vast and heavy in weight, nor how great their extent is. He, the Exalted, says to His creatures: So let your deeds, O people, be in what pleases your Lord with regard to you, for We are witnesses to your deeds, nothing of them is hidden from us, and We count them and will repay you for them.

* *

The readers differed in reading His saying: ﴿nor anything smaller than that or greater﴾.

The majority of readers read it with a fatḥah on the rā' of ﴿aṣghara﴾ and ﴿akbara﴾, meaning they are in the genitive case, the "aṣghar" being conjoined to "dharrah" and "akbar" to "aṣghar", and their rā's were given a fatḥah because they are not declined.

* *

Some Kufans read it [wa-la aṣghara min dhalika wa-la akbara] with a ḍammah (nominative), conjoining it to the meaning of "mithqal," since its meaning is nominative. That is because if "min" were removed from the sentence, "mithqal" would be nominative, and the sentence would then be: "wa-ma ya'zubu 'an rabbika mithqalu dharratin wa-la aṣghara min mithqali dharratin wa-la akbaru," similar to His saying: ﴿min khaliqin ghayru Allah﴾ and ﴿ghayru Allah﴾ [Surah Fatir: 3]. [[Abu Ja'far did not mention the nominative reading in this verse in its place in the commentary on Surah Fatir, to be discussed later at 22: 77 (Bulaq), and I will point to that in its place there. This is another instance of Abu Ja'far's abridgment in places, as I indicated in many of my notes.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads with a fatḥah, in the genitive and conjoined to "dharrah," because that is the reading of the regional readers and most readers follow it, and it is more sound in its Arabic derivation, although the other has a known basis.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except in a clear record﴾, it means: all of that is only in a Book with God, ﴿clear﴾, revealing the reality of God's report to whoever looks into it, that nothing has been or will be except that God, His praise be exalted, has recorded it therein, and that the knowledge of nothing of His creation is hidden from God wherever it is, in His heaven or on His earth. [[See the explanation of "mubin" in the earlier lexical indexes under (b-y-n).]]

* *

17701- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and not absent⦆, he said: it is not hidden from Him.

17702- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And not absent from your Lord﴾, he said: what is not hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 62:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His mention, means: Indeed, the supporters of Allah, no fear will be upon them in the Hereafter from the punishment of Allah, because Allah is pleased with them and has granted them security from His punishment; and they will not grieve over what they missed of the world.

* *

"Al-awliya'" is the plural of "wali," which means the supporter (al-nasir). We have explained this with its evidences. [[See the explanation of "wali" in the earlier indices of language (w-l-y), but here there is a detailed discussion of the meaning of "awliya' Allah," which has no precedent.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning who deserves this designation.

Some of them said: They are a people whom Allah is remembered by when seen, due to the marks of goodness and humility upon them.

Mention of those who said this:

17703 – Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Yamān narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾. He said: They are those by whose sight Allah is remembered.

17704 – Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Yamān narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Ishaq, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it. [[The report 17704: "Ash'ath ibn Sa'd ibn Malik al-Qummi," trustworthy, passed as no. 78, and this report is mursal.]]

17705 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yamān narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu al-Duha, the like of it.

17706 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyib, from his father: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾. He said: The one by whose sight Allah is remembered.

17707 – ... He said: Ibn Mahdi and 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu al-Duha, who said: I heard him say concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾. He said: Among the people are "keys," [["Mafatih," plural of "miftah," which is that by which a door is opened. This is a metaphor; he meant that they open the door of goodness for people, and the greatest goodness is the remembrance of Allah, glorified and exalted be He.]] when they are seen, Allah is remembered by their sight.

17708 – ... He said: My father narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Sahl Abu al-Asad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about "the allies of Allah," and he said: Those who, when seen, Allah is remembered. [[The report 17708: "Sahl Abu al-Asad al-Qarari al-Hanafi," trustworthy, mentioned in al-Kabir 2/2/100 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/206. In the printed edition it was "Sahl ibn al-Asad," which is an editorial alteration and an error, differing from the manuscript. "Al-Qarari," with a qaf, al-Bukhari said: "And Qarar is a tribe," which is from Hanifa, from Bakr. Among the books of men is "Sahl al-Fazari" with a fa', and "Sahl ibn so-and-so al-Qarari" with a qaf, who is unknown to them, and I fear he may be "Sahl al-Qarari." See also Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/206, Mizan al-I'tidal 1:431, and Lisan al-Mizan 3:123. Regardless, this is a mursal report from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.]]

17709 – ... He said: Zayd ibn Habbab narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾. He said: Those who, when seen, Allah is remembered by their sight.

17710 – ... He said: Abu Yazid al-Razi narrated to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: They are those who, when seen, Allah is remembered.

17711 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Furat narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about "the allies of Allah," and he said: They are those who, when seen, Allah is remembered.

17712 – ... He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: al-'Awwam informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾, the verse, he said: Indeed, the wali of Allah, when he is seen, Allah is remembered.

* *

Others said, regarding this:

17713 – Abu Hashim al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from 'Imara ibn al-Qa'qa' al-Dabbi, from Abu Zur'a ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir al-Bajali, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Indeed among the servants of Allah are servants whom the prophets and martyrs envy! It was said: Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? Perhaps we would love them! He said: They are a people who love one another for the sake of Allah, not for wealth or lineage; their faces are light, upon pulpits of light; they do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve when people grieve. And he recited: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾. [[The report 17713: "Ibn Fudayl" is "Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan al-Dabbi," trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, passed many times, the last being no. 14247. In the printed and manuscript editions it was "Abu Fudayl," which is an error; the correct reading is from Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4:314, which transmitted this report from this place of the commentary. His father: "Fudayl ibn Ghazwan al-Dabbi," trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, passed as no. 14247. "Imara ibn al-Qa'qa' al-Dabbi," trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, passed as nos. 14203, 14209, 14715. "Abu Zur'a ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali," a trustworthy Successor, whom the group narrated from, passed many times, the last being no. 14715. In the printed and manuscript editions it was "Abu Zur'a, from 'Amr ibn Hamza," and similarly in the manuscript, but "Hamza" is badly written and is actually "Jarir," one letter having entered another. The error in his name has passed many times. This is a sound isnad.

al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:310, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi.]]

17714 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Imara, from Abu Zur'a, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Indeed among the servants of Allah are people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whom the prophets and martyrs envy on the Day of Resurrection because of their station with Allah! They said: O Messenger of Allah, tell us who they are and what their deeds are, so that we may love them for that! He said: They are a people who love one another in Allah through the Spirit of Allah, with no kinship between them nor wealth they exchange. By Allah, indeed their faces are light, and indeed they are upon light; they do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve when people grieve. And he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾. [[The report 17714: its narrators were explained in the previous isnad, except that Abu Zur'a ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir did not narrate from 'Umar except as mursal, so it is a good isnad but disconnected (munqati').]]

17715 – Bahr ibn Nasr al-Khawlani narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram narrated to us, saying: Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There will come from the scattered folk of people and the strangers of the tribes, [["Afna' al-nas" are the mixed ones, and those who do not know from which tribe they are. "Nawazi' al-qaba'il" is the plural of "nazi'," irregularly, and they are the strangers who dwell beside tribes that are not theirs. I only said "irregular plural" because the well-known form is "nazza' al-qaba'il," as occurs in another hadith. And the adjectival form "fa'il" for the masculine is not pluralized as "fawa'il" among them except by transmission, such as "fawaris" and "hawalik."]] people whose kin-ties are not closely connected, [[In the printed edition: "lam yatassil," and the correct reading is from the manuscript and Musnad Ahmad.]] who love one another in Allah and are sincere to one another in Allah. Allah will set for them on the Day of Resurrection pulpits of light, and He will seat them upon them; people will be terrified, but they will not be terrified, and they are the allies of Allah, of whom there is no fear and they do not grieve." [[The report 17715: "Bahr ibn Nasr ibn Sabiq al-Khawlani al-Misri," the teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy, passed as nos. 3841, 10588, 10647. In the printed edition here it was "al-Hasan ibn Nasr al-Khawlani," and I do not know where that came from, though it hits part of the correct form; this is surprising. In the manuscript it is "al-Hasan ibn al-Khawlani," and the correct reading is what is adopted here. His narration from "Yahya ibn Hassan" passed as no. 2643, though there too an error occurred in his name, written "Yahya ibn Nasr," and we struggled with its misreading; the correct form is "Bahr ibn Nasr," which should be corrected there. "Yahya ibn Hassan al-Tinnisi al-Misri," trustworthy, passed as no. 2643, and the narrator from him there is also "Bahr ibn Nasr," as previously stated. "'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram al-Fazari," trustworthy, whom Ahmad and others declared trustworthy, passed many times, the last being no. 17417. "Shahr ibn Hawshab" passed many times, and his reliability has passed; my brother Ahmad al-Sayyid, may Allah have mercy on him and forgive him, declared him trustworthy. "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm al-Ash'ari," whose companionship is disputed, is counted among the first tier of Successors. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab sent him to teach people jurisprudence; he was attached to Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and was the most learned of the people of Syria, and he is the one who taught most of the Successors in Syria, and he had standing and rank. Abu Malik al-Ash'ari is the one known by his kunya, with a disputed name, a Companion, whose biography is in al-Isaba, al-Tahdhib, and all the other books. This is a report of sound isnad. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad at length, 5:343, and al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:310, attributing it additionally to Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Kitab al-Ikhwan, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is to say: "The wali" – I mean "wali Allah" – is the one who has the description by which Allah described him, and he is the one who believed and was God-fearing, as Allah said: ﴿Those who believed and were God-conscious﴾.

* *

In accordance with what we have said on this matter, Ibn Zayd used to say:

17716 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾: Who are they, O Lord? He said: ﴿Those who believed and were God-conscious﴾. He said: He refused that faith be accepted except with piety. [[In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "an yuqabbal," and the correct reading is what is adopted here.]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believed and used to be God-fearing (63)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: those who affirmed God and His Messenger, and what came to him from God, and who used to fear God (taqwa) by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

* *

As for His words, ﴿those who believed﴾, it is a qualifier (na't) of "the friends (awliya')," and the meaning of the statement is: Verily, the friends of God are those who believed and were God-fearing; there is no fear upon them, nor do they grieve.

* *

If someone says: Given that the meaning of the statement is what I have mentioned to you, is ﴿those who believed﴾ in the nominative position (raf') or in the accusative position (nasb)?

It is said: In the nominative position. It is so, even though it is a qualifier of "the friends," because it comes after the predicate of "the friends." The Arabs do this specifically with "inna" (verily): when the qualifier of the noun on which it operates comes after the completion of its predicate, they put it in the nominative, saying, "Inna akhaka qa'imu al-zarifu" (verily your brother is standing, the witty one), as God said: ﴿Say: Indeed my Lord hurls the truth; He is the Knower of the unseen [ghuyub]﴾ [Surah Saba': 48], and as He said: ﴿Indeed that is truth: the disputing of the people of the Fire﴾ [Surah Sad: 64]. [See Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1: 470, 471.]

* *

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed regarding the reason for which it is said this way, although all of them agree that what we have stated is the correct usage of the Arabs. This is not the place to explain the reasons for which it is said thus.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 64 (part 1 of 3):

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no alteration in the words of Allah. That is the great triumph.ﴩ (64)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The good news from Allah in this world and in the Hereafter is for the friends of Allah who believed and were mindful of Him. [[See the explanation of "al-bushra" (good news) above, 14:508, footnote 1, and the references there.]]
* *
Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning "al-bushra" (the good news) with which Allah gave good tidings to these people: what is it, and what is its nature? Some of them said: It is the good dream (al-ru'ya al-salihah) that a Muslim man sees, or that is seen for him; and in the Hereafter, it is Paradise.

١٧٧٢٨- Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Mu'addib narrated to us, who said: Ammar ibn Muhammad narrated to us, who said: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾: "A good dream that a righteous servant sees, or that is seen for him. And in the Hereafter it is Paradise."

[[The report: 17728. "Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Sulayman al-Zummi," al-Mu'addib, the teacher of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari), is trustworthy (thiqah). Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Hatim al-Razi and others narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/238, and in Tarikh Baghdad 2/268.

"Ammar ibn Muhammad al-Thawri," the nephew of Sufyan al-Thawri, is not objectionable (la ba'sa bihi). Ahmad, Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam and Abu Kurayb narrated from him. Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy, and al-Bukhari said: "He was more trustworthy than Sayf." Sayf was his brother, a lying, wicked shaykh who fabricated hadith. Ibn Hibban said of Ammar: "His errors were grave and his wahm (mistakes) numerous, so he deserves to be abandoned (al-tark)." In my view Ibn Hibban went to an extreme in this. Nevertheless, I fear that his statement is an explanation of al-Bukhari's remark that he was more trustworthy than his lying brother Sayf, and that he was weak to some degree, but not to the degree of abandonment or discarding.
