١٧٧٢٩- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, who said: Rushdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu al-Samh, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "For them is good news in the life of this world": "A good dream by which the servant is given good news is one part of forty-nine parts of prophethood."

[[The report: 17729. It is a hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr; it will come by another route, no. 17754.

The "Muhammad ibn Yazid" whom Abu Kurayb narrated from is not specified here. I think he is "Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Hizami al-Bazzaz," who narrated from Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Walid ibn Muslim, Damrah ibn Rabi'ah, Sharik and Ibn Uyaynah. al-Bukhari narrated from him in al-Tarikh, and so did Abu Kurayb. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/261, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/128, and Mizan al-I'tidal 3/150. al-Bukhari did not mention any criticism of him there.

As for "Rushdin ibn Sa'd al-Misri," he is weak in hadith (da'if al-hadith). His weakening has passed at nos. 19, 1938, 2176, 2195. Abu Kurayb narrates from Rushdin directly, as has passed in the reports I mentioned.

"Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Ya'qub al-Misri" is trustworthy and a memorizer (thiqah hafiz). He has passed many times, the last at no. 13570.

As for "Abu al-Samh," he is "Darraj ibn Sam'an," freedman of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As. He is trustworthy, though spoken of (muta'allam fihi). My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, favoured his trustworthiness in earlier passages, nos. 3187, 5518. In the printed edition it read "from Abu al-Shaykh," which is a clear error. The manuscript has the same unpointed form. The correct reading is what I have written, as will come at no. 17754.

"Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr al-Misri," the jurist, is trustworthy. He narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr, Uqbah ibn Amir, Amr ibn Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi, and Abu al-Darda'. Abdullah ibn Amr was proud of him (kana Abdullah ibn Amr bihi mu'jaban). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/221.

This report is weak in its chain because of the weakness of Rushdin ibn Sa'd. It will come with a sound chain at no. 17754.]]

١٧٧٣٠- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Khalid ibn Safwan, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that he said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter." We know the good news of the Hereafter; what is the good news of this world? He said: "A good dream that the servant sees, or that is seen for him, and it is one part of forty-four parts, or sixty parts, of prophethood."

[[The report: 17730. This is the third route of the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit.

"Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabadhi" is weak, whose narration is not permissible to rely upon (la tahillu al-riwayah 'anhu). He has passed many times, the last at no. 16229.

"Ayyub ibn Khalid ibn Safwan al-Ansari" is trustworthy but spoken of. He narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah and from the Successors (al-tabi'un). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/412, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/245. al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, and Ibn Abi Hatim, distinguished between him and "Ayyub ibn Khalid ibn Abi Ayyub al-Ansari." Abu Zur'ah also distinguished between them. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "Ibn Yunus took them to be one person. I say: the reason for this is that Khalid ibn Safwan was the father of Ayyub, and his mother was Amrah bint Abi Ayyub al-Ansari, so he was her maternal grandfather. The more likely view is that of Ibn Yunus, since al-Bukhari anticipated him." But I have seen that al-Bukhari distinguished between them in his Tarikh, so I do not know from where the Hafiz Ibn Hajar derived that.

This chain is weak, because of the weakness of Musa ibn Ubaydah, and it is also an interrupted chain (munqati'), because Ayyub ibn Khalid did not narrate from Ubadah ibn al-Samit.

In the printed edition it read "or seventy parts of prophethood," and I have preferred what is in the manuscript.]]

١٧٧٣١- Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, who said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, who said: Abu Amr narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that he asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about this verse: "For them is good news in the life of this world." He said: "You have asked me about something that none of my community asked me about before you! It is the good dream that the Muslim sees, or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter is Paradise."

[[The report: 17731. This is the first route of the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, as I detailed at no. 17718. It is another chain for the report at no. 17718.]]

١٧٧٣٢- Ahmad ibn Hammad al-Dulabi narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, from his father, from Sabba' ibn Thabit, from Umm Kurz al-Ka'biyyah: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Prophethood has gone, and the bearers of good news remain."

[[The report: 17732. "Ahmad ibn Hammad ibn Sa'id al-Dulabi," the teacher of al-Tabari, is trustworthy, and has passed at nos. 2593, 3571.

"Sufyan" is Ibn Uyaynah.

"Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid al-Makki" is trustworthy, and has passed at nos. 20, 3778, 10274, 14673-14677.

His father, "Abu Yazid al-Makki," is trustworthy, and has passed at no. 20.

"Sabba' ibn Thabit," an ally of the Banu Zuhrah, was counted among the Companions by Ibn Hajar and Ibn al-Athir. He is biographed in both, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/312, but no companionship is mentioned for him. In the manuscript alone it read "Sabba' ibn Abi Thabit," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.

This report comes through Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain, and Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan, p. 1283, no. 3896, and al-Darimi in his Sunan 2/123, with the same wording. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad 6/381 through Sufyan ibn Uyaynah as well, and narrated three other hadiths with the same chain in which it reads: "Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, from his father, from Sabba' ibn Thabit." Abu Abd al-Rahman, his son, said: "I heard my father say: Sufyan erred in these hadiths. Ubayd Allah heard them from Sabba' ibn Thabit." He then quoted one of the four hadiths through Affan, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: "Sabba' ibn Thabit narrated to me," explicitly stating the transmission.

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned in the biography of Sabba' ibn Thabit that Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid narrated from Sabba' ibn Thabit through the narration of Ibn Jurayj and Hammad ibn Zayd from him. He said: "As for Ibn Uyaynah, he narrates from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, from his father, from Sabba' ibn Thabit."

This report is sound (sahih), despite the differences in it, and the error lies with Sufyan.]]

١٧٧٣٣- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from al-A'mash, from Dhakwan, from a man, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding his saying: "For them is good news in the life of this world." He said: "A good dream that the Muslim sees, or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter is Paradise."

[[The report: 17733. It is a hadith of Abu al-Darda', from the first route that I explained in the commentary on no. 17717. Here it is narrated through al-A'mash, from Abu Salih Dhakwan. See the commentary on no. 17717.

Ahmad narrated it through this route in his Musnad 6/445, with his chain from Abd al-Razzaq, from Sufyan.]]

١٧٧٣٤- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from a man who was in Egypt, who said: I asked Abu al-Darda' about this verse: "For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter." Abu al-Darda' said: "No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it!" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one has asked me about it before you. It is the good dream that the Muslim sees, or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter is Paradise."

[[The report: 17734. It is a hadith of Abu al-Darda', from the third route that I explained at no. 17717, and it repeats no. 17722, which I took out there.]]

١٧٧٣٥- . . . He said: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Salih, from Abu al-Darda', who said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about his saying: "For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter." He said: "No one has asked me about it other than you. It is the good dream that the Muslim sees, or that is seen for him."

[[The report: 17735. This is the second route of the hadith of Abu al-Darda' as well, but it is the narration of Abu Salih Dhakwan directly from Abu al-Darda', as will come at no. 17741. I have detailed this in the commentary on no. 17717. This is the route that al-Tirmidhi pointed to in his Sunan, in the Book of Tafsir, as an appendix to the report that Abu Ja'far narrated at no. 17724.

"Asim" is "Asim ibn Bahdalah," and "Asim ibn Abi al-Najud." He is trustworthy, and the whole group narrated from him. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from him in conjunction with others, because there was something in his memory. I fear that what he is alone in reporting may be from his poor memory in it. See the commentary on the whole hadith of Abu al-Darda'.]]

١٧٧٣٦- . . . He said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu al-Darda' regarding his saying: "For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter." He said: "I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it, and he said: No one has asked me about it before you. It is the good dream that the servant sees, or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter is Paradise."

[[The report: 17736. This is the fourth route of the hadith of Abu al-Darda', being the narration of Abu Salih al-Samman, Dhakwan, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu al-Darda' directly, without an intermediary. "Ata' ibn Yasar" narrates from Abu al-Darda'.

Its chain is good (hasan). See what I said in the commentary on no. 17717, and what will come at no. 17743.]]

١٧٧٣٧- . . . He said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay', from Abu Salih = Ibn Uyaynah said: then I heard it from Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Salih al-Samman = from Ata' ibn Yasar, from a man from the people of Egypt, who said: I asked Abu al-Darda' about this verse: "For them is good news in the life of this world." He said: "No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it." Then he said: "No one has asked me about it since it was revealed to me, except one man. It is the good dream that the man sees, or that is seen for him."

[[The report: 17737. The hadith of Abu al-Darda' is from the third route that I explained at no. 17717.

Ibn Uyaynah heard this report from Amr ibn Dinar, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay', and then heard it from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay' directly.

"Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay' al-Asadi" is a trustworthy Successor, whom the whole group narrated from. He has passed at no. 14810.

Ahmad narrated it through this route in his Musnad 6/447, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay', without "Amr ibn Dinar" between them. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Sunan, in the Book of Tafsir, as a follow-up to the report that passed at no. 17724.]]

١٧٧٣٨- . . . He said: Abdullah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us, from Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah, from Amr ibn Dinar: that he asked a jurist from the people of Egypt, who had come to them in one of those seasons. He said: I said: "Will you not tell me about the saying of God, may He be remembered: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾?" He said: "I asked Abu al-Darda' about it, and he informed me that he had asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it, and he said: It is the good dream that the servant sees, or that is seen for him."

[[The report: 17738. This is the fifth route of the hadith of Abu al-Darda'.

"Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Habib al-Sahmi" is trustworthy, and has passed at no. 10885.

"Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah" is trustworthy, and has passed at nos. 17410, 17411.

"Amr ibn Dinar" did not hear from Abu al-Darda', but he narrated it here from an unknown person, a "jurist from the people of Egypt." Therefore it is a weak hadith.]]

١٧٧٣٩- . . . He said: My father narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the saying of God, may He be exalted: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾. He said: "It is the good dream that the servant sees, or that is seen for him."

[[The report: 17739. This is a hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, from the first route that I explained at no. 17718.

I have detailed the hadith from him in the commentary on no. 17721, that defective chain, and at no. 17720, and I explained its defect there.

Ahmad narrated it through this route in his Musnad 5/315.

Ibn Majah in his Sunan, p. 1283, no. 3898.

al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2/340, and he said: "This hadith is sound in its chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. I have already shown that Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman did not hear from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, so the chain is interrupted (munqati'). That is its defect, even though the rest of the chain is sound.]]

١٧٧٤٠- al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim and Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi narrated to us, the two of them saying: Aban narrated to us, who said: Yahya narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾." He said: "You have asked me about something that none before you asked me about, or: none of my community asked me about." He said: "It is the good dream that the righteous man sees, or that is seen for him."

[[The report: 17740. It is a hadith of Ubadah from the first route, like the one before it. It repeats no. 17720, which I took out there.]]

١٧٧٤١- . . . He said: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, who said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Salih, who said: I heard Abu al-Darda', when he was asked about: ﴿Those who believed and used to be mindful of God, for them is good news in the life of this world﴾. He said: "No one has asked me about it before you since I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it. Then he said: No one has asked me about it before you. It is the good dream that the servant sees, or that is seen for him."

[[The report: 17741. It is a hadith of Abu al-Darda' from the second route. It repeats no. 17735, and I took it out there.]]

١٧٧٤٢- al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from a man of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his saying: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾. He said: "It is the good dream that a person sees, or that is seen for him."

[[The report: 17742. "Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid al-Makki" is trustworthy, and has passed shortly before at no. 17732. "Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im al-Nawfali" is a famous Successor and one of the Imams, who has passed at no. 17429. This report was narrated by Nafi' from a Companion whose name he did not state. Perhaps it is Abu Hurayrah. The ignorance of a Companion does not harm. So it is a sound hadith, God willing.]]

١٧٧٤٣- . . . He said: Ibn Jurayj said, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Abu al-Darda' = or Ibn Jurayj, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about it, and he said: It is the good dream."

[[The report: 17743. This hadith of Abu al-Darda' comes through two routes: the route of Amr ibn Dinar from Abu al-Darda' without an intermediary, which is the sixth route that I explained at no. 17717. "Amr ibn Dinar" did not hear from Abu al-Darda', as I showed at no. 17738, so it is weak because of its break in continuity (inqita').]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 64 (part 3 of 3):

The chain through Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abu al-Darda', is the fourth route. Its explanation has already passed in the takhrij of the report numbered 17736. See also the report of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from a man of the people of Egypt, from Abu al-Darda', numbered 17723 and 17724.]]

17744. ... Ibn Jurayj said, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father: "It is the dream a man sees."

17745. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: "It is the righteous dream that a Muslim sees, or that is seen for him."

17746. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿAbda narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, concerning ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world﴾, he said: "It is the righteous dream that a righteous servant sees."

17747. ... He said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "It is the righteous dream that a Muslim sees, or that is seen for him."

17748. ... He said: ʿAbda ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Talha al-Qannad, from Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world﴾, he said: "It is the good dream that a Muslim sees for himself or for some of his brothers." [[The report 17748: this is a report halted at Ibn ʿAbbas (mawquf).]]

17749. He said: My father narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, who said: "They used to say: the dream is among the good tidings."

17750. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Qays ibn Saʿd: that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about it, and he said: "No one from my community has asked me about it since it was revealed to me before you!" He said: "It is the righteous dream that a man sees for himself, or that is seen for him." [[The report 17750: this is a mursal report.]]

17751. ... He said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from al-ʿAwwam, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, that Ibn Masʿud said: "Prophethood has gone, and the good tidings remain!" It was said: "And what are the good tidings?" He said: "The righteous dream that a man sees, or that is seen for him." [[The report 17751: this is a report halted at Ibn Masʿud (mawquf), with a sound chain.]]

17752. He said: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world﴾, that it is His saying to His Prophet: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 47]. He said: "It is the good dream that a believer sees, or that is seen for him."

17753. ... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahiʿa narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from ʿAta', concerning His saying ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world﴾, he said: "It is the dream of a Muslim man who is given good tidings by it during his life."

17754. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world﴾: "The righteous dream by which a believer is given good tidings is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood." [[The report 17754: the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr has passed through another weak route, numbered 17729. ʿAmr ibn al-Harith al-Misri is trustworthy, passed under 17729.
And "Darraj ibn Sam'an", "Abu al-Samh", is trustworthy, also passed under 17729, and the authentication of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, for him. It was narrated by Ahmad at length with its chain, numbered 7044, through the route of Hasan ibn al-Ashyab, from Lahi'a, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, and my brother said: "Its chain is sound." Al-Haythami also cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 175, and said: "Ahmad narrated it through the route of Ibn Lahi'a from Darraj." Their hadith is good, though there is weakness in both; the rest of its narrators are trustworthy. This other route, through Ibn Wahb, is more reliable than the route of Ibn Lahi'a. Al-Haythami also cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 36 and said something similar.]]

17755. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Anas ibn ʿIyad informed us, from Hisham, from his father, concerning this verse: ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾, he said: "It is the righteous dream that a man sees, or that is seen for him."

17756. Muhammad ibn ʿAwf narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us: that a man asked ʿUbada ibn al-Samit about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. ʿUbada said: "You have asked me about a matter that no one before you has asked me about. I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what you have asked me, and he said to me: 'O ʿUbada, you have asked me about a matter that no one from my community has asked me about! It is the righteous dream that a believer sees for himself, or that is seen for him.'" [[The report 17756: this is the second route of the hadith of ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, which I mentioned under 17718.
Muhammad ibn ʿAwf ibn Sufyan al-Ta'i, the teacher of al-Tabari, passed under 5445, 12194, 13108. Abu al-Mughira is ʿAbd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj al-Khawlani, trustworthy, passed under 10371, 12194, 13108. Safwan is Safwan ibn ʿAmr ibn Harim al-Sakasaki, trustworthy, passed under 7009, 12807, 13108. Ahmad narrated it from this same route in the chain, 5: 325, from Abu al-Mughira, from Safwan, from Humayd ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Yazani. Humayd ibn ʿAbd Allah passed under 17725, where it resembles "al-Muzani", and I noted that in Ibn Abi Hatim it is "al-Madani", and in the Musnad "al-Yazani", as you have seen. Then there is another difference: in the Musnad, "Humayd ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Yazani"; but I have not found this difference in any of the collections, so I fear it is an error of a copyist of the Musnad. It was noted under 17725 that this chain is interrupted between Humayd ibn ʿAbd Allah and ʿUbada ibn al-Samit.]]

* *

Others said: It is good tidings that the believer is given in this world at the time of death.

Those who said this:

17757. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri and Qatada, concerning ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world﴾, he said: "It is the good tidings at death in the life of this world."

17758. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Yaʿla narrated to us, from Abu Bistam, from al-Dahhak, concerning ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world﴾, he said: "He knows where he will be before death."

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these sayings concerning the interpretation of this, in my view, is to say: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, has informed that for His righteous friends who fear Him there is good tidings in the life of this world. Among the good tidings in the life of this world is the righteous dream that a Muslim sees, or that is seen for him; and among them is the good tidings of the angels to him at the departure of his soul with the mercy of Allah, as has been related from the Prophet ﷺ: "The angels who attend him at the departure of his soul say to his soul: 'Come out to the mercy and pleasure of Allah.'" [[A hadith without a chain, which I have not been able to find in its wording nearby.]]
Among them is: Allah's good tidings to him of what He has promised in His Book and upon the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ of abundant reward, as the Exalted said: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds, that for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 25], and so on.
All these meanings are among the good tidings Allah gives him in this worldly life; He did not single out one meaning over another. So it is among what His Exalted saying encompasses: that ﴿for them is good tidings in the life of this world﴾. As for the Hereafter, it is Paradise.

* *

As for His saying ﴿There is no alteration to the words of Allah﴾, its meaning is: Allah does not break His promise, and there is no change in His word from what He has said; rather, He fulfills His promises to His creation and accomplishes them for them. [[See the explanation of "alteration of the words" above, 2: 62, notes 1 and 3, and the references there.]] And:

17759. Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafiʿ, who said: "al-Hajjaj prolonged the sermon, so Ibn ʿUmar placed his head in my lap. Al-Hajjaj said: 'Ibn al-Zubayr has altered the Book of Allah!' Ibn ʿUmar sat up and said: 'You cannot do that, nor can Ibn al-Zubayr! There is no alteration to the words of Allah!' Al-Hajjaj said: 'You have been given knowledge, if it benefits you!'" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "You have been given knowledge that you would act," which is clearly corrupt; its correct form is from al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim.]] He said: Ayyub said: "When he turned to him in his own personal matter, he fell silent." [[The report 17759: al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2: 339, 340, through Abu al-Nu'man, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayya, from Ayyub, similar to it, without the word "Ayyub" in it. He said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. This report is of great significance, containing the character of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, manifest as their Messenger taught them: leaving aside awe of tyrants, rejecting wrong by word and deed, vigilance toward the meanings of speech and the aims of actions, teaching people openly the errors of their rulers and governors, and patience with the harm of these tyrants when the harm touches them personally. As for when the matter is the command of Allah and His Messenger, and the revealed Book with truth for the pious and the tyrannical alike, commanding and forbidding them equally, they do not fear a tyrant who has accustomed his sword to shedding blood and trained his tongue to sting and to wrangle. May Allah have mercy on a nation whose noble leaders and guides were like these!]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿That is the great triumph﴾, the Exalted means: this good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter is "the great triumph," meaning attainment of the need and the desire, and deliverance from the Fire. [[See the explanation of "triumph" above, 14: 439, note 4, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 65:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (10:65)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty and Glorious is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not let grieve you, O Muhammad, the speech of these polytheists about their Lord, what they say, and their associating with Him idols and images [[See the explanation of "al-huzn" (grief) earlier, 10:108, note 5, and the references there.]] — for indeed, all honor belongs to Allah. Exalted is He says: Indeed, Allah alone possesses the honor of this world and the Hereafter, with no partner in it, and He is the Avenger against these polytheists who utter about Him the false speech they utter, so none will help them against His vengeance, for nothing can overpower Him [[See the explanation of "al-izzah" (honor, might) earlier, 10:421, note 3, and the references there.]]. ﴿He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ That is, He is the One who hears what they say of slander and lies against Him, and the One who knows what they conceal in their souls and what they make apparent, all of it counted against them, and He is ever watchful over them. [[See the explanation of "al-Sami'" (the All-Hearing) and "al-'Alim" (the All-Knowing) earlier, in the language indices under (s-m-' ) and ('-l-m).]]

* *

The "inna" in His saying ﴿Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah﴾ is pronounced with a kasra (inna, not anna) because it is a statement from Allah beginning a new sentence, and the verb "qawl" (saying) does not govern it, because "qawl" refers to the speech of the polytheists, and His saying ﴿indeed, all honor belongs to Allah﴾ was not part of the polytheists' speech, nor is it a report that they said it. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:471–472, which contains a detailed discussion of the position of "inna" after "qawl" and similar verbs.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 66:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Verily, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And those who call upon other than Allah as partners do not follow them. They follow only conjecture, and they are only guessing.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: Verily, to Allah, O Muhammad, belongs everyone who is in the heavens and everyone who is on the earth, as possessions and as servants, and none possesses anything of that besides Him. He means: how, then, could one be a god worthy of worship when these polytheists worship idols and images, which are themselves the property of Allah? Worship is due only to the owner, not to the owned, and to the Lord, not to the one who is lord over others. ﴿And what do those who call upon other than Allah as partners follow?﴾ The Exalted says: What is it that those who call upon other than Allah, meaning: other than Allah and besides Him, as partners, follow? The meaning of the statement is: What is it that they follow, those who falsely claim that Allah has partners in His authority and dominion, when Allah alone possesses the dominion of everything in heaven or on earth? ﴿They follow only conjecture﴾ means: in their saying that and their claim, they follow nothing but conjecture; that is, nothing but doubt, not certainty. ﴿And they are only guessing﴾ means: they only fabricate falsehood by conjecture and by guessing at lies, [[In the printed edition: "tazannanan," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript, as pointed in the manuscript, though its letters are largely unpointed. "Al-tazanni" is "al-tazannun," and its final nun was changed to a yā' because of the succession of nuns, which is heavy, a common and widespread usage in the speech of the Arabs.]] without knowledge on their part of what they say.

The commentary on the words of God Almighty: ﴿He it is Who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day to see by. Surely in that are signs for a people who hear.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Surely your Lord, O people, Who deserves worship from you, is the Lord who made the night for you and separated it from the day, so that you may rest therein from the fatigue and toil, and be at ease therein from the movement and activity for livelihood and the exertion you were in during the day. ﴿And the day to see by﴾: he says, and He made the day to see by. He attributed "seeing" (al-ibsar) to "the day," whereas it is in the day that one sees, and the day is not itself what sees. But since its meaning was understood in the speech of the Arabs, He addressed them in the language and idiom they use.

This is like the saying of Jarir:

"You blamed us, O Umm Ghaylan, for travelling by night, and you slept, yet the night of the riding camels is not asleep."

Here he attributed "sleep" to "the night" and described it with it, while its meaning is itself: that neither he nor his camel was asleep in it.

* *

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So He who does that is your Lord, who created you and what you worship, not what does not benefit or harm and does nothing.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Surely in that are signs for a people who hear﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Surely in the variation of the condition of the night and the day, and the condition of their people within them, there is evidence and proofs that the One who alone deserves worship, without partner, is the One who created the night and the day and made them differ, by making this a place of rest for creation and that a means of livelihood for them, unlike what does not create, does nothing, and neither harms nor benefits.

* *

He said: ﴿for a people who hear﴾, because what is meant by it is: those who hear these proofs and reflect upon them, so that they take lessons from them and are admonished. It does not mean those who hear with their ears and then turn away from its lessons and admonitions.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 68:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They say, "Allah has taken a son." Glory be to Him! He is the Self-Sufficient. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. You have no authority for this. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His mention, exalted is He, says: These polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, said: ﴿Allah has taken a son﴾, and this is their saying: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Allah says, declaring Himself free of what they said and falsely attributed to Him of that: "Glory be to Allah" (subhan Allah), a declaring of Allah free of what they said and claimed about their Lord [[See the explanation of "subhan" (glorification, exalting God above imperfection) earlier, p. 47, footnote 1, and the references there.]]. "He is the Self-Sufficient" means: Allah is free of need from all His creation, so He has no need of a son, [[See the explanation of "al-Ghani" (the Self-Sufficient, Free of Need) earlier, 12:126, footnote 1, and the references there.]] for a son is only sought by one who seeks him, to be a helper to him in his life and a memory of him after his death. Allah is free of all of that, so He has no need of a helper to assist Him in His governing, and He does not perish such that He would need a successor after Him. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: His mention, exalted is He, says: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth as possession, and the angels are His servants and His property. So how could a man's servant and property be his son? That is, do you not reason, O people, about the error of what you say? ﴿You have no authority for this﴾: that is, you have no proof, O people, for what you say and claim, that the angels are the daughters of Allah, by which you argue, and that is the authority [[See the explanation of "sultan" (authority, proof) earlier, 12:523, footnote 2, and the references there.]], ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾: that is, do you say about Allah a saying whose reality and correctness you do not know, and attribute to Him what is not permissible to attribute to Him, out of your ignorance of what you say, without any argument or proof?

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 10, verses 69–70**

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed. (69) [They have] enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾ (70)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to them: ﴿Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah﴾, meaning they say falsehood about Him and claim that He has a son [[See the explanation of "al-iftira' (invention)" earlier in the language indices, under (f-r-w).]] = ﴿will not succeed﴾, meaning: they will not remain in this world. [[See the explanation of "al-falah (success)" earlier, p. 46, note 1, and the references there.]]

But they have enjoyment in this world, which they enjoy, and provision with which they sustain themselves until the term whose end is decreed for them. = ﴿Then to Us is their return﴾, meaning: then, when their appointed term that was decreed for them has passed, to Us is their destination and their final turning. [[See the explanation of "al-marji' (return)" earlier, p. 98, note 2, and the references there.]]

= ﴿Then We will make them taste the severe punishment﴾, and that is their being burned in Hell. [[See the explanation of "al-dhawq (tasting)" earlier, p. 102, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿because they used to disbelieve﴾ in Allah in this world, so they denied His messengers and rejected His signs.

* *

The word ﴿enjoyment﴾ is in the nominative by an elided element before it, which is either "that" (dhalika) or "this" (hadha). [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:472, where he says: "either (huwa) or (dhak)."]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 10, verses 69–70**

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed. (69) [They have] enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾ (70)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to them: ﴿Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah﴾, meaning they say falsehood about Him and claim that He has a son [[See the explanation of "al-iftira' (invention)" earlier in the language indices, under (f-r-w).]] = ﴿will not succeed﴾, meaning: they will not remain in this world. [[See the explanation of "al-falah (success)" earlier, p. 46, note 1, and the references there.]]

But they have enjoyment in this world, which they enjoy, and provision with which they sustain themselves until the term whose end is decreed for them. = ﴿Then to Us is their return﴾, meaning: then, when their appointed term that was decreed for them has passed, to Us is their destination and their final turning. [[See the explanation of "al-marji' (return)" earlier, p. 98, note 2, and the references there.]]

= ﴿Then We will make them taste the severe punishment﴾, and that is their being burned in Hell. [[See the explanation of "al-dhawq (tasting)" earlier, p. 102, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿because they used to disbelieve﴾ in Allah in this world, so they denied His messengers and rejected His signs.

* *

The word ﴿enjoyment﴾ is in the nominative by an elided element before it, which is either "that" (dhalika) or "this" (hadha). [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:472, where he says: "either (huwa) or (dhak)."]]

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: "And recite to them the account of Noah, when he said to his people, 'O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of the signs of Allah has been burdensome to you, then upon Allah I have relied. So resolve upon your affair, with your associates, then let not your affair be obscured to you; then carry it out against me and do not give me respite'" (10:71).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "And recite" to these polytheists who said, "Allah has taken a son" [from among your people] "the account of Noah" — that is, the report of Noah [see the explanation of "al-naba'" (the report) earlier, p. 102, note 3, and the references there] — "when he said to his people, 'O my people, if my standing [among you] has been burdensome to you'" — that is, if my standing among you and my being a burden upon you has been heavy and grievous to you [see the explanation of "kabura" (to be heavy) earlier, 11:336, 337] — "and my reminding you of the signs of Allah" — that is, my admonishing you with the proofs of Allah and my alerting you to them [see the explanation of "al-tadhkir" (reminding) earlier in the lexicon entry on (dh-k-r)] — "then upon Allah I have relied" — that is: if my standing among you has been burdensome to you, and my reminding you of the signs of Allah, and you have resolved to kill me or expel me from among you, then upon Allah is my reliance, in Him is my trust, and He is my support and my backing [see the explanation of "al-tawakkul" (reliance) earlier, 14:587, note 3, and the references there] — "So resolve upon your affair" — that is: prepare your affair and determine upon what you intend concerning me.

[In the printed edition: "and what you advance upon," and in the manuscript: "and what you sawwimun" without dots, which is a scribal error; the correct reading, which I favour, is what I have given, because "ijma'" (resolving) is the firming up of intention and determination.]

* *

It is said of it: "I resolved upon such-and-such" (ajma'tu 'ala kadhā), meaning: I determined upon it [see the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:473, where he discusses it at length].

From it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever does not resolve upon fasting from the night, there is no fasting for him," meaning: whoever does not determine [it]. [This is a hadith he transmitted without an isnad. It was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Hafsa, Mother of the Believers. See Sunan Abi Dawud 2:441, 442, no. 2454.]

From it is also the saying of the poet [the speaker of which I have not identified, though I think it is Abu al-Najm, as I recall]:

"Would that I knew, though wishes do not profit: Shall I ever go out one day while my affair is resolved?"

[Nawadir Abi Zayd: 133; Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:473; al-Lisan (j-m-') and (z-f-a). After it, as Abu Zayd transmitted: "And beneath my saddle is a swift, lean camel, a tool that, when I restrain it, turns back."]

* *

It is related from al-A'raj on this matter:

17760 - One of our companions related to me, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Harun, from Usayd, from al-A'raj regarding "So resolve upon your affair, with your associates," that he said: "Make your affair firm, and call upon your associates."

[Report 17760: 'Abd al-Wahhab is 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi, who has passed many times, the last at no. 14229. Harun is Harun ibn Musa al-A'war the grammarian, who has passed at nos. 4985, 11693, 15514, 15515. Usayd is Usayd ibn Abi Usayd, Yazid, al-Barrad, who transmitted the readings from al-A'raj; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 2/1/49, where it says only that he related from al-A'raj in recitation, and gives no lineage. In Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/316, under the entry "Usayd ibn Yazid al-Madani," it says he related from al-A'raj and that Harun the grammarian related from him; then he follows it with the entry "Usayd ibn Abi Usayd al-Barrad," saying the father's name was Yazid, without mentioning any narration from al-A'raj or Harun from him, thereby making them two men. However, I have seen Ibn al-Jazari in Tabaqat al-Qurra' 1:381, in the entry on al-A'raj, who is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, saying: "Usayd ibn Abi Usayd related the readings from him." See this disagreement in al-Tahdhib and what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said there.]

The accusative of His saying "and your associates" is by a hidden verb governing it, namely "and call upon your associates," and it is coordinated with "affair" in His saying "your affair," in the manner of the poet's words:

"And you saw your husband in battle, girt with a sword and a spear."

[This line and its takhrij have passed in several places, the last at 13:434, note 2, and the references there; see also the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:473.]

For the spear is not girt, but since what was apparent in the speech was evidence of what was omitted, what was mentioned was sufficient in place of what was omitted. [In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "fa-iktafa" with a fa', and the correct reading is to omit it; the scribe merely made an error.] Likewise is it in His saying "and your associates."

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this.

The readers of the metropolitan cities recited it: "And your associates" in the accusative, and His saying "fa-ajmi'u" with the hamza on the alif and its opening, from "ajma'tu amri fa-ana ajma'uhu ijma'an" (I resolved my affair, so I resolve it resolutely).

* *

It is mentioned from al-Hasan al-Basri that he recited it: "fa-ajmi'u amrakum" with the opening of the alif and the hamza, "wa-shuraka'ukum" in the nominative, meaning: resolve your affair, and let your associates also resolve their affair along with you.

[See the detail of this in the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:473.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this is the recitation of those who recite "fa-ajmi'u amrakum wa-shuraka'akum" with the opening of the alif in "ajmi'u" and the accusative of "al-shuraka'" (the associates), because it is in the Mushaf without a waw, and because the consensus of the community (hujja) upon this reading, and the rejection of what contradicts it; and it is not to be objected to by one upon whom error and inadvertence are permissible.

* *

By "al-shuraka'" (the associates) is meant their gods and their idols.

* *

His saying: "Then let not your affair be obscured to you (thumma la yakun amrukum 'alaykum ghummah)" — that is: then let not your affair be unclear to you, confused, ambiguous.

* *

= from their saying: "The crescent was obscured to the people (ghumma 'ala al-nas al-hilal)," when it was unclear to them and they did not discern it; and from it is the saying of [al-'Ajjaj]: [In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "the saying of Ru'ba," and I incline to think this is a scribal error, so I have placed it in brackets; Abu Ja'far took this from Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda, where it correctly reads "al-'Ajjaj."]

"Nay, if you had witnessed the people when they were covered with an obscurity, if it had not been dispelled, they would have been obscured."

[His Diwan: 63; al-Lisan (gh-m-m), (k-m-m), and elsewhere. This is the first of his long rajaz in the Diwan, in which he mentions Mas'ud ibn 'Amr al-'Itki and what befell him and his people of Tamim, the kin of al-'Ajjaj; the explanation of that was given earlier at 13:75, note 2, in explaining a line of this rajaz. His saying "takammu" is from "takammahu," meaning he covered it and concealed it; then, as the m's accumulated in "takammamu," the last was changed to a ya', as was said in "al-tazannun" and "al-tazanni"; and when the waw was attached to it, he said "takammu."]

It is said also that this is from "al-ghamm" (distress), because the breast is constrained by it, and its owner does not make clear his matter, having no outlet from which what is in his heart can be released. [In the printed edition: "is released from it," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct.] From it is the saying of al-Khansa':

"And one in distress whom Ibn 'Amr relieved of his strangling, and his distress was lifted from his face, and he was revealed."

[Her Diwan: 22; her wording is "and one choked, whom Ibn 'Amr relieved of his strangling," from her elegy for her brother Sakhr.]

* *

Qatada used to say about this:

17761 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding "Your affair be obscured to you": he said, "Let not your affair be difficult for you."

* *

As for His saying: "Then carry it out against me" — its meaning is: then pursue what is in your souls against me and finish with it, as:

17762 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding "Then carry it out against me and do not give me respite": he said, "Carry out against me what you were going to carry out."

17763 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "Then carry it out against me and do not give me respite": he said, "Carry out against me what is in your souls."

17764 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

The people of knowledge of the Arabic language differed regarding the meaning of His saying: "Then carry it out against me" [see the explanation of "qada" (to decide/carry out) earlier, p. 33, note 4, and the references there].

Some of them said: its meaning is: pass on to me, as one says "so-and-so has qada" meaning he has died and passed away.

* *

Others said: rather its meaning is: then empty yourselves toward me; and they said: "al-qada'" is emptying, and "qada" (fulfilment) is from that. They said: and as "qada daynahu" (he settled his debt) is from that, it is only that he emptied himself of it.

* *

It has been related from some readers that he recited it: "Thumma afdu ilayya" (then reach me), meaning: proceed toward me until you reach me, from their saying "afda ilayya al-waja' wa-shabahuhu" (pain and the like reached me). [See the explanation of this reading in the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:474.]

* *

His saying: "and do not give me respite" — that is: and do not delay.

* *

= from the speaker's saying: "I granted so-and-so respite regarding what I am owed by him of debt." [See the explanation of "al-inzar" (granting respite) earlier, 13:322, note 3, and the references there.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is only a report from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, of the words of His Prophet Noah, peace be upon him, to his people: that he is confident in Allah's support for him against them, and is not fearful of their plotting and their calamities [in the printed edition: "their plotting and their covenants," which is a corrupt reading; the correct text is what I have given. The manuscript is undotted. "Al-bawa'iq" is the plural of "ba'iqah," meaning their dangers, their evil, their wrongs, and their aggression against him], and it is also an announcement from him to them that their gods neither harm nor benefit. He says to them: carry out what you are speaking to yourselves about concerning me, with a sound and firm resolve; and seek help from whoever supports you against me, with your gods whom you call upon besides Allah; and do not delay that, for I have relied upon Allah, and in Him I am confident that you will not harm me, except if my Lord wills.

And although this is a report from Allah, exalted is He, about Noah, it is also an exhortation from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to follow his example, and an instruction from Him regarding the path of rectitude in what He has entrusted to him of prophethood and conveying the message from Him.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Then if you turn away, I have not asked you for any wage. My wage is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be among those who submit﴾ (10:72).

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says, relating the words of His Prophet Noah, peace be upon him, to his people: ﴿Then if you turn away﴾, O people, meaning after my calling you and conveying the message of my Lord to you, turning your backs, so that you turn away from what I have called you to of the truth, and from acknowledging the Oneness of God, sincerely worshipping Him, and abandoning the associating of gods with Him in worship. Then you would be squandering and neglecting a duty owed to God upon you, not because of any fault on my part. For I have not asked you for any wage in exchange for what I have called you to, nor any recompense that I would take from you in return for your answering me to what I have called you to of truth and guidance, nor have I sought from you any reward or payment for it. ﴿My wage is only from Allah﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: my recompense, the reward of my work and its reward, is only from my Lord, not from you, O people, nor from anyone else. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among those who submit﴾: my Lord has commanded me to be among those who submit to Him in obedience, who yield to His command and prohibition, who humble themselves before Him. And for this reason I call you to Him, and by His command I order you to abandon the worship of idols. [[See the explanation of "al-tawalli" (turning away), "al-ajr" (wage), and "al-Islam" (submission) in the earlier lexical indexes under the roots (w-l-y), (a-j-r), (s-l-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 73:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. So look at the outcome of those who were warned﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So his people denied Noah in what he informed them of from Allah concerning the message and the revelation. ﴿Then We saved him and those with him﴾, of those who were carried with him ﴿in the ark﴾, meaning in the ship [[See the explanation of "al-fulk" (the ark) earlier: 12:502 / 15:55.]]. ﴿And We made them successors﴾, meaning: We made those whom We saved with Noah in the ship successors on the earth, in place of his people who denied him, ﴿after We drowned those who denied Our signs﴾, meaning Our proofs and evidences of Our oneness and of the message of Our messenger Noah [[See the explanation of "al-khilafah" (succession) earlier: p. 38, footnote 2, and the references there.]].

Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿So look﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿at the outcome of those who were warned﴾, meaning those whom Noah warned of Allah's punishment for their denial of him and their worship of idols. He, may His praise be exalted, says to him: Look at what their denial of their messenger brought upon them. For the outcome of those among your people who deny you, if they persist in their disbelief and their rebellion against their Lord, will be like the outcome of the people of Noah when they denied him. [[See the explanation of "al-'aqibah" (outcome) earlier: p. 93, footnote 3, and the references there.]]

He, may His praise be exalted, says: So let them beware lest there befall them the like of what befell them, if they do not repent.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 74–75:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Then after him We sent messengers to their peoples, and they brought them clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors.﴾ (74)

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: Then We sent, after Noah, messengers to their peoples, and they brought them clear proofs (bayyinat) of the arguments and evidences of their truthfulness, and that they were messengers of God, and that what they called them to was the truth. ﴿But they were not to believe in what they had denied before﴾: He says, they were not to believe in what their messengers brought them, by the same denial that the people of Noah and the nations before them, the earlier generations who preceded them, had practised. ﴿Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors﴾: He, the Exalted, says: Just as We sealed the hearts of those and set a seal upon them, so they would not accept the counsel of God's prophets, nor respond to their call to their Lord, because of the sins they committed and the wrongs they acquired [[See the explanation of "sealing" (al-tab') above, vol. 14, p. 424, footnote 2, and the references there.]]. Thus do We seal the hearts of those who transgress against their Lord, going beyond what He commanded them of His unity and opposing what their messengers called them to of obedience, as a punishment for them for their disobedience towards their Lord, from these latter ones after them.

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Then after them We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they were arrogant, and they were a guilty people.﴾ (75)

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: Then We sent, after these messengers whom We had sent after Noah to their peoples, Moses and Aaron, the two sons of Imran, to Pharaoh of Egypt and his chiefs, meaning: the nobles of his people and their leaders [[See the explanation of "al-mala'" (chiefs) above, vol. 13, p. 36, footnote 1, and the references there.]]. ﴿With Our signs﴾: He says, with Our proofs of the truth of what they called them to, namely submission to God in servitude, and acknowledgment to them both of the messengerhood. ﴿But they were arrogant﴾: He says, they were arrogant in refusing to acknowledge what Moses and Aaron called them to [[See the explanation of "al-istikbar" (arrogance) above, vol. 13, p. 114, footnote 1, and the references there.]]. ﴿And they were a guilty people﴾: meaning, sinful towards their Lord, by their disbelief in God. [[The phrase "sinful towards their Lord" is an expression that has occurred many times in Abu Ja'far's speech; I have clarified and explained it above, see vol. 12, p. 303, footnote 3, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 76–77:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Indeed, this is evident magic."﴾ ﴿Moses said, "Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' And magicians do not succeed."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿When the truth came to them from Us﴾, meaning: when there came to them the clear evidence of what Moses and Aaron called them to, namely the proofs they brought them, which are the truth that came to them from God, ﴿they said, "Indeed, this is evident magic,"﴾ meaning that it is manifestly magic with no reality to it, for whoever sees it and witnesses it [[See the explanation of "magic" above, 13:49, note 1, and the references there.]]. ﴿Moses said﴾ to them: ﴿"Do you say of the truth when it has come to you"﴾, from God, ﴿"Is this magic?"﴾

* *

The scholars of Arabic differed regarding the reason for the interrogative alif in His saying: ﴿"Is this magic?"﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: It was introduced in reporting their words, for they had said, "Is this magic?", so he said: "Do you say, 'Is this magic?'"

* *

And some grammarians of Kufa said: They said, "This is magic," and did not say it with an alif, because most of what comes is without an alif. It is said: Then why was the alif introduced? It is said: It is possible that it is from their speech while they knew it was magic, just as a man says to a prize when it comes to him, "Is this true?" while he knows it is true. It is also possible that it is an expression of their astonishment: "Is this magic? How great it is!" [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:474.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that the object is omitted, and that His saying ﴿Is this magic?﴾ is from the speech of Moses, rebuking Pharaoh and his chiefs for their saying of the truth when it came to them, "magic." The meaning of the statement then is: Moses said to them: ﴿"Do you say of the truth when it has come to you"﴾, which are the signs he brought them from God as proof of his truthfulness, "it is magic? Is this truth which you see magic?" Thus the first "magic" is omitted, being sufficiently indicated by Moses' saying ﴿"Is this magic?"﴾ that it is intended in the statement, just as Dhu al-Rummah said:

When they donned the night, or when she raised toward him, from the two sides of her ears, while she was inclining...

[[The line, its takhrij and explanation, have passed above 1:327, note 2.]]

He means: "or when he approached," then it was omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the context, as God, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, to distress your faces﴾ [Surah al-Isra: 7], meaning: We sent them to distress your faces. So that was left out, being sufficiently indicated by the context, and there are many similar instances to what we have mentioned, whose enumeration would be tiresome.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And magicians do not succeed﴾, it means: And the magicians will not prosper, nor will they endure. [[See the explanation of "success (falah)" above, p. 146, note 3, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 78:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿They said: "Have you come to us to turn us away from that upon which we found our fathers, and that you two may have greatness in the land? We are not going to believe you two."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says: Pharaoh and his chiefs said to Musa: ﴿"Have you come to us to turn us away"﴾, meaning: to divert us and twist us ﴿"from that upon which we found our fathers"﴾, meaning: from the religion, prior to your coming.

* *

It is said of this: "Fulan twisted (laffa) the neck of Fulan" when he wrenched it, as Ru'bah said:

[[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "as Dhu al-Rummah said", which is an error beyond doubt; the correct attribution is what is recorded here, as indicated by Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 280. I incline to think that this is from the copyist, not from Abu Ja'far, since he transmitted from Abu 'Ubaydah. Compare what has passed on p. 150, note 1, where I placed the correct reading between brackets.]]

*Laftan wa-tahza'an sawa' al-laft*

[[His Diwan 24; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 280; al-Lisan (h-z-‘). From a rajaz in which he describes himself, comparing himself to a lion; before it he says:

*Fa-in tarayni ahtamī bi-l-sakti*
*Fa-qad aqūmu bi-l-maqāmi l-thabti*
*Ashja‘a min dhī libadin bi-khabti*
*Yaduqqu sulbāti l-‘izāmi raftī*

"Raft" means crushing and breaking. His words "sawa' al-laft" mean "siwa al-laft," with "sawa'" (with fatha on the sin) and "siwa" (with kasra on the sin) both meaning "other than."]]

"Tahza'" means crushing, and "laft" means twisting, as:

17765 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿"to turn us away"﴾: he said, "to twist us away from that upon which our fathers were."

* *

As for His words ﴿"and that you two may have greatness in the land"﴾, it means magnificence, and it is "al-fi'liyā'" from "al-kibr." From it is the saying of Ibn al-Raqqa':

*Su'dadan ghayra fāḥishin lā yudā-*
*-nīhi tijbāratun wa-lā kibriyā'u*

[[I did not find this verse elsewhere. In the printed edition it reads "tajbārah," and likewise in the manuscript. As for its vocalisation, it has troubled me, because the lexicographers did not mention among the derivatives of "al-jabarut" anything except "al-tajbār" (with fatha then sukun) meaning pride. It seems its reader reads it as in the printed edition and manuscript, "tajbāra" (with fatha then sukun), with the ha' added. My opinion is that the vocalisation I have adopted is better, even though they did not mention it in the sources in the lexicons available to us. The verbal noun of "tif‘āl" (with kasra on the ta' and fa' and shaddah on the ‘ayn) is the analogical infinitive of "taf‘‘al," but it has become a heard form that is not analogised upon; what came from it is sufficient (al-Shafiyah 1: 166), such as "timillāq," and the entry of the ta' in such a noun is permissible in Arabic. With the vocalisation I have given, the metre of the poetry is correct, so I fear this noun is on this pattern, which the lexicon books have omitted.]]

* *

17766 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿"and that you two may have greatness in the land"﴾: he said, "the kingship."

17767 – ... he said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿"and that you two may have greatness in the land"﴾: he said, "the authority in the land."

17768 – ... he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: It reached me from Mujahid that he said: "the kingship in the land."

17769 – ... he said: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿"and that you two may have greatness in the land"﴾: he said, "the obedience."

17770 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿"and that you two may have greatness in the land"﴾: he said, "the kingship."

17771 – ... he said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

17772 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

17773 – al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, who said: "the authority in the land."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: All of these sayings are close in meaning, since kingship is authority, and obedience is kingship, except that the meaning of "al-kibriya'" is what is established in the speech of the Arabs, and then it is magnificence through kingship, authority, and other things.

* *

As for His words ﴿"We are not going to believe you two"﴾, it says: "and we are not going to believe you two," O Musa and Harun, meaning: we will not acknowledge that you two are messengers sent to us.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 79–80:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "Bring me every skilled sorcerer."  So when the sorcerers came, Moses said to them, "Throw down what you are going to throw."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is He, means: Pharaoh said to his people, "Bring me every one among the sorcerers who practises magic, [[See the explanation of "sorcery" (sihr) above, p. 155, commentary note 4, and the references there.

And the explanation of "skilled" ('alim) in the earlier lexical indexes (under the root ʿ-l-m).]] ﴿so when the sorcerers came﴾, to Pharaoh, Moses said: ﴿Throw down what you are going to throw.﴾ That is, from your ropes and your staffs.

* *

In the speech there is an omitted element that has been left out, and it is: "So they brought him the sorcerers, and when the sorcerers came," but it is sufficient that the indication of His saying, ﴿so when the sorcerers came﴾, points to that, so its mention was dropped.

Likewise, after His saying, ﴿Throw down what you are going to throw﴾, there is also an omitted element whose mention has been dropped, and it is: ﴿So they threw down their ropes and their staffs﴾, and ﴿so when they had thrown, Moses said﴾, but it is sufficient that what appears of the speech indicates it, so its mention was dropped.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 79–80:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 81:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when they had cast, Moses said, "What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will expose it. Indeed, Allah does not allow the work of corrupters to prosper."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When they had cast what they were going to cast, Moses said to them: "What you have brought is magic."

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this.

The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq recited ﴿مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ﴾ (ma ji'tum bihi as-sihr) as a declarative statement from Moses about what the sorcerers of Pharaoh had brought, that it is magic. As if the meaning of the speech, according to their interpretation, is: Moses said: "What you have brought, O sorcerers, is magic."

* *

Mujahid and some of the Medinan and Basran reciters recited it ﴿مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ آلسِّحْرُ﴾ (ma ji'tum bihi a-sihr) in the form of an interrogative from Moses to the sorcerers about what they had brought: is it magic or something else? [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 475, where there is a useful detailed discussion.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations in my view is the recitation of the one who recited it as a declarative and not as an interrogative, because Moses, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was not doubtful about what the sorcerers had brought, that it was magic with no reality, so that he would need to ask the sorcerers about it, what it is.

Another reason: he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had knowledge of the sorcerers; Pharaoh had only brought them to contest him with the truth that Allah had given him. It would not be hidden from him that they did not truthfully report what they had brought of falsehood, so that he would ask them or deem it permissible to ask them about it. Rather, he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, informed them that he knew the falsehood of what they had brought with the truth that had come to him. [[In the manuscript: "ما جاؤوا به من ذلك الحق الذي أتاه", and I incline to think the scribe of the manuscript dropped some words, but what is in the printed edition conveys its meaning, by adding the particle "ب" in "بالحق", though the sentence seems weak to me.]]

And he nullifies their plot with its force. [[In the printed edition: "بجده" with a jim, and the correct reading is with a ha'. And "al-hadd" means severity, might and power.]]

And this is more fitting to the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than the other.

* *

If someone says: What is the reason for the entry of the definite article in "as-sihr" if the matter is as you described, while you know that the Arabic usage in the like of this is to say: "What Amr brought me is a dirham = and the one your brother gave me is a dinar", and they hardly say:

"The one your brother gave me, the dirham = and what Amr brought me, the dinar?"

It is said to him: Yes. The usage of the Arabs is to introduce the "alif and lam" in the predicate of "ma" and "alladhi" when the predicate concerns a known referent that both the addressee and the speaker recognize. Indeed, it is not permitted in that case except with the "alif and lam", because the predicate then is a statement about a specific thing known to both parties. Without the "alif and lam" it comes when the predicate concerns something unknown, unspecified and not intended as a particular thing; then the "alif and lam" does not enter the predicate. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript, "واللام" is omitted.]] [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 475.]] The statement of Moses was a statement about something known to him and to the sorcerers, because they had attributed what Moses had brought them of the signs, which Allah had made a sign for his truthfulness and prophethood, to being magic. So Moses said to them: "The magic that you have described what I brought you of signs with, O sorcerers, is what you yourselves have brought, not what I have brought." Then he informed them that Allah would nullify it. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah will expose it﴾, meaning: will eliminate it. And He, may His remembrance be exalted, eliminated it by empowering over it the staff of Moses, which he had turned into a serpent that swallowed it, until nothing of it remained. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not allow the work of corrupters to prosper﴾, meaning: He does not make prosper the work of one who strives in the earth of Allah with what He dislikes and acts in it by His disobedience. [[See the explanation of "al-ifsad" in the previous indices of language (fasada).]]

* *

It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b it is: ﴿مَا أَتَيْتُمْ بِهِ سِحْرٌ﴾.

* *

And in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ سِحْرٌ﴾, [[See these two recitations in the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 475.]] and this supports the recitation of the one who recited in the manner of what we have chosen in it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verses 82–83:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah will establish the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it﴾ (82)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, is informing about Musa that he said to the magicians: ﴿And Allah will establish the truth﴾, meaning: Allah will confirm the truth that I have brought you from Him, so He will make it prevail over your falsehood and make it sound. "By His words" means: by His command [[See the explanation of "yuhiqq al-haqq bi-kalimatihi" earlier, 13:407, footnotes 2, 3, and the references there.]] ﴿even if the criminals dislike it﴾, meaning those who earned sin against their Lord [[See the explanation of the meaning of "atham bi-rabbihi" earlier, p. 155, footnote 3, and the references there.]] by their disobedience to Him.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿But none believed in Musa except a few [dhurriyyah] of his people, out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, that he would persecute them. Indeed, Pharaoh was haughty in the land, and indeed he was among the transgressors﴾ (83)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: So none believed in Musa, despite the proofs and evidences that came to them, ﴿except a few [dhurriyyah] of his people﴾, fearing Pharaoh and their chiefs.

Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of "dhurriyyah" (offspring, descendants) in this place.

Some of them said: "Dhurriyyah" in this place means: a few.

Those who said this:

17774 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿So none believed in Musa except a few [dhurriyyah] of his people﴾, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: "Dhurriyyah" means: a few.

17775 – It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, exalted is He: ﴿So none believed in Musa except a few [dhurriyyah] of his people﴾: "Dhurriyyah" means: a few, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿As He produced you from the descendants [dhurriyyah] of another people﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 133].

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: none believed in Musa except the descendants [dhurriyyah] of those to whom Musa was sent from the Children of Israel, because of the long passage of time, since the fathers had died and the sons remained. So they were called "dhurriyyah," because they were the descendants of those who had perished from among those to whom Musa, peace be upon him, was sent. 17776 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿So none believed in Musa except a few [dhurriyyah] of his people﴾, he said: The children of those to whom he was sent, because of the long passage of time, and their fathers had died.

17778 – And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17779 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿So none believed in Musa except a few [dhurriyyah] of his people﴾, he said: The children of those to whom Musa was sent, because of the long passage of time, and their fathers had died.

* *
