17904 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shabl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih who said: "When they saw the punishment descending, they separated every female from her offspring among people and livestock, then they all stood up and called upon God, and sincerely directed their faith, and they saw the punishment lifted from them. Yunus said when the punishment was lifted from them: I will return to them, though I have lied to them! Yunus had promised them the punishment at the dawn of the third day, so at that point he went out angry and his opinion of [God] became evil. [[See the explanation of "his opinion became evil" above, 3:585, note 1 / 13:95, note 4.]]

17905 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Malik, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: When Yunus was sent to his people calling them to Islam and to abandon what they were upon. He said: He called them, and they refused. It was said to him: Inform them that the punishment will strike them at dawn. They said: We have never tested him with a lie, so wait: if he stays among you, then it is nothing; and if he does not stay, know that the punishment will strike you at dawn. When it was the middle of the night, he took a bag of curd (al-'ulathah) and took some provision from it, then went out. When they awoke in the morning, the punishment covered them as a person is covered by a cloth in the grave; they separated the human from her child and the beast from its young; then they cried out to God and said: "We believe in what Yunus brought, and we confirm it!" God removed the punishment from them. Yunus went out to look at the punishment, but saw nothing. He said: They have tested me with a lie! So he went away angry at his Lord until he came to the sea.

17906 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun who said: Ibn Mas'ud narrated to us in the treasury (bayt al-mal), he said: Yunus, peace be upon him, had promised his people the punishment, and informed them that it would come to them within three days. They separated every mother from her child, then went out and cried to God and sought His forgiveness. God withheld the punishment from them, and Yunus went out in the morning to look at the punishment, but saw nothing. Whoever had lied and had no proof was killed, so he set off angry.

17907 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Salih al-Murri narrated to us, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Abu al-Jald Jaylan who said: When the punishment covered the people of Yunus, they went to a shaykh from the remnant of their scholars and said to him: The punishment has descended upon us, so what do you advise? He said: Say: "O Living when there is no living, O Living who gives life to the dead, O Living, there is no god but You!" So the punishment was lifted from them, and they were allowed to enjoy [their lives] for a time. [[Report 17907: "Abu al-Jald" is "Jaylan ibn Abi Farwa al-Asadi," passed as nos. 434, 723, 1913.]]

17908 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar who said: It reached me in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "fa-lawla," meaning ﴿fa-hallа﴾ (why then not).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world﴾, it means: when they confirmed their messenger and acknowledged what he brought them, after the punishment had overshadowed them, the command of God had overtaken them, and affliction had descended upon them, We removed from them the punishment of humiliation and abasement in their life in this world [[See the explanation of "al-khizy" (disgrace) above, 14:330, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and We let them enjoy [their lives] for a time﴾, means: We postponed their terms and did not hasten punishment upon them, and We left them in the world to enjoy their terms until the time of their death and the time of the end of their lives, which I had decreed should end. [[See the explanation of "al-mata'" (enjoyment) above in the language indices (m-t-').]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 99:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely. Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ (10:99)

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted says to His Prophet: ﴿And if your Lord had willed﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely﴾ in you, and would have affirmed that you are the Messenger of God to them, and that what you have brought them and what you call them to, namely the Oneness of God and sincere devotion to Him, is the truth. But He does not will that, because it had already preceded in God's decree, before He sent you as a messenger, that they would not believe in you or follow you so as to affirm what God has sent you with of guidance and light, except for those for whom happiness had preceded in the first Book, before the heavens and the earth and what is in them were created. And these who marvel at the truthfulness of Our revelation to you of this Qur'an, so that you may warn with it those whom you have been commanded to warn, are those for whom it has already preceded with Me that they will not believe in you in the earlier Book.

* *

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

17909 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His statement: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely﴾ and ﴿No soul could believe except by the permission of God﴾ (10:100), and similar to this in the Qur'an. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to be eager that all people would believe and follow him in guidance, so God informed him that none would believe except those for whom happiness had already been decreed from God in the first Remembrance [[In the printed edition: "does not believe from his people", which adds what is not in the manuscript, so I omitted it.]], and none would go astray except those for whom wretchedness had already been decreed from God in the first Remembrance.

* *

If someone says: What is the purpose of His statement ﴿those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely﴾? For "kull" (all) indicates "jami'" (entirety), and "jami'" indicates "kull", so what is the point of repeating it when each of them suffices without the other?

It is said: The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) have differed regarding this.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He used "jami'an" (entirely) in this place as an emphasis (tawkid), as in: ﴿Do not take two gods (ilahayn ithnayn)﴾ (16:51), where "ilahayn" already indicates "ithnayn".

Another said: He used "jami'an" after "kulluhum" because "jami'an" only occurs as an emphasis, whereas "kulluhum" occurs both as an emphasis and as a noun; therefore "jami'an" came after "kulluhum". He said: If it were said that he combined them to make known that their meaning is one, it would be permissible here. He said: Likewise with ﴿ilahayn ithnayn﴾, the whole number is explained by it, as one says "I saw a people, four", and when he said "ithnayn" having already been satisfied with the number, because they say "I have a dirham and two dirhams", and it suffices from their saying "I have one dirham, and two dirhams: two", but when they say "dirhams" they say "three", because the plural is ambiguous, whereas "one" and "two" are not ambiguous. Then the singular and the dual were built upon the form of [the] plural, [[In the printed edition: "did not make the singular and dual conform to the contrariness of the plural", which has no meaning. In the manuscript: "then built the singular and dual upon the contrariness of the plural", unpointed; I inferred this reading as I have given it, adding "ma" between "bina'" and "fi al-jami'". Nevertheless, something remains unclear to me in the explanation of this statement; I fear some part has dropped out, for it is not clear to me.]] because it is necessary that with each one there be one, since "dirham" indicates the genus of which it is part, and "one" indicates all genera. Likewise "two" indicates all genera, and "two dirhams" indicates themselves; therefore the numbers were used, because that is the original form.

* *

As for His statement: ﴿Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): He will not believe you, O Muhammad, nor follow you and acknowledge what you have brought, except those whom your Lord wills to believe you, not by your compulsion of them, nor by your eagerness for that. ﴿Would you then compel the people until they become believers﴾ to you, affirming what you have brought them from your Lord? He says to him, the Exalted: So proclaim what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists against whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled, that they will not believe.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 100:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not for any soul to believe except by the permission of Allah, and He places defilement upon those who do not reason.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet: "It was not for any soul that I created to have a path to believing in you, O Muhammad, except that I permit it to do so. So do not exhaust yourself in seeking its guidance; convey to it the warning of Allah, make known to it what your Lord has commanded you to make known, and then leave it alone, for its guidance is in the hand of its Creator."

* *

Al-Thawri used to say, concerning His words ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾: it means:

17910- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, concerning His words ﴿And it is not for any soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾, he said: "By the decree of Allah."

* *

As for His words ﴿and He places defilement upon those who do not reason﴾, He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed Allah guides whomever He wills of His creatures to believe in you, O Muhammad, and permits him to affirm your truth, so he affirms you, follows you, and acknowledges what you have brought from your Lord. ﴿And He places defilement﴾, which is the punishment and the wrath of Allah, ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾, meaning those who do not understand from Allah His proofs, admonitions, and signs by which He, majestic is His praise, indicated the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the truth of what he called them to, namely the oneness of Allah and the renunciation of rivals and idols.

17911- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿and He places defilement﴾, he said: "The wrath."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 101:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists of your people who ask you for signs as proof of the truth of what you call them to, namely the Oneness of God and the renunciation of rivals and idols: Look, O people, at what there is in the heavens of signs that indicate the truth of what I call you to regarding the Oneness of God, such as its sun and its moon, the alternation of its night and its day, and the descent of rain bringing the sustenance of the servants from its clouds; and in the earth, such as its mountains, its splitting open with plants, the provisions of its inhabitants, and all the various kinds of its wonders. Indeed, in that is, for you, if you reason and reflect, an admonition and a lesson, and a proof that this is the work of One who may not have any partner in His dominion, nor any helper in His governance and preservation, who would suffice you apart from the other signs.

God, exalted is His praise, says: ﴿But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe.﴾ He, exalted is His praise, says: The proofs, lessons, and warning messengers do not avail in deterring from the worship of God and His punishment [[See the explanation of "aghnā" above, p. 89, note 2, and the references there.]] a people for whom wretchedness from God has already preceded, and for whom it has been decreed in the Mother of the Book that they are among the people of the Fire, so they do not believe in any of that nor affirm it. ﴿Even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [[See the explanation of "nadhīr" above, 10: 85.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 102:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Then do they await only the like of the days of those who passed away before them? Say, "Then wait; indeed, I am with you among the waiting."﴾ (10:102)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), warning the polytheists of his people of the swift arrival of His vengeance upon them, like that which befell their counterparts before them among the other nations that passed away before them, who followed the same path in denying the messengers of Allah and rejecting the Oneness of their Lord: "Then do these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, who deny what you have brought them from Allah, await anything but a day on which they witness the punishment of Allah, like the days of their predecessors who were upon the same polytheism and denial as they are upon, those who passed away before them, from the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud?" Say to them, O Muhammad, if they are indeed awaiting that: "Then wait for the punishment of Allah upon you and the descent of His wrath upon you; indeed, I am among those awaiting your destruction and ruin through the punishment from Allah that will descend upon you."

* *

And those of the people of interpretation (ta'wil) said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

17912 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Then do they await only the like of the days of those who passed away before them﴾, he said: "The encounters (waqa'i') of Allah with those who passed away before them: the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud."

17913 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then do they await only the like of the days of those who passed away before them. Say, "Then wait; indeed, I am with you among the waiting."﴾ He said: "He warned them of His punishment, His vengeance and His retribution. Then He informed them that when something of that occurred, Allah would save His messengers and those who believed with them. So Allah said: ﴿Then We save Our messengers and those who believe. Thus it is incumbent upon Us to save the believers.﴾"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 103:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Then We shall deliver Our messengers and those who believe. Thus it is incumbent upon Us: We shall deliver the believers.﴾ (10:103)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people: Wait for the like of the days of those who passed away before you, from the earlier nations who were destroyed by the punishment of God. For when that comes, none will be destroyed by it except them, and those who are upon the same condition as they are in denying you. Then We shall deliver there Our messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and those who believed in him, affirmed him and followed him in his religion, just as We did before that with Our messengers whose nations We destroyed. We delivered them and those who believed in them along with them from Our punishment when it became due upon their nations. ﴿Thus it is incumbent upon Us: We shall deliver the believers﴾ means: just as We did with the past messengers, delivering them and the believers with them and destroying their nations, so We shall do with you, O Muhammad, and with the believers: We shall deliver you and the believers who are with you, as a truth incumbent upon Us, without doubt.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say, O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those whom you worship besides God, but I worship God, who takes your souls at death. And I have been commanded to be among the believers.﴾ (10:104)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists of your people who wondered that I had revealed to you: "If you are in doubt, O people, about my religion to which I call you, and you have not known that it is the truth from God, then I do not worship those whom you worship besides God, from among the gods and idols, which do not hear, do not see, and do not avail me anything, so that you would doubt its soundness."

This is an allusion (ta'rid) and a subtle figurative speech (lahn) ["lahn" (figurative speech): alluding to a matter and indicating it without stating it plainly, by turning the speech away from its direct course, which makes it more effective and more stirring to the understanding of the listener.]

The meaning of the speech is: If you are in doubt about my religion, you should not doubt it; rather, you should doubt what you are upon, namely the worship of idols that understand nothing and neither harm nor benefit. As for my religion, you should not doubt it, because I worship God, who seizes creation and causes them to die when He wills, and benefits them and harms them when He wills. [In the printed and manuscript editions: "and He benefits them and harms whom He wills." This seems to be a scribal error, for the context requires what has been adopted.] This is because the worship of one who is like this is not denied by one of sound nature, whereas the worship of idols is denied by every person of intellect and sound reason.

* *

As for His words, ﴿but I worship God, who takes your souls﴾, He says: but I worship God, who seizes your souls and causes you to die at your appointed times [See the explanation of "tawaffi" (taking in full) above, p. 98, note 1, and the references there.] = ﴿and I have been commanded to be among the believers﴾, He says: and He is the One who commanded me to be among those who affirm what has come to me from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verses 105–106:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [it was commanded to me]: Set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be of those who associate others with Allah﴾ (10:105).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And I was commanded to be among the believers," and "an aqim" (that I should set) and the second "an" (that) is conjoined to the first "an."

By His saying ﴿Set your face toward the religion﴾, He means: set yourself upon the religion of Islam [see the explanation of "the face" (wajh) earlier, 2:510–512, 526–546 / 10:23 and what follows]. ﴿Inclining (hanifan)﴾: upright upon it, not deviating from it toward Judaism or Christianity, nor the worship of idols [see the explanation of "hanif" (upright, inclining) earlier, 12:283, note 1, and the references there]. ﴿And never be of those who associate others with Allah﴾ means: and never be of those who associate, in the worship of their Lord, gods and rivals, so that you would be among the ruined.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not call upon other than Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you. For if you did, then you would [certainly] be of the wrongdoers﴾ (10:106).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And do not call upon, O Muhammad, other than your worshipped Lord and Creator, anything that does not benefit you in this world or in the Hereafter, and does not harm you in religion or in worldly life. By this He means the deities and the idols. He says: do not worship them hoping for their benefit or fearing their harm, for they neither benefit nor harm. ﴿For if you did﴾ that, and called upon them besides Allah, ﴿then you would [certainly] be of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: of those who associate others with Allah, wronging their own souls. [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "the one who wrongs himself," but the context does not suit this, and I think it is a copyist's error, so I have replaced it with what is established here.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verses 105–106:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [it was commanded to me]: Set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be of those who associate others with Allah﴾ (10:105).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And I was commanded to be among the believers," and "an aqim" (that I should set) and the second "an" (that) is conjoined to the first "an."

By His saying ﴿Set your face toward the religion﴾, He means: set yourself upon the religion of Islam [see the explanation of "the face" (wajh) earlier, 2:510–512, 526–546 / 10:23 and what follows]. ﴿Inclining (hanifan)﴾: upright upon it, not deviating from it toward Judaism or Christianity, nor the worship of idols [see the explanation of "hanif" (upright, inclining) earlier, 12:283, note 1, and the references there]. ﴿And never be of those who associate others with Allah﴾ means: and never be of those who associate, in the worship of their Lord, gods and rivals, so that you would be among the ruined.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not call upon other than Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you. For if you did, then you would [certainly] be of the wrongdoers﴾ (10:106).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And do not call upon, O Muhammad, other than your worshipped Lord and Creator, anything that does not benefit you in this world or in the Hereafter, and does not harm you in religion or in worldly life. By this He means the deities and the idols. He says: do not worship them hoping for their benefit or fearing their harm, for they neither benefit nor harm. ﴿For if you did﴾ that, and called upon them besides Allah, ﴿then you would [certainly] be of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: of those who associate others with Allah, wronging their own souls. [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "the one who wrongs himself," but the context does not suit this, and I think it is a copyist's error, so I have replaced it with what is established here.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 107:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him; and if He intends you good, there is none to repel His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [10:107].

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet: "And if Allah afflicts you, O Muhammad, with hardship or trial," [[See the explanation of "al-mass" (touching) above, p. 49, footnote 1, and the references there.

As for the explanation of "al-darr" (harm), see the lexical indexes above under (ḍ-r-r).]] "then there is none to remove it except your Lord, who has afflicted you with it, rather than what these polytheists worship of gods and rivals" [[See the explanation of "al-kashf" (removal) above, vol. 11, p. 354 / vol. 13, p. 73 / vol. 15, pp. 36, 205.]] — "And if He intends you good," meaning: and if your Lord intends you with ease, or blessing, well-being and joy [[See the explanation of "al-khayr" (good) above in the lexical indexes under (kh-y-r).]] — "then there is none to repel His bounty," meaning: then no one can come between you and that, nor turn you away from it or deprive you of it; for it is He in whose hand are ease and hardship, not the gods and idols, nor anything else besides Him — "He causes it to reach whom He wills," meaning: your Lord, O Muhammad, causes ease, trial, happiness and hardship to reach whomever He wills and intends [[See the explanation of "al-iṣābah" (causing to reach) above in the lexical indexes under (ṣ-w-b).]] "of His servants, and He is the Forgiving," for the sins of whoever repents and turns back to Him among His servants from their disbelief and polytheism to faith in Him and obedience to Him — "the Merciful" toward those among them who believe in Him and obey Him, that He would punish them after repentance and turning back. [[See the explanation of "al-Ghafur" (the Forgiving) and "al-Rahim" (the Merciful) above in the lexical indexes under (gh-f-r) and (r-ḥ-m).]]

Commentary on the words of His Exalted Majesty: ﴿Say, "O mankind, the truth has certainly come to you from your Lord. So whoever is guided, it is only for [the benefit of] his own soul that he is guided; and whoever goes astray, it is only against it [i.e., his own soul] that he goes astray. And I am not over you a manager."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Says God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the people: ﴿O mankind, the truth has certainly come to you from your Lord﴾, meaning: the Book of God, in which is the clarification of everything that people need concerning the matter of their religion. ﴿So whoever is guided﴾ means: whoever goes straight, follows the path of truth, and affirms what has come from God of clear guidance. ﴿Then it is only for his own soul that he is guided﴾ means: he only keeps to the right guidance and takes the straight path for his own soul; it is for himself that he seeks good by that action, not for anyone else [[See the explanation of "guidance" (ihtida') in the preceding indexes of vocabulary, root (h-d-y).]]. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾ means: whoever deviates from the truth that came to him from God, opposes His religion, and what He sent Muhammad with, and the Book He revealed to him. ﴿Then it is only against it that he goes astray﴾ means: his straying only harms himself and not others, because no one else will be held accountable for it, and no one but himself will be led by his straying into destruction. ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [[See the explanation of "straying" (dalal) in the preceding indexes of vocabulary, root (z-l-l).]]. ﴿And I am not over you a manager﴾ means: I am not over you one who has authority to make you upright; your affair is with God, and it is He who sets right whomever He wills among you. I am only a messenger who conveys, delivering to you what I was sent with.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 10, verse 109:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges, and He is the best of judges.﴾ (10:109)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: Follow, O Muhammad, the revelation of Allah that He reveals to you, and His revelation that He sends down to you; so act upon it, and be patient over what afflicts you for Allah's sake from the polytheists of your people, of harm and hardships, and over what befalls you from them, until Allah decides His command concerning them and concerning you by a decisive act. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾: that is, He is the best of those who decide and the most just of those who separate (truth from falsehood). [See the explanation of "al-hukm" (judgment) above, 12:561, footnote 1, and the references there.] So He, may His praise be exalted, judged between him and them on the Day of Badr, and slew them by the sword, and commanded His Prophet ﷺ regarding those who remained of them that he should treat them in the manner of those of them who were destroyed, or that they should repent and turn back in obedience to Him, as:

17914 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And you are not over them a guardian. And be patient until Allah judges, and He is the best of judges﴾: "This is abrogated" — ﴿until Allah judges﴾: Allah's judgment was to fight them, and He commanded him to be harsh with them.

[At this point ends a part of the old division; in our manuscript, after this there is the following text:

"The end of the commentary on Surah Yunus, peace be upon him, and praise be to Allah alone, and may Allah bless Muhammad and his family.

Followed by the commentary of the surah in which Hud is mentioned."

Followed by:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, my Lord, make it easy."] The end of the commentary of Surah Yunus.
